Somo lilikuwa fupi. “Dkt. Waldron, unaweza kumpigia Mrs. Jones kurudi kuhusu matokeo yake ya maabara?”

Nilikasirika. Sikumbuki kuagiza maabara yoyote kwa Mrs. Jones. Kadri nilivyokumbuka, alikuwa akimtazama mtaalam na alianza tu kufanyiwa upasuaji kwa saratani ya kolon. Labda wao walikuwa wameagiza maabara. Lakini ikiwa ni hivyo, kwa hakika wangepaswa kufuatilia matokeo hayo.

Nimempigia yeye halafu daktari wa figo. Katika nusu saa iliyofuata, hali yake ilianza kuwa wazi. Kwa sababu ya upasuaji wa kolon, alikuwa akipoteza kiasi kikubwa cha maji mwilini, vya kutosha kwamba hakuweza kuyafuatilia. Hii, kwa upande mwingine, ilikuwa ikifanya kazi ya figo yake kuwa mbaya zaidi, pamoja na kushuka kwa kiwango chake cha potasiamu.

Ili kutatuliwa, angehitaji maji ya kuingizwa kwa vena (IV) — mara moja au mbili kwa wiki — ili kufidia maji anayopoteza. Bila hayo, figo zake zingefunga kabisa.

Kwa namna fulani, Mrs. Jones alikuwa akikabiliwa na upotevu wa nguvu za figo — hali ambapo zinatoa zaidi ya zinavyoinuliwa na kuumia kwa matokeo.

Nilipokuwa nikifikiria hili, akili yangu ilielekea Bahari ya Wafu. Bahari ya Wafu ni “Wafu” kwa sababu ina kiwango cha juu sana cha madini na chumvi kiasi kwamba wachache tu, isipokuwa baadhi ya viumbe vidogo, wanaweza kuishi.

Sababu ya hili ni kwamba Bahari ya Wafu haina njia ya kutiririka. Mto Yordani unaingia ndani yake, ukileta maji safi, kisha ukakaa kwenye bakuli. Sehemu ya maji huvukiza, na kile kinachobaki ni chumvi na madini yaliyomo ndani ya maji.

Kutokana na maelfu ya miaka tangu kuanguka kwa Sodoma na Gomora, mwili huu wa maji wa ndani umekuwa mojawapo ya maeneo yenye chumvi nyingi duniani. Ni mwili wa maji usiofaa kwa umwagiliaji wala mahali ambapo mimea na wanyama wanaweza kustawi.

Hakuna mojawapo ya hali hizi za afya, lakini hivi ndivyo watu wengi huishi maisha yao, mara nyingi wakielekea upande mmoja au mwingine. Wao au wanaleta ratiba yao hadi kiwango cha juu kabisa, bila nafasi ya tafakari ya kimya, au wanakataa jitihada zozote za kuwafanya waweke wakati na vipaji vyao na kuepuka aina hizi za shughuli.

Nataka kutumia muda kidogo kufikiri kuhusu uchovu wa kazi. Nini husababisha, na tunavyoweza kuepuka?

Kila Mtu Ana Mipaka

1 Samweli 30 inasimulia hadithi ya Daudi akiendelea kurudi Ziklag. Alipowasili, aligundua, kwa kuhuzunika kwake, kwamba Waamaleki walivamia eneo la Wafilisti, waliteketeza mji, na kuwachukua mateka watu wote waliokuwepo.

Daudi na wanamume wake walikuwa wameondoka kwa siku tatu na tayari walikuwa na uchovu kutokana na safari yao ya kwenda na kurudi kutoka Apheki, ambapo Mfalme Agagi alikuwa amekusanya jeshi lake. Licha ya hili na uchungu wao kwa kupoteza wapendwa wao na mali, Daudi aliomba kushauriana na Mungu na akamua kuwafuata Waamaleki hadi jangwani.

Walikuwa wameenda hadi Mto Besori tu wakati theluthi moja ya wanamume wake walikata tamaa. Maandiko yanatuambia walikuwa “wapuuzaji” kupita kiasi kutavuka mto. Walikuwa wamechoka kimwili na kiakili. Hata kama wangeweza kusimamia siku nyingine, wangekuwa havina maana katika vita.

Hivyo Daudi aliwaacha nyuma na kuendelea kuwafuata Waamaleki, hatimaye kuwashinda kwa wanamume mia nne ambao waliweza kustahimili. Hapa, tunakuja sehemu ya kuvutia. Wanamume waliopata ushindi waliwaangalia wale waliokuwa wamelala moyo. Wakasema wanaume wale waoga waweze kurudishiwa wake familia, lakini mzigo wa kuondoa mali ungehifadhiwa kwa wale waliopata ushindi.

Daudi akajibu, “Hamfanyi hivyo, ndugu zangu, kwa yale ambayo Bwana ametupatia, amewatunza na akatuokoa; nami ameweka wapinzani walioingia kwetu mikononi mwetu. Kwa maana nani atakaye sikiliza kwenu katika jambo hili? Bali kama sehemu yake ya yule anayeuwa kwenda mapigoni, ndivyo pia sehemu yake ya yule anayetwaa vitu: wote watagawana pamoja.” (1 Samweli 30:23,24)

Daudi hakutaka kuadhibu wale ambao walijaribu lakini hawakuwa na nguvu ya kufika hadi mapigano ya mwisho.

Labda hili linaonyesha neema tunayopaswa kuwapa wengine ambao hawana nguvu au nishati ya kuendelea kwa msimu fulani. Labda pia linatufahamisha kwamba tunapaswa kuelekeza neema hiyo kwa sisi wenyewe.

Uchovu wa Kazi Ni Nini?

Kuna ufafanuzi tofauti kwa uchovu wa kazi, lakini yote yanarejea kwenye hali ya uchovu wa kimwili, kisaikolojia, au kihisia unaohusishwa na msongo wa mawazo wa muda mrefu. Tendaji kutuona msongo huu kama unaohusiana na kazi pekee. Kuna miradi nyingi kwa wakati mmoja, msaada mdogo, au mwajiri mwenye matarajio makubwa.

Msongo ni msongo, na yote hujikusanya. Hata kama kazi siyo chanzo cha msongo, ikiwa una mtoto mchanga nyumbani, mwanachama wa familia mwenye dalili za kupoteza kumbukumbu, au wajibu mwingi wa kanisani, bado unaweza kufika mahali ambapo huna kitu cha kutoa.

Kama vile uko katika gari unaosafiri kwa maili 90 kwa saa, unabana mguu wa gesi kidogo zaidi, na hakuna kinachotokea. Kwa kujibu, unabana gesi kwa nguvu zaidi, na sauti ya kusurika inatoka kwenye injini. Ghafla, dashibodi inajaa taa za ajabu, na gari inaanza kupungua mwendo.

Swali ni, tunaweza kuiepuka vipi uchovu wa kazi na tunapaswa kufanya nini tukigundua tunazidi kuuelekea?

Kuelewa Uchovu wa Kazi

Uchovu wa kazi husababisha upungufu wa kimwili na kihisia. Tatizo la uchovu wa kazi ni kwamba hata kama chombo fulani cha msongo ndicho kimesababisha — sema, hali kazini au shida ya afya ya familia — itatafika kwa mahusiano mengine mengi.

Watu wanaokumbwa na uchovu wa kazi mara nyingi huonyesha dalili zinazofanana na unyogovu na wasiwasi. Wanaweza kujiondoa, kukosa motisha ya kushiriki katika shughuli za kanisa na familia, au kuchukizwa haraka zaidi kuliko watu wasiokumbwa na uchovu huo.

Kuna hata mapendekezo kwamba uchovu wa kazi unaweza kusababisha udhaifu wa mfumo wetu wa kinga. Hii inaweza kupelekea mafua na maambukizi ya virusi mara kwa mara.

Tambua Dalili za Mapema

Tunahitaji kujijua. Kuna dalili ambazo watu wengine wanaweza kuziwona katika maisha yetu na jinsi tunavyohusiana na wengine ambazo hatutambulii kuwa tatizo.

Watu walio karibu na kuingia kwenye uchovu wa kazi wanahisi kukata tamaa. Wanaweza kuficha hili kwa wenzake wa kazi, lakini mara nyingi, familia yao hugundua kwamba kuna kitu kibaya. Ulikuwa na tabasamu mara nyingi, na sasa umechanganyikiwa, siyo tu kuhusu sasa bali pia kuhusu siku za usoni.

Unaweza kukosa motisha na kuwa na kiwango cha chini cha nishati. Kwa namna fulani, unafanya tu mambo kwa mtiririko wa kawaida na ukifanya vya kutosha tu kuvuka — kazini na nyumbani. Hii ina uwezekano kuwa inahusiana na hisia zako za kukata tamaa.

Unaweza kubaini kuwa wewe ni mtu mwenye hasira zaidi kuliko kawaida. Mambo madogo yanakukera au kunyanyasa, na unajikuta ukitilia mfadhaiko majibu ya hasira.

Ni muhimu kutambua kwamba unaelekea njia hii kwa sababu kadhaa. Kwanza, si wewe peke yako anayeteseka unapotofautishwa na uchovu. Familia yako lazima iwashughulikie wewe na “ukakasi” wako. Pia, kadri unavyokwenda bila kutatua mambo, ndivyo zinavyokuwa vigumu zaidi kupata usawa tena.

Kama daktari, ninaona watu kila mara ambao “hawakuwa na muda” wa kushughulikia jambo mpaka wakiwa hawawezi kuzuia tena. Wakati huu, itahitaji taratibu kuu ya tiba kurekebisha. Ingenifika kwa urahisi zaidi iwapo wangekuja wakiwa na dalili ya kwanza.

Fanya Orodha ya Kipaumbele

Kila kitu katika maisha yetu kina kiwango cha kipaumbele. Watu wasioweka vipaumbele wanajikuta wamehuzunika wanapojaribu kufanya kila kitu kwa wakati mmoja. Hii ni kichocheo cha maafa. Kwangu, inaonekana kuwa busara kugawa majukumu yetu katika makapu manne:

  1. Mambo yanayohitajika kufanywa haraka
  2. Mambo yanayohitajika kufanywa lakini yanaweza kusubiri kidogo
  3. Mambo tunayopenda kufanya, lakini hayahitajiki
  4. Mambo ambayo tunapaswa kuyaacha.

Hapa mungkin ni mahali pazuri kutaja kwamba kwa sababu kitu kinahitaji kufanywa haimaanishi lazima ufanye wewe mwenyewe. Wakati mwingine, mtu nyumbani kwako au kazini anaweza kusaidia na moja ya kazi kwenye orodha yako.

Mara tu tukifanya orodha ya vipaumbele, tunahitaji kuchukua hatua. Ikiwa utaweka tu kipaumbele kwa kila kitu katika maisha yako lakini ukaendelea kujaribu kufanya kila kitu, haitasaidia kabisa.

Madhumuni ya zoezi hili ni kubaini mambo unayoweza kuondoa kwenye ratiba yako, ili upate nafasi zaidi ya kupumua.

Weka Kwanza Mambo Muhimu

Kimoja kati ya mambo yanayotokea tunapofadhaika ni kwamba tunaacha kujijali. Tunachukua chakula kisicho na afya tunapotembea, tunaacha kutumia muda katika sala na kuabudu, na kuacha mazoezi.

Kufanya mambo haya kunachukua muda, na hiyo ndio hasa tunafikiria hatuna wakati tunapoishi kwa kikomo cha nishati yetu. Kujitunza ni muhimu sana lakini mara nyingi kunapewa kipaumbele cha sifuri na nadra kuingizwa kwenye shughuli za siku.

Tunapoanza kujaza upya lishe yetu ya kiroho, lazima pia tuhakikishe tunajali afya yetu ya mwili.

Chukua Muda Peke Yako

Baada ya kumlisha umati, Marko 6:46 inasema kuhusu Yesu, “Na baada ya kuwa wamemwacha, yeye peke yake alikwenda juu ya mlima kulilia.” Hata Yesu alikuwa na wakati ambapo alihitaji kuwa peke yake bila usumbufu.

Ni rahisi kuzingatia kipengele cha sala katika aya hii, na hilo ni muhimu, lakini tuzingatie kipengele cha kuwa peke ya mtu katika uzoefu huu. Yesu hata alimuacha waabudu wake wa karibu nyuma wakati wa kipindi hiki cha kutafuta uso wa Mungu.

Kuna nyakati ambazo tunahitaji kutoroka kutoka kwa shinikizo la mwingiliano wa binadamu na kupata mahali pa amani ambapo tunaweza kuwa peke yetu.

Weka Teknolojia Pembeni

Sehemu ya kufanya muda wa mapumziko uwe wa kweli ni kuondoa vyanzo vya usumbufu. Simu na vidonge vya elektroniki ni aina za vitu vinavyoweza kuzuia akili yetu kufikia amani (shalom) tunayotaka na tunayohitaji.

Uchovu wa kidijitali ni neno jipya linalotumika kuelezea watu wanaohisi kupoteza hamu na kuchoka kutokana na kutazama skrini kwa masaa kila siku. Wafanyakazi wengi hutumia saa saba au nane kwa siku kutazama skrini za kompyuta na kisha kuendelea tena baada ya kazi.

Kitu cha kuchekesha ni kwamba wafanyakazi wenye tija mara nyingi ni wale wanaotumia vitu vya zamani kama kalenda za karatasi na kuacha simu nje ya mikutano. Ingawa simu ni nzuri, pia ni vichocheo vikubwa kwa wengi wetu.

Mara nyingi, tunakuwa na muda wa mbali ambao si wa kupumzika kabisa. Sababu ni kwamba tunaendelea kupokea maandishi na barua pepe na bado tunafikika mitandao ya kijamii. Ikiwa wewe si mtu anayeeza kuweka simu yake mbali na kuisiacha (inahitaji nguvu ya ndani kubwa kufanya hivyo), basi wacha simu yako katika chumba kingine na tengeneza umbali. Hii itaonekana kuwa na msongo, lakini tunaweza kujikita katika kujajaza nguvu kwa kuunda eneo lisilo na skrini.

Jenga Mapumziko Kwenye Siku Yako

Kuna kazi fulani inayopaswa kufanywa kila siku, na mara nyingi inahisi ni nyingi mno kwa masaa 24 yaliyotengwa. Hakika hakuna wakati wa kusimama, kunyoosha, na kutembea kwa dakika tano, au angalau ndivyo tunavyojisemea.

Katika ukweli, ikiwa utachukua mapumziko ya dakika tano kila baada ya masaa machache kufanya kitu kisichohusiana na kazi, utafika umechoka kidogo na kuwa tayari zaidi kukabiliana na matatizo ya siku.

Fanya kitu cha kiafya wakati huu. Tembea kwa dakika fupi au kula tufaha. Kula chipsi za viazi au mikate ya sukari siyo matokeo yanayotarajiwa.

Tatizo mara nyingi liko katika matarajio yetu wenyewe. Watu wanaopambana na uchovu wa kazi mara nyingi wana viwango vya juu sana vya viwango vya kibinafsi na huzungumza chanzo wanaposhindwa kufikia kiwango hicho.

Kuwa Makusudi Kuhusu Kupumzika

Moja ya ujumbe wa Agano la Kale ulikuwa umuhimu wa Sabato. Nimesikia watu wengi wakikataa kwamba katika Agano Jipya hatuhitaji tena kuadhimisha Sabato. Je, Paulo hakusema kwamba siku moja ni kama nyingine? Je, Yesu hakawafafanulia wandani wake kwa kuharibu nafaka siku ya Sabato?

Bila kujali unaamini nini kuhusu umuhimu wa kuifanya Sabato, bado ni muhimu kuchukua muda wa kupumzika. Huu ndiyo ujumbe halisi ambao Yesu alikuwa akutoa aliposema kwamba “Sabato umetengenezwa kwa ajili ya mwanadamu, si mwanadamu kwa ajili ya Sabato” (Marko 2:27).

Kupumzika si tu kulala hadi saa 10 asubuhi kisha kutofanya chochote. Kupumzika ni kufanya maamuzi kwa makusudi yatakayosaidia kujaza upya betri zetu zilizochoka. Nenda kula kifungua kinywa na rafiki, fanya matembezi, au chukua kitabu kizuri na uende mahali pasipo huduma ya simu na ujielekeze kitu mbali na hali zinazokuchosha.

Yesu alielewa haja ya mwanadamu ya kupumzika, ndiyo sababu akamwambia wanafunzi wake “Nanyi tujiondoe kidogo kwa mahali penye upweke, mkapumzike” (Marko 6:31). Muda huu wa kupumzika ungewapa nishati kwa utumishi wao uliokuja.

Usikubali Hadithi Potofu

Watu hujinyonya hadithi mbalimbali zinazowafanya wajisukume kupita kiasi. Nitataja chache na mawazo kuhusu kila moja.

“Mimi ndiye tu anayefanya kazi hii.” Hii inaonekana kweli. Wengine nyumbani kwetu au kazini hawatusaidii kama tunavyotaka. Wakati mwingine, ni rahisi zaidi kufanya kazi yenyewe kuliko kutumia muda kumfundisha mwingine jinsi ya kuitenda. Tunapaswa kukumbuka kwamba tungemkufa, watu waliotuzunguka wangepata njia ya kufanya mambo. Tunaweza kuwaagiza baadhi ya wajibu leo kabla hatujafariki.

“Ikiwa nitamaliza kazi hii leo, kesho itakuwa rahisi.” Napendelea kuleta habari mbaya, lakini kila siku ina masaa 24, na kwa namna fulani, daima hujazana. Nimeacha wazo kwamba kuna siku fulani maisha yangu yatakuwa bila kitu lolote kwenye ratiba. Ikiwa mapumziko yatakuwepo, yatafika kwa sababu nimefanya juhudi ya kuondoa ratiba, sio kwa bahati mbaya kwamba siku moja sitakuwa na kazi yoyote.

“Mungu hatatanipa zaidi ya niwezayo kubeba.” Mungu ameahidi mambo mengi. Ameahidi kwamba wakati kuna kuwapo kwa jaribio, Atatupatia njia ya kukwepa (1 Wakorintho 10:13). Pia ameahidi kwamba hatatutuacha wala kutuachia (Waebrania 13:5). Sikuona mahali lolote katika Maandiko kuwa Mungu atatuzuia kujajaza maisha yetu kupita kiasi. Ameahidi tu kwamba atatupa fursa ya kuchagua njia nyingine na atatembea nasi sote tunapoelekea.

Mara nyingi mzigo mzito tunaoibeba ni kwa sababu watu wengine, au hata sisi wenyewe, tumeweka vitu vingi mno kwenye orodha ya majukumu. Ikiwa ninachagua kuweka wagonjwa wengi mno kwenye ratiba yangu na nahisi kuchoka, ni wakati wa kuchukua uwajibikaji kwa kile nilichokifanya, badala ya kudai ahadi ya hadithi kwamba Mungu atakunizuia kujazaa maisha yangu kwa mwendo uliotelekezwa.

“Haya yote ni mambo mema ninayofanya.” Madaktari wanakutana na hili mara nyingi. Tunataka kuongeza mgonjwa mmoja tu kwenye ratiba na kukaa kidogo jioni kujibu ujumbe mwingine kwa sababu tunajisikia kuwajibika. Tunahofu kufikiria kwamba mtu angetaka kwenda Idara ya Dharura kwa sababu hatukuwa tayari kumsaidia alipotaka.

Kwamba vitu kwenye ratiba yako ni “mambo mema” yanayomsaidia mtu mwingine na kujenga ufalme, haimaanishi kwamba huna haja ya kupunguza katika eneo fulani. Ikiwa unahisi umechoka kihisia, inahitajika kuondoa vitu vichache kwenye orodha yako ya kufanya.

Hitimisho

Kuna mambo mengine ambayo yanaweza kutajwa. Kupata msaada kutoka kwa mtu mwingine, kutafakari Maandiko, na hata kwenda mapumziko ni mambo yote ambayo yanaweza kusaidia.

Ninaposoma kuhusu baadhi ya wachungaji mashuhuri wa zamani, ninaona katika baadhi ya maisha yao mzunguko wa mwinuko na kushuka. Walijisukuma hadi kiwango cha juu, wakajihusisha katika miradi mingi, kisha wakapata mshtuko wa kihisia. Wangepumzika kwa muda, na mwezi au miwili baadaye, kuanza tena shughuli zile zile. Mzunguko huu ulidumu katika huduma yao yote.

Yesu anatueleza kuwa mzigo wake ni mwepesi, na mzigo wake ni mwembamba (Mathayo 11:28-30). Ikiwa tuko mahali pa kuchoka kabisa, tunahitaji kuzingatia kama tunabeba mzigo wa Yesu au tuko chini ya mzigo wa uumbaji wetu wenyewe.

Yesu anafahamu mipaka yetu. Anatamani tuwe na usawa, kuishi kwa njia ambayo si tu tunapata nguvu kwa leo bali pia kesho, wiki ijayo, na mwaka ujao — mpaka atakaporudi tena.

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

내가 회심했을 때, 나는 아나바프티스트라는 용어조차 들어본 적이 없었다. 다른 사람들에게 증인이 되는 것에 대해서도 별로 들어본 바가 없었다. 방금 내게 일어난 일을 모르는 내 친구들 모두가 떠올라서 생각했던 것을 기억한다. 7년 동안 사귀던 여자친구조차 이해하지 못했다. 한 가지 생각이 계속 내 머릿속을 맴돌았다. “그들에게 알려야 해!” 내게 좋은 일이 일어났고, 똑같은 일이 그들에게도 일어날 수 있다는 것을 모두가 알아야 했다! 형과 내가 많은 사람들에게 예수님을 전할 수 있는 장소를 생각하던 때를 기억한다. 우리는 메이저 리그 야구 경기에 가기로 했다. 나는 초조했고, 두려웠고, 그 일이 일어났던 것을 결코 잊지 못할 것이다. 나는 한 번도 많은 군중 앞에서 말해본 적이 없었지만, 입을 열자 하나님께서 그것을 채워 주셨다.

모르는 사람들에게만 가서 말한 것이 아니었다. 옛 친구를 보면 무슨 일이 내게 일어났는지 전하곤 했다. 그들은 대개 이미 들어봤다며 진정하라고 설득하려 들었다. 초창기 몇 년 동안 내가 실수한 일들이 있었다는 것을 먼저 인정하겠다. 놀랍게도 많은 사람들이 나를 좋아하지 않았지만, 나를 가장 싫어하는 것처럼 보였던 사람들은 스스로 기독교인이라고 말하는 사람들이었다. 어느 날 나는 평생 대부분을 기독교인으로 살아왔다는 한 연로한 남자와 이야기를 나누고 있었다. 대화 중에 그는 전구를 가리키며 말했다. “저 전구 보이죠? 말하지 않잖아요.” 나는 충격을 받았다. 그는, 그렇다고, 예수님이 우리가 세상의 빛이라고 말씀하시지만, 등불은 조용히 빛나야 한다고 말하고 있었다. 등불은 말을 하지 않는다.

나는 깜짝 놀랐다. 과연 그 말이 사실일까? 집에 돌아가 성경 공부를 했다. 머지않아 나는 마태복음 4장 23절과 같은 구절을 찾았다. “예수께서 온 갈릴리에 두루 다니사 그들의 회당에서 가르치시며 천국의 복음을 전파하시며 백성 중의 모든 병과 모든 약한 것을 고치시니라.” 그리고 마태복음 9장에서는 예수께서 “무리를 보시고 불쌍히 여기셨으니 이는 저희가 목자 없는 양과 같아서 힘이 없고 기진함이라 하시며 제자들에게 이르시되 추수할 것은 많되 일꾼이 적으니”라고 하시고 제자들에게 “그러므로 추수하는 주인에게 구하여 저의 추수할 일꾼들을 보내시게 하라”(마태복음 9:36-38)고 하셨다.

내가 보기에는 예수님이 가시는 곳마다 사람들에게 왕국에 대해 말씀하셨다. 나는 때때로 공격적으로 보이는 방식으로 하나님을 전하는 사람들을 보았다. 그러나 그렇다고 우리가 증언하지 말아야 한다는 뜻일까? 사도행전을 읽어보면 거의 그것뿐이다—복음이 퍼져 나가는 이야기! 어떤 기록에서 당국은 제자들을 붙잡아 조용히만 하면 풀어주겠다고 말했다. 그러나 제자들은 그럴 수 없다고 했다. “우리는 보고 들은 것을 말하지 않을 수 없다”(사도행전 4:20). 이후 그들은 침묵을 강요받았으니—죽음으로써였다.

얼마 뒤 나는 아나바프티스트라고 불리는 사람들에 대해 들었다. 그들을 연구하면서, 그들도 결코 침묵하지 않았음을 보기 시작했다. 나는 The Martyr’s Mirror 한 부를 주문했고, 제자들처럼 살았던 이 사람들에 대해 읽고 깜짝 놀랐다. 그들은 예수께서 말씀하신 바를 성취했다. “너희는 내 이름 때문에 모든 사람에게 미움을 당하리라 오직 끝까지 견디는 자는 구원을 얻으리라”(마태복음 10:22). 그리고 로마서 8장 36절에 “기록된 바 우리가 온종일 죽임을 당하며 도살할 양으로 여김을 받는도다”라는 말씀이 있다.

사랑하는 형제자매 여러분, 나는 불이 꺼져 가고 있다고 믿는다. 많은 우리의 아나바프티스트들이 조용하고 평화로운 삶을 사는 것에 대해 이야기하는 것을 듣는다. 예수님은 씨 뿌리는 자의 비유에서 “가시떨기 가운데 뿌린 자는 세상의 염려와 재물의 유혹이 말씀을 막아 결실이 없게 되는 자”(마태복음 13:22)라고 말씀하신다. 그것이 우리 중 많은 사람이 처한 자리일 수 있을까? 우리는 돈을 얻기 쉬운 자유의 땅 미국에 산다. 혹시 우리가 우리 자신의 부와 세상 염려에 속아 넘어간 것은 아닐까? 박해를 피하기 위해 세상과 닮아버린 것은 아닐까?

여러 해 전, 한 무리의 아나바프티스트가 박해를 피해 억압이 덜한 나라로 이주했다. 그들은 스스로를 부양하기 위해 가구점을 열었지만, 공포의 아나바프티스트였기 때문에 가구를 팔 수 없었다. 곧 상황은 절박해졌고 그들은 음식을 살 돈이 없게 되었다. 어느 날 한 부유한 남자가 가게에 들어왔다. 모든 일꾼들이 하던 일을 멈추었다. 그들은 속으로 생각했다. “아마 이 사람이 뭔가를 살지도 몰라, 그러면 우리는 먹을 수 있을 거야!” 한 늙은 형제가 다가가 그 손님에게 예수님을 아느냐고 물었다. 짧은 대화 후에 그 남자는 분을 참지 못하고 가게에서 뛰쳐나갔다. 배고픈 일꾼들은 왜 그가 유일한 판매 기회를 쫓아냈는지 늙은 형제에게 물었다. 그는 이 남자가 예수님을 알게 되는 것이 그들이 돈을 버는 것보다 훨씬 더 중요하다고 설명했다.

초기 아나바프티스트들의 사고방식에서는 예수의 복음이 가장 중요했다. 사도행전에서처럼, 그들도 보고 들은 것을 말하지 않을 수 없었다. 그리고 그들도 또한 “온종일 죽임을 당하였”다.

그렇다면 우리는 조용하고 평화로운 삶에 관한 구절을 어떻게 이해해야 하는가? 그 구절은 디모데전서 2장 1-2절에 있다. “그러므로 내가 권하노니 먼저 모든 사람을 위하여 간구와 기도와 도고와 감사하는 것이 되게 하라. 임금들과 모든 높은 지위에 있는 자들을 위하여 하라 이는 우리로 하여금 모든 경건함과 정직함으로 조용하고 평온한 생활을 하게 하려 함이라.” 사도 바울이 이 글을 쓸 때 무슨 뜻이었는가? 그가 복음에 관해 조용히 하며 죄인을 결코 도전하지 말라는 뜻이었을까? 바울이 스스로 하지 않았던 일을 우리에게 하라고 말하고 있다고 믿기 어렵다. 그리스도 자신도 결코 하지 않으셨던 일이다. 사실 성경에서 하나님을 따랐던 사람들 가운데 그들의 믿음에 대해 조용했던 사람은 없다. 믿음 때문에 체포된 초기 기독교인들의 수많은 기록에서 당국은 그들에게 그냥 조용히 있으라고 애원하곤 했다. 그러나 그들은 제자들처럼 거절했다. 그들도 조용하고 평화로운 삶보다 죽음을 택했다.

체포된 한 젊은 아나바프티스트는 첫 아이를 기다리던 사랑하는 아내를 남겨두고 떠났다. 당국은 아이가 태어나기를 기다린 뒤 유아를 감옥에 있는 새 아버지에게 데려갔다. 그에게 이제 아버지가 되었으니 집에 가서 아내와 아들과 함께 있을 수 있다고, 심지어 같은 신앙을 유지할 수도 있지만 국가 교회에 대하여 죄를 책망하지 않고 조용히 있으라고 말했다. 젊은 아버지는 거절했다. 그에게 조용히 있는 것은 선택지가 아니었다. 그들은 그를 화형에 처했다.

그러면 디모데전서 2장 1-2절은 무엇을 의미하는가? 성경과 초대 교회의 그리스도인들은 모두 복음을 전파하는 데 전념했다. 그들은 그리스도의 교회에 온 힘을 기울였다. 그들은 복음을 전파하기 위해 이곳저곳을 다니며 산과 숲이나 사람들이 모이는 아무 데서나 모임을 가졌다. 그것이 그들의 삶이었다. 디모데전서 2장의 구절에서 바울은 권세자들이 우리가 복음을 전하게 내버려 두도록 기도하라고 말하고 있는 것 같다. 그리스도인들은 복음을 전하고 왕국을 향해 나아가야 한다. 우리의 기도는 권세자들이 우리가 평안히 살게 해 주시기를 구하는 것이며, 그동안 우리는 평화의 왕을 섬기려 하는 것이다.

오늘날 죄인을 결코 도전하거나 형제를 바로잡지 않으면서 조용하고 평화로운 삶에 안주하면 기독교인되기 쉽다. 그러나 누가 그것이 쉬울 것이라고 말했는가?

우리가 아이티에 살던 때 우리는 교회에 예수를 따르는 대가에 대해 가르쳤다. 아이티 사람들의 삶에 예수의 가르침을 적용한 간증을 듣는 것은 놀라운 일이었다. 어느 번에는 두 교인들이 복음을 따르다가 직장을 잃게 될 처지에 놓였다고 말했다. 진리를 따라 설 때 그들이 결단하는 것을 들으니 기뻤다. 교회의 또 다른 자매는 자녀들이 다니는 학교에서 유니폼을 입어야 하고 소녀들은 바지를 입도록 요구받는다고 말했다. 그녀가 딸을 단정한 드레스로 학교에 보냈을 때 딸은 교장으로부터 그런 옷을 입고는 등교해서는 안 된다는 쪽지를 들고 집으로 돌아왔다.

베드로전서 4장 14절은 이렇게 말한다. “만일 그리스도의 이름으로 욕을 받을지라도 너희는 복이 있나니 영광과 하나님의 신이 너희 위에 머물렀음이라 저희는 악을 말하되 너희는 선을 말하리라.”

참된 기쁨은 고난에서 온다. 고난은 예수께 복종함으로 온다. 우리가 세상이 멸망해 가는 동안 사소한 일들로 너무 바쁘지는 않은가? 초대 교인들처럼 예수님을 따르자. 사람들이 그들 안에서 하나님의 능력이 역사하고 있음을 부인할 수 없었던 그들처럼 말이다. 우리에게는 모든 사람이 필요로 하는 것이 있다. 무엇을 기다리고 있는가? 함께 다시 연합하여 모이고 자기를 부인하며 십자가를 지고 그를 따르자!

It was one of those Sunday afternoons in late spring when the sun was finally shining warmly. It was the time of year when little boys seem to have plenty of extra energy. Little Davy was sitting on the road bank with some neighborhood boys who had stopped by. He felt like jumping up and down in anticipation of the upcoming race.

Two older boys, Big David and Paul, showed up with brand-new bicycles. These were not the ordinary bicycles the other boys had. They were beautiful Vista bicycles with gleaming new paint, shiny chrome fenders, and three speeds. These bicycles glided smoothly on the chip-and seal road without a rattle. With new ball bearings, they whizzed along with hardly any effort being applied to the pedals. Even though there did not seem to be much difference between the bicycles, Big David’s was a gleaming chestnut brown, and Paul’s a sparkling metal flake blue.

“Well,” Big David began to brag, “With my longer legs, and freshly sprayed WD40, my bike is sure to be the fastest.”

“No,” challenged Paul, “my shorter legs can pump faster, and Schwinn’s high-test bicycle oil by far outperforms WD40, which really is only for squeaks.”

“A race! A race!” the other boys said, “Why not settle it with a race?”

“Okay,” Big David said, “We’ll have a race and see whose bike is really the fastest.”

“You bet!” Paul agreed. “We’ll start at the top of Billy’s hill and race all the way down to the bottom,” he said, pointing to the road bank where the other boys were sitting.

One, two, three, GO and they were off! Down the hill they came, pedaling for all they were worth.

“Go Paul!” and “Go Big David!” shouted the boys at the bottom of the hill. All the commotion woke up Little Davy’s rat terrier dog, Nellie. Yapping loudly, Nellie zoomed around the silo as fast as her four little legs could carry her. She headed straight for Big David’s bicycle in the front, barking loudly to try to make it stop. Poor Nellie did not realize another bicycle was trying to pass up the first one.

Thump, the passing bicycle hit the dog! Crash, bang, the two bicycles ran into each other!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Two boys flew over the handlebars and landed hard on the road. Those shining bicycles were no longer gleaming. They were lying on a heap, scratched and streaked with tar. Nellie limped back beside the silo and stayed lying there for several hours.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.

كان ذلك أحد أمسيات يوم الأحد في أواخر الربيع عندما بدأت الشمس أخيراً تشرق بدفء. كان ذلك الوقت من السنة الذي يبدو فيه أن الأولاد الصغار يملكون الكثير من الطاقة الإضافية. كان الصغير ديفي جالساً على حافة الطريق مع بعض أولاد الحي الذين توقفوا لزيارة. كان يشعر برغبة في القفز صعوداً وهبوطاً بترقّب للسباق القادم.

ظهر صبيان أكبر سناً، ديفيد الكبير وبول، يحملان دراجتين جديدتين كلياً. لم تكونا الدراجة العاديتين اللتين يملكهما الأولاد الآخرون. كانتا دراجتي فيستا جميلتين بطلاء لامع جديد ورفارف من الكروم اللامع وثلاث سرعات. كانت هاتان الدراجتان تنزلقان بسلاسة على طريق رقائق الإسفلت دون اهتزاز. مع محامل كُرية جديدة، كانتا تسرعان مع بذل قليل جداً من الجهد على الدواسات. وعلى الرغم من أنه لم يبدو أن هناك فرقاً كبيراً بين الدراجتين، إلا أن دراجة ديفيد الكبير كانت بنية صدئية لامعة، ودراجة بول زرقاء لامعة بنقش رقائق معدنية.

«حسناً»، بدأ ديفيد الكبير يتفاخر، «بساقي الأطول وبزيت WD40 الذي رُشّ تواً، دراجتي بالتأكيد ستكون الأسرع.»

«لا»، تحدى بول، «ساقاي الأقصر يمكنها الضخ أسرع، وزيت دراجات شويْن عالي الجودة يتفوق بكثير على WD40، الذي هو فعلاً فقط للصرخات.»

«سباق! سباق!» قال الأولاد الآخرون، «لم لا نقرّره بسباق؟»

«حسناً»، قال ديفيد الكبير، «سنقيم سباقاً ونرى أي دراجة هي الأسرع حقاً.»

«أراهن!» وافق بول. «سنبدأ من قمة تلة بيلي ونركب بالسباق حتى الأسفل،» قال مشيراً إلى حافة الطريق حيث كان الأولاد الآخرون جالسين.

واحد، اثنان، ثلاثة، انطلقوا وانطلقوا! نزلوا التلة وهم يدفعون على الدواسات بكل ما يملكون.

«انطلق يا بول!» و «انطلق يا ديفيد الكبير!» صاح الأولاد في أسفل التلة. أيقظ كل هذا الضجيج كلب ديفي الصغير من سلالة رات تيرير، نيلّي. ونباحاً عالياً، انطلقت نيلّي حول الصومعة بأسرع ما تملك من قوّة على أربع سيقانها الصغيرة. توجّهت مباشرة نحو دراجة ديفيد الكبير في المقدمة، تنبح عالياً محاولة إيقافها. المسكينة نيلّي لم تدرك أن دراجة أخرى كانت تحاول أن تتجاوز الأولى.

ثُمّةَ... اصطدمت الدراجة العابرة بالكلب! تصادم، تحطّم، اصطدمت الدراجتان ببعضهما!

«هيه – آه!» أووف! طار صبيان فوق المقود وسقطا بقوة على الطريق. تلك الدراجات اللامعة لم تعد تلمع. كانت ملقاة في كومة، مخدوشة ومخططة بطبقة من القطران. عادت نيلّي تعرج بجانب الصومعة وبقيت مستلقية هناك لساعات عدة.

وقف الأولاد الآخرون على الحافة وأفواههم مفتوحة. ركضوا بسرعة إلى الصبيين الكبيرين المستلقين بجانب دراجتيهما الجديدتين. «هل أنتما بخير؟» سألوا.

«سأكون بخير»، قال بول ببطء، «لكن لا مزيد من السباقات. من يهتم أصلاً أي دراجة هي الأسرع.»

على الرغم من أن الصغير ديفي الآن جد، لم ينسَ سباق الدراجات في ذلك اليوم الأحد البعيد عندما تعلم ديفيد الكبير وبول أن التفاخر والتباهي عادة ما ينتهي بانهيار.

"O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for His mercy endureth for ever"
—Psalm 136:26

In your journey of life, from infancy to where you are today, have you ever taken a few minutes to meditate on the mercy God has shown you? Infancy to childhood, childhood to youth, youth to adulthood, and beyond, God's everlasting mercy is upon them that fear Him! The scripture says in Deuteronomy 7:9 that the mercy of God extends way past our short lives here on earth, even to a thousand generations. Take a moment and wonder in the glory and beauty of this unchanging, eternal attribute of God!

As we take a look at the history behind this hymn, let us endeavor to see the hand of God at work in the life of the hymn writer. The hymn, "When All Thy Mercies O My God," written in 1712, has been published in 994 hymnals and is to this day in the list of the best 100 hymns ever written. As the writer nears the end of his time on earth, he reflects in this hymn his awe at the mercies of God toward him throughout his life.

Joseph Addison, born May 1, 1672, was an English essayist, poet, and man of letters. Concerning his birth, we find that he “appeared weak and unlikely to live", Mr. Tyers says.* And that “he was laid out for dead as soon as he was born.” Without doubt, the providence of God preserved his young life and gave him nearly half a century to serve Him on the earth. He was the eldest son of Lancelot Addison, a well-learned man and minister in his church. His father, being a studious man himself, made sure his son Joseph had a good education. He commenced his studies in his hometown of Milston, in Wiltshire, England.

While in school around 1685, the 13-year-old hymn writer met and became best of friends with Richard Steele, the two of them being only a few months apart in age. They continued their friendship throughout the years, and 27 years later from 1711 to 1712, they cofounded The Spectator magazine, in which this hymn was first published.

After passing through several schools, Addison went to Oxford when he was about 15 years old. While he was there, he continued to gain in learning and skill, especially in the areas of writing Latin poems and essays. By the time he was 22, in 1694, he also began to show his skill at writing English poetry.

One of the most notable details of his life that conveyed to him the mercy of God is how he managed to narrowly escape an awful shipwreck. It was this tragedy and his frightening tale of survival that would go on to inspire the writing of this uplifting hymn.

Here is the hymn with the original 13 verses:

When all Thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view,
I’m lost In wonder, love and praise.

Thy Providence my life sustained,
And all my wants redressed,
While in the silent womb I lay,
And hung upon the breast.

To all my weak complaints and cries
Thy mercy lent an ear,
Ere yet my feeble thoughts had learned,
To form themselves in prayer.

Unnumbered comforts to my soul
Thy tender care bestowed,
Before my infant heart conceived
From Whom those comforts flowed.

When in the slippery paths of youth
With heedless steps I ran,
Thine arm unseen conveyed me safe,
And led me up to man.

Through hidden dangers, toils, and deaths,
It gently cleared my way;
And through the pleasing snares of vice,
More to be feared than they.

O how shall words with equal warmth
The gratitude declare,
That glows within my ravished heart?
But thou canst read it there.

Thy bounteous hand with worldly bliss
Hath made my cup run o’er;
And, in a kind and faithful Friend,
Hath doubled all my store.

Ten thousand thousand precious gifts
My daily thanks employ;
Nor is the last a cheerful heart
That tastes those gifts with joy.

When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou
With health renewed my face;
And, when in sins and sorrows sunk,
Revived my soul with grace.

Through every period of my life
Thy goodness I’ll pursue
And after death, in distant worlds,
The glorious theme renew.

When nature fails, and day and night
Divide Thy works no more,
My ever grateful heart,
O Lord,Thy mercy shall adore.

Through all eternity to Thee
A joyful song I’ll raise;
For, oh, eternity’s too short
To utter all Thy praise!

As we endeavor to understand the life and story of the hymnologist, let's take a short look at some disappointments he faced. Being single into his 40s, he had hopes of someday having a happy marriage. His marriage to Charlotte, a widow of 15 years, didn’t turn out as he had anticipated. It is said that their courtship was long and anxious. They were married in August 1716 in his 44th year. A quote states that “He is said to have first known her by becoming tutor to her son. The marriage, if uncontradicted report can be credited, made no addition to his happiness; it neither found them nor made them equal."* In addition to his less-than-ideal marriage, the loss of his good friend Richard Steele sometime after that took a toll on him.

By the year 1717, his health began to decline rapidly, and by March 1718, he had to resign some of his work positions, having a great need for rest and quietness. "The disease under which Addison laboured appears to have been asthma. It became more violent after his retirement from office and was now accompanied by dropsy. His deathbed was placid and resigned, and comforted by those religious hopes which he had so often suggested to others..." *

One last note I will include here on the life of the hymn writer is the account of his passing. There was a young man by the name of Lord Warwick, rough and loose in character, who Addison had often tried to win to the faith, all to no avail. Nearing the end of his life, he endeavored one last attempt to impress this young man with the importance of Christianity. He sent for him to come and be present as he passed away, saying, "I have sent for you that you may see how a Christian can die." We have no record of how this experience affected Warwick’s behavior, but we can assume that it most likely did. Joseph Addison died at Holland House on the 17th of June, 1719, six weeks after his 47th birthday. He is buried in the Poet's Corner of Westminster Abbey.

This hymn has several tunes: “St Peter,” composed by Alexander Robert Reinagle in 1836, is used in the Church Hymnal and Christian Hymnary. The tune "Geneva" was composed by John Cole in 1805. He was born in Tewksbury, England, and came to the United States in his boyhood. Baltimore, Maryland became his American home, and he was educated there. Early in life, he became a musician and music publisher. He continued to compose music until his death. This tune is found in the Zion's Praises, Hymns of the Church, and Harmonia Sacra. The tune "Contemplation", composed by F.A.Gore Ouseley, is more widely used by evangelical and other church groups. Other hymns by Joseph Addison include "The Lord my Pasture Shall Prepare" and "The Spacious Firmament." Here is one final quote to help us understand who Joseph Addison was and what he believed. "His religion has nothing in it enthusiastic or superstitious; he appears neither weakly credulous nor wantonly skeptical; his morality is neither dangerously lax nor impracticably rigid. All the enchantment of fancy and all the cogency of argument are employed to recommend to the reader his real interest, the care of pleasing the Author of his being."

*sourced from Wikipedia and hymnary.org

«اِعْطُوا الشُّكْرَ لِإِلَهِ السَّمَاوَاتِ، لأَنَّ رَحْمَتَهُ إِلَى الأَبَدِ»
—مزمور 136:26

في رحلتك الحياتية، من الطفولة إلى حيث أنت اليوم، هل أخذت بضع دقائق للتأمل في الرحمة التي أظهرها الله لك؟ من الطفولة إلى الصبا، ومن الصبا إلى الشباب، ومن الشباب إلى البلوغ، وما بعده، رحمة الله الأبدية على الذين يهابونه! تقول الكتابات في تثنية 7:9 إن رحمة الله تمتد إلى ما بعد حياتنا القصيرة هنا على الأرض، حتى إلى ألف جيل. خذ لحظة وتأمل في مجد وجمال هذه الصفة الثابتة والأزلية لله!

وأثناء نظرتنا إلى التاريخ الكامن وراء هذا النشيد، لنحرص على رؤية يد الله تعمل في حياة كاتب النشيد. النشيد "عندما تحيط بي كل رَحَمَتِكَ، يا إلهي"، الذي كُتب عام 1712، نُشر في 994 كتاب ترانيم ولا يزال إلى اليوم ضمن قائمة أفضل 100 نشيد كُتبت على الإطلاق. وبينما يقترب الكاتب من نهاية زمانه على الأرض، يعكس في هذا النشيد رهبة رحمة الله نحوه طوال حياته.

جوزيف أديسون، المولود في 1 مايو 1672، كان كاتب مقالات وشاعرًا ورجل أقلام إنجليزيًا. وبخصوص ولادته نجد أنه "بدا ضعيفًا ومن غير المرجح أن يعيش"، كما يقول السيد تايرز.* وأنه "وُضِع على أنه ميت فور ولادته." بلا شك، حفظت عناية الله مقدرًا حياته الصغرى وأعطته ما يقرب من نصف قرن ليخدمه على الأرض. كان الابن الأكبر للانسيلوت أديسون، رجل متعلم وواعظ في كنيسته. وبما أن والده رجل مجدٍ في الدراسة، فقد حرص على أن يحصل ابنه جوزيف على تعليم جيد. بدأ دراسته في بلدته ميلستون في مقاطعة ويلتشير في إنجلترا.

أثناء وجوده في المدرسة حوالي عام 1685، التقى كاتب النشيد البالغ من العمر 13 عامًا بصديقه المقرّب ريتشارد ستيل، وكان الفارق بينهما بضعة أشهر فقط. استمرت صداقتهما على مر السنين، وبعد 27 سنة، من 1711 إلى 1712، شاركا في تأسيس مجلة The Spectator، التي نُشر فيها هذا النشيد لأول مرة.

بعد الانتقال عبر عدة مدارس، ذهب أديسون إلى أكسفورد عندما كان حوالي 15 عامًا. وهناك واصل اكتسابه للعلم والمهارة، خاصة في كتابة القصائد والمقالات اللاتينية. وبحلول أن بلغ 22 سنة، في عام 1694، بدأ أيضًا يظهر براعته في كتابة الشعر الإنجليزي.

من أبرز تفاصيل حياته التي بيَّنت له رحمة الله كيف نجا بأعجوبة من غرق مروع. كانت هذه المأساة وقصته المخيفة في النجاة من أسباب إلهام كتابة هذا النشيد المشجِّع.

إليك النشيد بالأبيات الثلاثة عشر الأصلية:

عندما تحيط بي كل رَحَمَتِكَ، يا إلهي،
تُراقب نفسي النابعة،
وصفقتُ للمنظر هائمة،
ضائعة في العجبِ والمحبةِ والحمدِ.

عنايَتُكَ السامية أمدّت حياتي،
وكشفتْ كل نواقصي،
بينما كنتُ في الرحم الساكنِ أستلقي،
وأتشبثُّ على الصدر.

لشكواي الضعيفة ونوحي
مدّت رحمتُك أذنًا صاغية،
قبل أن تتعلم أفكاري الضعيفة،
أن تُشكِّل ذاتها في صلاةٍ.

عزازات لا تُحصى لروحي
منحتْها رعايتُك الرقيقة،
قبل أن يَخْطُرَ في قلب طفولتي
مَنْ تُفِدُّ تلك العزازات.

حين غدت طرق الشباب زلقةً
وسرتُ بخطواتٍ متهورة،
ذراعُكَ الخفي أنقلَني سالماً،
وقادني إلى بلوغي إنسانًا.

عبر مخاطر خفية وكدٍّ وموتٍ،
نَقَت طريقي بلطف؛
وعبر فخاخ اللذة المحببة،
التي تُخشى أكثر منها.

أوهُ كيفَ تعلنُ الكلماتُ بحرارةٍ متكافئةٍ
الامتنانَ الذي يُبدي،
ويتلألأ في قلبي المفتون؟
لكنك تستطيع قراءته هناك.

يدُك الكريمةُ بالنعيمِ الدنيوي
أفرَغتْ كأسِي في فيضٍ؛
وفي صديقٍ محبٍّ ومخلصٍ،
ضاعفتْ ما عندي من ذخيرة.

عشرون ألفًا من الهبات الثمينة
توظف شكرَـي اليومي؛
وليس آخرُها قلبٌ بشوشٌ
يتلذذ بتلك الهبات بفرح.

حينُ استماتَ بي المرضُ، كثيرًا قد جددتَ وجهي بالصحة؛
وعندما غُرِقْتُ في الخطايا والأحزان،
أحيةَتْ روحي بالنعمة.

عبر كل فترةٍ من حياتي
سأطاردُ لطفَك؛
وبعد الموت، في عوالم بعيدة،
سأجَدِّدُ هذا الموضوع المجيد.

عندما تخبو الطبيعة، وتفترقُ نهارٌ وليلٌ
عن أعمالك فلا تعود تُفكَّك،
قلبي الدائم الشكران،
يا ربُ، سيرتّلُ رحمتك ويعظّمها.

طوال الأبديةِ لكَ
سأرفع أنشودة فرح؛
لأن، آه، الأبديةَ قصيرةٌ جدًا
لتفوه بكل مديحك!

بينما نسعى لفهم حياة وقصة مؤلف النشيد، دعونا نُلقي نظرة سريعة على بعض خيبات الأمل التي واجهها. بقي عازبًا حتى الأربعينات من عمره، وكان يأمل أن ينال زواجًا سعيدًا يومًا ما. لم تَكن زواجه من شارلوت، أرملة توفي زوجها قبل 15 سنة، كما كان يتوقع. ويقال إن مواعدتهما كانت طويلة وقلقة. تزوجا في أغسطس 1716 في عامه الرابع والأربعين. وتذكر اقتباسات أن "يقال إنه عرفها أولًا عندما أصبح معلمًا لابنها. الزواج، إن صدق التقرير غير المتناقض، لم يُضف إلى سعادته؛ لم يجدِدهما ولا جعلهما متساويين."* بالإضافة إلى زواجه الذي لم يكن مثالياً، فقد أخذت خسارة صديقه الحميم ريتشارد ستيل بعد ذلك أثرًا عليه.

بحلول عام 1717، بدأت صحته تتدهور بسرعة، وبحلول مارس 1718، اضطر إلى الاستقالة من بعض مناصبه، إذ كانت حاجته كبيرة للراحة والهدوء. «يبدو أن المرض الذي عانى منه أديسون كان الربو. وأصبح أكثر عنفًا بعد تقاعده من العمل ورافقه آنذاك الاستسقاء. كانت فراش موته هادئًا ومُستسلمًا، معزَّى بتلك الآمال الدينية التي اقترحها غالِبًا على الآخرين...» *

ملاحظة أخيرة أوردها هنا عن حياة كاتب النشيد هي رواية وفاته. كان هناك شاب يدعى اللورد ووريك، ذا طبع خشن ومتحرر، حاوَل أديسون مرارًا جذبَه إلى الإيمان، لكن دون جدوى. قرب نهاية حياته، بذل محاولة أخيرة ليُبْقِي هذا الشاب شاهدًا على أهمية المسيحية. أرسله ليحضر وهو يفارق الحياة، قائلاً: «أرسلتُ لك لتَرى كيف يموت المسيحي.» لا سجل لدينا عن كيف أثّرت تلك التجربة في سلوك ووريك، لكن يمكننا الافتراض أنها على الأرجح أثّرت فيه. توفي جوزيف أديسون في هولاند هاوس في 17 يونيو 1719، بعد ستة أسابيع من عيد ميلاده السابع والأربعين. ودفن في ركن الشعراء في كاتدرائية وستمنستر.

لهذا النشيد عدة ألحان: "سانت بيتر"، ألفه ألكسندر روبرت رايناجل عام 1836، ويُستخدم في كتاب الترانيم الكنسي وChristian Hymnary. لحن "جنيف" ألّفه جون كول عام 1805. وُلد في توكسبري بإنجلترا، وجاء إلى الولايات المتحدة في صباه. أصبحت بالتيمور بولاية ماريلاند موطنه الأمريكي وتلقى تعليمه هناك. في حياته المبكرة أصبح موسيقيًا وناشرًا للموسيقى. واصل تأليف الموسيقى حتى وفاته. يوجد هذا اللحن في Zion's Praises وHymns of the Church وHarmonia Sacra. اللحن "تأمّل"، ألفه ف. أ. غور أوسيلي، يُستخدم على نطاق أوسع من قبل الجماعات الإنجيلية وغيرها من المجموعات الكنسية. من ترانيم جوزيف أديسون الأخرى: "الرب يُعد مرتعي" و"الفلك الواسع." وإليك اقتباس أخير يساعدنا على فهم من كان جوزيف أديسون وما كان يؤمن به. «دينُه لا يشتمل على شيء متحمّس أو خرافي؛ فهو لا يبدو ساذجَ الإيمان ولا متشككًا مُتعمدًا؛ أخلاقه ليست رخوة بشكل خطير ولا متشددة بصورة لا تُعقل. كل سحر الخيال وكل قوة الحجة تُستعمل لتوصية القارئ بمصلحته الحقيقية، رعاية إرضاء خالق وجوده.»

*المصدر من ويكيبيديا وhymnary.org

I doubt that there is a soul alive that has not been offended at one time or another. The persistent weeds of evil influence seem to sprout at every corner, testing the best of blooming relationships. The more communication tools we possess, the more miscommunication we seem to encounter, and people are offended. Ministers of the Gospel today are expected to be soft and effeminate lest they offend their listeners. While we certainly must meet people where they are and seek not to offend them, the bane of the modern church is not the bold and offensive minister.

I wish to give no license to hardhearted preachers who are void of tenderness and tears. Woe be unto the dry-eyed prophets who wield the sword of the Lord without an ounce of consideration that there are real people between the ears that they are chopping off in the process. Yet, it seems that there is an epidemic of our day that has surpassed the bubonic plague, outstripped the damage of polio, and makes our modern cancer appear like a minor inconvenience. I speak to the outbreak of the millions of offended hearts that are arising from the rubbish of the innumerable hordes of broken and strained relationships about us on every hand. Jesus mentioned that one of the signs of the end times is that “then shall many be offended . . . and shall hate one another” (Matthew 24:10). Divorce-riddled homes have risen to an all-time high, producing a generation of immense mistrust and pain. Couples will deem themselves as incompatible and separate at the slightest offense. Christians will spend years outside a church setting because they have been offended by fellow believers.

Many will automatically side with the offended party, assuming them to be a victim. Many times they are. “Woe unto the world because of offences!” (Matthew 18:7) But the equation changes when we consider that the sinless Christ offended many. He told His disciples that they must eat His flesh and many left Him. He informed the inner 12 that had stuck with Him, “All ye shall be offended because of me this night” (Mark 14:27). The Pharisees were offended when Christ exposed their vain worship, and Jesus offended His own countrymen simply by doing good. The Greek word is skandalízō meaning “to scandalize”.1 In Hebrew, it means “a stumbling block”. The problem is that many today will stumble over the slightest obstruction in their path and the molehill becomes a mountain.

“Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them” (Psalm 119:165). What shall we say then to this passage? Here are people who have learned how to walk upon the rocky path of life without going down every time a discomfiting obstacle arises before them. We wish to heap no condemnation upon the sensitive soul, but the word sensitive is not in the Bible. The closest word we can find there is sensual, which is very similar in its roots and means natural. Christ described these plants as having “not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended” (Matthew 13:20-21). It is so easy and very natural to feel sorry for the offended. They carry a tremendous sob story, and they usually share it in tears. “In many things, we offend all” (James 3:2). No one is as sinless in their offending as Christ, so there is usually an element of truth poured out against the offender. It seems to me that we all would be much further down the road if we would withhold some of our sympathy for the offended and spend our energies teaching them how to walk upright on the path of life despite the jagged and copious stumbling stones that greet us daily upon our journey. We will learn to live life unoffended when we learn to . . .

Walk Worthy

“I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called, with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love” (Ephesians 4:1-2). To walk worthy, as Paul describes it here, is to walk in humility. “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall” (Proverbs 16:18). The more pride-laden our vessel, the more apt we are to be offended. The more honestly we appraise our worth, the less offended we shall be when derided. More humble equals less stumble. When we are accused of a wrong, it always hurts. Jesus says that we should be happy when people say all manner of evil against us falsely. While such a demeaning wound may fester under our skin, there is a condition that is far worse. That is when people say all evil against us truly. Many accusations against us carry a certain percentage of truth in them. It is this portion that the Lord would have us to reckon with, rather than decrying the overstatement. While these falsities levied against us may raise our ire, they are not the reason we stumble and walk around with consequential bruises. Offense arises when the opinion of another doesn't measure up to the extent we tout ourselves.

“Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way, take up the stumbling block out of the way of my people. For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones” (Isaiah 57:14-15). Here, Isaiah instructs us to remove the stumbling block but makes no mention of the offender. The antidote is to be of a contrite and humble spirit. We will never be able to exterminate every avenue of offense. But if reckoned correctly, there is no offense that shall ever be able to divert us from the promise, “they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint” (Isaiah 40:31). It is predominantly our pride which stands in the way of our successful journey, rather than ill-treatment.

Walk In Love

“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet smelling savour. But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints; neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting . . .” (Ephesians 5:2-4). It takes no scholar to observe the stumblings of a selfish fool. This selfish ambition to obtain friends, wealth, and affluence is guaranteed to bring a man flat on his nose at some time or another. The trail of sins mentioned here are all following in tow to the gratifying of self. King Ahasuerus counseled of Haman on how to honor a worthy man. Haman’s narcissistic mind immediately brooded, “To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?” (Esther 6:6). God had other plans thus the man who was so offended by Mordecai was hung upon the gallows of his own creation. Selfish souls can point to a thousand and one reasons why they are not attaining their aspirations. Somebody wronged them. An unfortunate turn of events derailed them. But it was not Mordecai, Esther, nor even Ahasuerus that brought Haman stumbling to his bitter end. It was his own refusal to walk in love and to sacrifice himself for others that wrought the malignant demise in his soul.

Walk as Children of Light

“Walk as children of light . . . proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them” (Ephesians 5:8-11). Our innate passions contain the third rock of offense. There may be things that we believe are acceptable to our Lord, which are not. There are those who have “itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables” (2 Timothy 4:3-4). This may affect those with the most noble intentions and firm beliefs. Christ forewarned His disciples that they would be put out of the synagogues so that when it happened, they “should not be offended” (John 16:1-4).

John the Baptist was a burning and a shining light and no prophet born of women had risen greater. He walked worthy of his calling, baptized the Lord, and rebuked the Pharisees. He walked in love, and multitudes “were willing for a season to rejoice in his light” (John 5:35). Yet the day came when he sent his disciples to ask Jesus: Art thou he that should come? Or look we for another? To which Jesus replied, “Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached ... and blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me” (Luke 7:20-23). Christ's response would indicate that this apparently did not fully fit the aspirations of what John had in mind, and he was struggling to accept it. Like his Old Testament counterpart, Elijah, these like passions provided the fodder for the flames of discouragement. It seemed to John that evil had enveloped the nation and God wasn't doing His part.

We may mean well, but our own passionate feelings are not a good gauge of proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. Phaltiel was a dear soul who fell into such deceit. He had been given Michal by King Saul himself. The princess was no doubt a delicate and pleasing prize. David had evidently valued her so, for he risked his life and doubled the dowry with two hundred Philistine foreskins to secure her hand in marriage. But Phaltiel thought nothing of that, relishing his own good fortune and so enjoyed her company for years. Though this arrangement may have been socially acceptable at the time, no man has the right to receive what another has no right to give. The day came when “they sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish. And her husband went with her along weeping behind her” (2 Samuel 3:15-16). We know very little of Phaltiel, but if we dismiss ourselves from his emotional avalanche, we must declare him faulty. We dare not let our compassionate heart turn toward him or toward anyone who is offended when asked to separate from works of darkness. When these passionate feelings are allowed to rule, offense is the inevitable result. “For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? But if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God” (1 Peter 2:20) . . .

Walk Circumspectly

“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise” (Ephesians 5:15). “Be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men” (1 Corinthians 14:20). Herein we must honestly acknowledge that ignorance is not bliss. To enter the narrow gate may require a broad mind. Not so broad to allow sin, but broad enough to allow God. Circumspect is a compound word formed from the Latin words circum (around) and spectare (to behold). The one-dimensional soul will spend his days being offended, for he cannot see from the viewpoint of any but his own. There are over a dozen solid scriptures warning us against doing what is right in our own eyes. We must learn to honestly consider the counsel and wisdom of others lest we fall into condemnation.

In her early years, Michal loved David with deep and fervent loyalty but later fell prey to rash judgment. “As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal, Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart” (2 Samuel 6:16). As Michal viewed the scene from her upper vantage, there were two things evident. First, David was exuberantly thankful, and his joy knew no bounds. This is first love, “for whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God” (2 Corinthians 5:13). Second, during David's ecstatic dancing in his loin cloth, his discretion elapsed, and his flesh became a bit public. This would require great circumspection to view from another portal, and Michal will have none of it. Upon his entrance to bless his house, David was met with a blast of pent-up bigotry from his offended and sarcastic wife. While the accusation carried a dimension of truth, to cling to it as supreme was shameful prejudice. God had no sympathy for it and “therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death” (2 Samuel 6:23). Many a good woman has judged her man from her singular corner and parched the soil of the home with the same arid judgment. This narrow-mindedness will never be fruitful no matter how blatant the accusation. There is a correct way to express concern, but the outpouring of biased judgment will turn a celestial oasis into a barren wasteland in a prompt fashion.

“A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle” (Proverbs 18:19). So it is with a sister, husband, wife, friend, etc. While causes for offense abound on every side, does Christ desire us to be offended? Will He salute our sour and shriveled soul? Perhaps He gave us this test so that we may have root within ourselves, “that no man should be moved by these afflictions” (1 Thessalonians 3:3). While we may not be able to control our feelings during times of inward pain, we each can choose a redemptive path and walk in the Spirit. It is a choice to broadcast grievances, nurse hurts, withdraw from the offender, and decline to believe all things. Like the brother offended, these contentions serve to lock the soul like the bars of a castle. But who holds the power for release?

J doute qu'il existe une âme vivante qui n'ait été offensée à un moment ou à un autre. Les mauvaises herbes persistantes de l'influence du mal semblent pousser à chaque coin, mettant à l'épreuve les meilleures relations en fleur. Plus nous possédons d'outils de communication, plus nous semblons rencontrer de malentendus, et les gens sont offensés. Aujourd'hui, on attend des ministres de l'Évangile qu'ils soient doux et efféminés de peur d'offenser leurs auditeurs. Bien que nous devions certainement rencontrer les gens là où ils sont et chercher à ne pas les offenser, le fléau de l'église moderne n'est pas le ministre hardi et offensant.

Je ne veux donner aucune licence aux prédicateurs endurcis qui sont dépourvus de tendresse et de larmes. Malheur aux prophètes aux yeux secs qui brandissent l'épée du Seigneur sans la moindre considération pour les personnes réelles entre lesquelles ils coupent dans le processus. Pourtant, il semble qu'il y ait une épidémie de notre époque qui a surpassé la peste bubonique, dépassé les ravages de la polio, et fait paraître notre cancer moderne comme une simple gêne. Je parle de l'éclosion des millions de cœurs offensés qui surgissent des décombres des innombrables hordes de relations brisées et tendues autour de nous en toute direction. Jésus a mentionné que l'un des signes des derniers temps est que « alors plusieurs seront scandalisés... et ils se haïront les uns les autres » (Matthieu 24:10). Les foyers frappés par le divorce ont atteint un niveau record, produisant une génération de méfiance et de douleur immenses. Les couples se jugeront incompatibles et se sépareront à la moindre offense. Des chrétiens passeront des années en dehors d'un cadre d'église parce qu'ils ont été offensés par des frères en Christ.

Beaucoup prendront automatiquement le parti de la personne offensée, la supposant victime. Bien souvent, ils le sont. « Malheur au monde à cause des scandales ! » (Matthieu 18:7) Mais l'équation change quand nous considérons que le Christ sans péché a offensé beaucoup de gens. Il dit à ses disciples qu'ils devaient manger sa chair et beaucoup le quittèrent. Il informa les douze intimes qui étaient restés avec lui : « Vous tous serez scandalisés à mon sujet cette nuit » (Marc 14:27). Les pharisiens furent offensés lorsque le Christ exposa leur culte vain, et Jésus offensa même ses compatriotes simplement en faisant le bien. Le mot grec est skandalízō signifiant « scandaliser ».1 En hébreu, il signifie « une pierre d'achoppement ». Le problème est que beaucoup aujourd'hui trébuchent à la moindre obstruction sur leur chemin et que la taupinière devient une montagne.

« Une grande paix ont ceux qui aiment ta loi : et rien ne les scandalise » (Psaume 119:165). Que devons-nous dire alors de ce passage ? Ici sont des gens qui ont appris à marcher sur le chemin rocailleux de la vie sans tomber à chaque fois qu'un obstacle déplaisant se présente devant eux. Nous ne voulons pas condamner l'âme sensible, mais le mot « sensible » n'est pas dans la Bible. Le mot le plus proche que nous y trouvons est sensuel, qui est très similaire dans ses racines et signifie naturel. Le Christ décrivit ces plantes comme n'ayant « pas de racine en eux, mais ils durent un moment : et quand la tribulation ou la persécution survient à cause de la parole, aussitôt il est scandalisé » (Matthieu 13:20-21). Il est si facile et très naturel d'avoir pitié des offensés. Ils portent une histoire déchirante, et ils la partagent généralement en larmes. « En beaucoup de choses nous péchons tous » (Jacques 3:2). Personne n'est aussi irréprochable dans son offense que le Christ, si bien qu'il y a généralement un élément de vérité déversé contre l'offenseur. Il me semble que nous serions tous beaucoup plus loin si nous retenions une partie de notre sympathie pour les offensés et consacrions nos énergies à leur apprendre comment marcher droit sur le chemin de la vie malgré les pierres d'achoppement aiguës et copieuses qui nous accueillent chaque jour sur notre parcours. Nous apprendrons à vivre sans être offensés quand nous apprendrons à...

Marcher dignement

« Je vous exhorte donc, moi, le prisonnier dans le Seigneur, à marcher d'une manière digne de la vocation dont vous avez été appelés, avec toute humilité et douceur, avec patience, vous supportant les uns les autres avec amour » (Éphésiens 4:1-2). Marcher dignement, comme Paul le décrit ici, c'est marcher dans l'humilité. « L'orgueil va devant la ruine, et l'esprit hautain devant la chute » (Proverbes 16:18). Plus notre vaisseau est chargé d'orgueil, plus nous sommes sujets à être offensés. Plus nous évaluons honnêtement notre valeur, moins nous serons offensés quand on nous ridiculise. Plus d'humilité égale moins d'achoppement. Lorsqu'on nous accuse à tort, cela fait toujours mal. Jésus dit que nous devrions être heureux quand on dira toutes sortes de mal de nous faussement. Bien qu'une telle blessure dégradante puisse suppurer sous notre peau, il existe une condition bien pire : c'est quand les gens disent tout le mal véritablement contre nous. Beaucoup d'accusations portées contre nous contiennent un certain pourcentage de vérité. C'est cette portion que le Seigneur voudrait que nous prenions en compte, plutôt que de dénoncer l'exagération. Ces faussetés lancées contre nous peuvent éveiller notre colère, mais elles ne sont pas la raison pour laquelle nous trébuchons et portons des contusions conséquentes. L'offense naît quand l'opinion d'un autre ne correspond pas à l'exagération que nous faisons de nous-mêmes.

« Rebâtissez, rebâtissez, préparez le chemin, ôtez les pierres d'achoppement du chemin de mon peuple. Car ainsi parle celui qui est très haut et qui habite l'éternité, dont le nom est Saint : j'habite en un lieu élevé et saint, et aussi avec celui qui est contrit et humilié d'esprit, pour ranimer l'esprit des humbles, et pour ranimer le cœur des contrits » (Isaïe 57:14-15). Ici, Isaïe nous instruit d'enlever la pierre d'achoppement mais ne mentionne pas l'offenseur. L'antidote est d'avoir un esprit contrit et humble. Nous ne pourrons jamais exterminer toutes les sources d'offense. Mais si nous y prenons garde correctement, il n'y a aucune offense qui pourra jamais nous détourner de la promesse : « ils monteront avec des ailes comme des aigles; ils courront, et ne se fatigueront point; ils marcheront, et ne se lasseront point » (Isaïe 40:31). C'est principalement notre orgueil qui fait obstacle à notre voyage réussi, plutôt que le mauvais traitement.

Marcher dans l'amour

« Marchez dans l'amour, comme Christ aussi nous a aimés, et s'est livré lui-même pour nous en offrande et en sacrifice à Dieu, en parfum agréable. Mais la fornication, et toute impureté, ou la cupidité, qu'on n'en parle même pas parmi vous, comme il convient à des saints; ni d'impudicité, ni de propos insensés, ni de plaisanteries... » (Éphésiens 5:2-4). Il ne faut pas être savant pour observer les chutes d'un fou égoïste. Cette ambition égoïste d'obtenir des amis, des richesses et de l'aisance garantit qu'un homme finira par tomber à plat nez à un moment ou à un autre. La traînée de péchés mentionnée ici suit tous le chemin vers la satisfaction de soi. Le roi Assuérus conseilla à Haman comment honorer un homme digne. L'esprit narcissique d'Haman pensa aussitôt : « À qui le roi plairait-il de faire davantage honneur que moi ? » (Esther 6:6). Dieu avait d'autres desseins ; ainsi l'homme qui était si offensé par Mardochée fut pendu au gibet de sa propre création. Les âmes égoïstes peuvent avancer mille et une raisons pour lesquelles elles n'atteignent pas leurs aspirations. Quelqu'un les a lésées. Un malheureux enchaînement d'événements les a déraillées. Mais ce n'était ni Mardochée, ni Esther, ni même Assuérus qui firent tomber Haman jusqu'à sa fin amère. Ce fut son propre refus de marcher dans l'amour et de se sacrifier pour les autres qui causa la maligne perte de son âme.

Marcher comme des enfants de lumière

« Marchez comme des enfants de lumière... éprouvant ce qui est agréable au Seigneur. Et n'ayez point de communion avec les œuvres infructueuses des ténèbres, mais plutôt reprenez-les » (Éphésiens 5:8-11). Nos passions innées contiennent la troisième pierre d'offense. Il peut y avoir des choses que nous croyons agréables à notre Seigneur, et qui ne le sont pas. Il y a ceux qui ont « des oreilles qui démangent; et ils détourneront leurs oreilles de la vérité, et se tourneront vers des fables » (2 Timothée 4:3-4). Cela peut affecter ceux qui ont les intentions les plus nobles et des convictions fermes. Le Christ prévint ses disciples qu'ils seraient chassés des synagogues afin que, lorsque cela arriverait, ils « ne soient pas scandalisés » (Jean 16:1-4).

Jean-Baptiste était une lumière ardente et resplendissante et aucun prophète né de femme ne s'est levé plus grand. Il marcha dignement de son appel, baptisa le Seigneur, et réprimanda les pharisiens. Il marcha dans l'amour, et les foules « se plaisaient pour un temps à se réjouir dans sa lumière » (Jean 5:35). Pourtant le jour vint où il envoya ses disciples demander à Jésus : « Es-tu celui qui doit venir ? Ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ? » Jésus répondit : « Allez, rapportez à Jean ce que vous avez vu et entendu; comment les aveugles voient, les boiteux marchent, les lépreux sont purifiés, les sourds entendent, les morts ressuscitent, et la bonne nouvelle est annoncée aux pauvres... et heureux est celui qui ne sera pas scandalisé en moi » (Luc 7:20-23). La réponse du Christ indiquerait que cela ne correspondait apparemment pas entièrement aux aspirations que Jean avait en tête, et il avait du mal à l'accepter. Comme son homologue de l'Ancien Testament, Élie, ces mêmes passions fournissaient le combustible aux flammes du découragement. Il semblait à Jean que le mal avait enveloppé la nation et que Dieu ne faisait pas sa part.

Nous pouvons avoir de bonnes intentions, mais nos propres sentiments passionnés ne sont pas un bon étalon pour éprouver ce qui est agréable au Seigneur. Paltiel fut une âme chère qui tomba dans une telle tromperie. Il avait reçu Michal du roi Saül lui-même. La princesse était sans doute un prix délicat et séduisant. David l'avait manifestement tant estimée qu'il risqua sa vie et doubla la dot avec deux cents prépuces philistins pour obtenir sa main en mariage. Mais Paltiel n'en tint pas compte, savourant sa bonne fortune et profitant de sa compagnie pendant des années. Bien que cette situation ait pu être socialement acceptable à l'époque, nul homme n'a le droit de recevoir ce qu'un autre n'a pas le droit de donner. Le jour vint où « ils l'envoyèrent et la prirent de son mari, même de Paltiel, fils de Laïsh. Et son mari l'accompagna en pleurant derrière elle » (2 Samuel 3:15-16). Nous savons très peu de Paltiel, mais si nous nous excluons de son avalanche émotionnelle, nous devons le déclarer fautif. Nous n'osons pas laisser notre cœur compatissant se tourner vers lui ou vers quiconque est offensé quand on lui demande de se séparer des œuvres des ténèbres. Quand ces sentiments passionnés sont laissés dominer, l'offense est le résultat inévitable. « Car quel est l'avantage, si, lorsque vous frappez pour vos fautes, vous le supportez patiemment ? Mais si, lorsque vous faites bien et que vous souffrez pour cela, vous le supportez patiemment, ceci est agréable devant Dieu » (1 Pierre 2:20) ...

Marcher avec circonspection

« Prenez donc garde à votre marche, que ce ne soit pas comme des insensés, mais comme des sages » (Éphésiens 5:15). « Ne soyez pas enfants dans l'entendement : soyez, au contraire, des hommes dans l'entendement; et dans la malice, soyez des enfants » (1 Corinthiens 14:20). Ici, nous devons reconnaître honnêtement que l'ignorance n'est pas une béatitude. Entrer par la porte étroite peut nécessiter un esprit large. Pas assez large pour permettre le péché, mais assez large pour permettre à Dieu. Circonspect est un mot composé formé des mots latins circum (autour) et spectare (regarder). L'âme unidimensionnelle passera ses jours à être offensée, car elle ne peut voir que son propre point de vue. Il y a plus d'une douzaine de solides Écritures qui nous avertissent contre le fait de faire ce qui est juste à nos propres yeux. Nous devons apprendre à considérer honnêtement les conseils et la sagesse des autres de peur de tomber dans la condamnation.

Dans ses premières années, Michal aimait profondément et ardemment David mais tomba plus tard victime d'un jugement irréfléchi. « Comme l'arche du SEIGNEUR entrait dans la ville de David, Michal, fille de Saül, regarda par une fenêtre, et vit le roi David sautant et dansant devant le SEIGNEUR; et elle le méprisa en son cœur » (2 Samuel 6:16). Tandis que Michal observait la scène depuis sa haute loge, deux choses étaient évidentes. Premièrement, David exprimait une reconnaissance exubérante, et sa joie ne connaissait pas de bornes. C'est le premier amour, « car si nous sommes déraisonnables, c'est pour Dieu » (2 Corinthiens 5:13). Deuxièmement, pendant la danse extatique de David dans son linge de corps, sa discrétion fit défaut, et sa chair devint un peu publique. Cela aurait requis une grande circonspection pour le voir depuis un autre point de vue, et Michal n'en voulut rien savoir. À son entrée pour bénir sa maison, David fut accueilli par un flot de bigoterie refoulée de la part de sa femme offensée et sarcastique. Bien que l'accusation portât une dimension de vérité, s'y attacher comme s'il s'agissait de la suprême réalité était un honteux préjugé. Dieu n'eut aucune sympathie pour cela et « ainsi Michal, la fille de Saül, n'eut point d'enfant jusqu'au jour de sa mort » (2 Samuel 6:23). Beaucoup de bonnes femmes ont jugé leur homme depuis leur coin singulier et asséché le sol du foyer par ce même jugement aride. Cet étroitesse d'esprit ne portera jamais de fruit, si flagrante que soit l'accusation. Il y a une manière correcte d'exprimer une inquiétude, mais le déversement d'un jugement partial transformera promptement une oasis céleste en un désert stérile.

« Un frère offensé est plus difficile à gagner qu'une ville forte: et leurs dissensions sont comme les barres d'une forteresse » (Proverbes 18:19). Il en est ainsi d'une sœur, d'un mari, d'une femme, d'un ami, etc. Bien que les causes d'offense abondent de tous côtés, le Christ désire-t-il que nous soyons offensés ? Salue-t-il notre âme aigre et flétrie ? Peut-être nous donna-t-il cette épreuve afin que nous ayons la racine en nous, « afin que personne ne soit ébranlé par ces afflictions » (1 Thessaloniciens 3:3). Bien que nous ne puissions pas toujours contrôler nos sentiments en des temps de douleur intérieure, nous pouvons chacun choisir une voie rédemptrice et marcher dans l'Esprit. C'est un choix que de diffuser ses griefs, de soigner ses blessures, de se retirer de l'offenseur, et de refuser de croire toutes choses. Comme le frère offensé, ces dissensions servent à verrouiller l'âme comme les barres d'une forteresse. Mais qui détient le pouvoir de la délivrance ?

It was one of those Sunday afternoons in late spring when the sun was finally shining warmly. It was the time of year when little boys seem to have plenty of extra energy. Little Davy was sitting on the road bank with some neighborhood boys who had stopped by. He felt like jumping up and down in anticipation of the upcoming race.

Two older boys, Big David and Paul, showed up with brand-new bicycles. These were not the ordinary bicycles the other boys had. They were beautiful Vista bicycles with gleaming new paint, shiny chrome fenders, and three speeds. These bicycles glided smoothly on the chip-and seal road without a rattle. With new ball bearings, they whizzed along with hardly any effort being applied to the pedals. Even though there did not seem to be much difference between the bicycles, Big David’s was a gleaming chestnut brown, and Paul’s a sparkling metal flake blue.

“Well,” Big David began to brag, “With my longer legs, and freshly sprayed WD40, my bike is sure to be the fastest.”

“No,” challenged Paul, “my shorter legs can pump faster, and Schwinn’s high-test bicycle oil by far outperforms WD40, which really is only for squeaks.”

“A race! A race!” the other boys said, “Why not settle it with a race?”

“Okay,” Big David said, “We’ll have a race and see whose bike is really the fastest.”

“You bet!” Paul agreed. “We’ll start at the top of Billy’s hill and race all the way down to the bottom,” he said, pointing to the road bank where the other boys were sitting.

One, two, three, GO and they were off! Down the hill they came, pedaling for all they were worth.

“Go Paul!” and “Go Big David!” shouted the boys at the bottom of the hill. All the commotion woke up Little Davy’s rat terrier dog, Nellie. Yapping loudly, Nellie zoomed around the silo as fast as her four little legs could carry her. She headed straight for Big David’s bicycle in the front, barking loudly to try to make it stop. Poor Nellie did not realize another bicycle was trying to pass up the first one.

Thump, the passing bicycle hit the dog! Crash, bang, the two bicycles ran into each other!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Two boys flew over the handlebars and landed hard on the road. Those shining bicycles were no longer gleaming. They were lying on a heap, scratched and streaked with tar. Nellie limped back beside the silo and stayed lying there for several hours.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.
