বসন্তের শেষের দিকে একটি রবিবারের সেই দুপুরগুলোর মধ্যেকার একটি ছিল — সূর্য অবশেষে উষ্ণভাবে হাসছিল। সেই সময়টা ছিল যখন ছোট ছেলেরা যেন অতিরিক্ত জ্বালায় ভরে থাকে। ছোট ডেভি রাস্তার ধারে বসে ছিল অন্য কিছু পাড়া-প্রতিবেশী ছেলেদের সঙ্গে যারা রাস্তার পাশে এসে থেমে দাঁড়িয়েছিল। আসন্ন দৌড়ের উত্তেজনায় সে কিরিকির করে লাফ দিতে মন চাইছিল।

দুইজন বড় ছেলেই এসে উপস্থিত হল—বিগ ডেভিড এবং পল—নতুন নতুন সাইকেল নিয়ে। এগুলো অন্য ছেলেদের সাধারণ সাইকেলের মতো ছিল না। এগুলো ছিল সুন্দর ভিস্তা ব্র্যান্ডের সাইকেল, ঝকঝকে নতুন রঙ, উজ্জ্বল ক্রোম ফেন্ডার, এবং তিন গিয়ারের। চিপ-এন্ড-সীল রাস্তার উপর এগুলো নাড়াচাড়া না করে মসৃণভাবে চলছিল। নতুন বল বেয়ারিং থাকায় প্যাডাল চাপতেও তেমন কষ্ট লাগছিল না; সাইকেলগুলো তীব্র গতিতে ছুটে যাচ্ছিল। যদিও বাইসাইকেলগুলোর মধ্যে তেমন বড় পার্থক্য মনে হচ্ছিল না, তবু বিগ ডেভিডেরটি ঝকঝকে চেস্টনাট ব্রাউন, আর পলেরটি ঝকঝকে মেটাল ফ্লেক নীল ছিল।

“আচ্ছা,” বিগ ডেভিড গর্ব করতে করতে বলল, “আমার লম্বা পায়ের কারণে, এবং সদ্য ছিটানো WD40-এর সাথে, আমার সাইকেলই অবশ্যই সবচেয়ে দ্রুততম হবে।”

“না,” পল প্রতিবাদ করল, “আমার ছোট পা দ্রুতই প্যাম্প করতে পারে, এবং শ্রুইন-এর হাই-টেস্ট সাইকেল তেল WD40-কে অনেক পিছনে ফেলে দেয়, যা আসলে কেবল কুঁকড়ে থাকা শব্দের জন্যই উপযুক্ত।”

“একটা রেস! একটা রেস!” অন্য ছেলেরা বলল, “কেন না আমরা দৌড় দিয়ে মাপি?”

“ঠিক আছে,” বিগ ডেভিড বলল, “আমরা একটা রেস করব এবং দেখব কার সাইকেল সত্যিই সবচেয়ে দ্রুত।”

“ঠিক আছে!” পল সম্মত হল। “আমরা বিলি’র পাহাড়ের শীর্ষ থেকে শুরু করে নিচে পর্যন্ত দৌড়াব,” সে বলল, এবং অন্য ছেলেদের বসার রাস্তার ধারের দিকে ইঙ্গিত করল।

এক, দুই, তিন, শুরু — এবং তারা ছুটে পড়ল! পাহাড়ের নিচে তারা নামতে লাগল, প্যাডাল কষছিল তাদের সামর্থ্য অনুযায়ী।

“চল, পল!” এবং “চল, বিগ ডেভিড!” নিচে দাঁড়িয়ে থাকা ছেলেরা চিৎকার করে বলল। সমস্ত হট্টগোল শুনে ছোট ডেভির র‍্যাট টেরিয়ার কুকুর নেলি ঘুম ভাঙিয়ে উঠল। জোরে বজ্রবাদ্য করে ভোঁ-ভোঁ করে নেলি সিলোর চারপাশ দিয়ে তার ছোট চার পা যতটা দ্রুত চলতে পারে ততটাই ছুটল। সে সরাসরি বিগ ডেভিডের সামনে থাকা সাইকেলের দিকে এগোলো, জোরে জোরে ভোঁকার মাধ্যমে সাইকেলটিকে থামাতে চাইছিল। দু:খের বিষয়, নেলি বুঝতে পারেনি যে আরেকটি সাইকেল প্রথমটাকে পেছনে থেকে ঠেলে পার হতে চাচ্ছে।

ঠাম! পেছন থেকে আসা সাইকেলটি কুকুরটিকে ধাক্কা দিল! ধাক্কা, ধোঁ– দুই সাইকেল মুখোমুখি সংঘর্ষে লিপ্ত হল!

“হেই – আয়!” উফ! দুই ছেলে হ্যান্ডেলবারের ওপর থেকে উড়ে পড়ে রাস্তার উপর জোরে আঘাত খাইল। ঝকঝকে থাকা সাইকেলগুলো আর ঝকঝকে নেই। সেগুলো একখানে গড়াগড়ি করে পরে আছে—খোঁজাখুঁজি করে লেগে থাকা তাড় কুঁচকে এবং কালো ফোঁটা-মাঝে দাগ পড়ে গেছে। নেলি লাম্পটিয়ে সিলোর ধারে ফিরে এল এবং কয়েক ঘণ্টা সেখানে গড়িয়ে পড়ে রইল।

অন্যান্য ছেলেরা ধারে দাঁড়িয়ে মুখ খোলা করে দেখে থাকল। তৎক্ষণাৎ তারা ভেঙে পড়া দুই বড় ছেলেদের কাছে ছুটে গেল, যারা তাদের নতুন সাইকেলের পাশে পড়ে আছে। “তোমরা ঠিক আছ?” তারা জিজ্ঞেস করল।

“আমি ভাল থাকব,” পল ধীরে বলল, “কিন্তু আর কোনো রেস নয়। কার সাইকেল সবচেয়ে দ্রুত, তা এখন কারো মাথায় নেই।”

যদিও ছোট ডেভি এখন একজন দাদা, সে সেই বহু দিন আগের রবিবারের দুপুরের সাইকেল দৌড় ভুলে যায়নি—যখন বিগ ডেভিড এবং পল জানতে পারল যে অহংকার ও প্রদর্শনী সাধারণত একটি বিধ্বংসী ফল দেয়।

The message was brief. “Dr. Waldron, would you call Mrs. Jones back about her labs?”

I was puzzled. I didn’t remember ordering any labs for Mrs. Jones. As far as I could remember, she was seeing a specialist and just had surgery for colon cancer. Maybe they had ordered the labs. But if so, they certainly should have followed up on them.

I opened the chart and looked in the lab section. Quickly my eye went to my patient’s kidney function and stopped. Her kidney function had declined a huge amount in the last week.

I called her and then her kidney specialist. Over the next half hour, her situation came into view. Because of her colon surgery, she was losing a lot of fluid, enough that she couldn’t keep up. This, in turn, was making her kidney function a lot worse, along with dropping her potassium level.

To take care of it, she would need IV fluids – once or twice a week – to keep up with the fluids she was losing. Without that, her kidneys would shut down completely.

In a sense, Mrs. Jones was dealing with kidney burnout—a situation where they were putting out more than they were taking in and suffering as a result.

As I was thinking about this, my mind went to the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea is “Dead” because it has such a high level of minerals and salts that very few, other than a few microorganisms, can survive.

The reason for this is that the Dead Sea has no outlet. The Jordan River drains into it, carrying fresh water, and then sits in a basin. Some of the water evaporates, and what remains are the salts and minerals in the water.

Over the thousands of years since the fall of Sodom and Gomorrah, this inland body of water has become one of the saltiest places on earth. It is a body of water that is neither useful for irrigation nor a place where plants and animals can thrive.

Neither situation is healthy, yet this is exactly how most people live their lives, typically gravitating towards one pole or the other. Either they fill their schedule to the maximum, leaving no time for quiet reflection, or they resist any efforts to get them to invest their time and talents and avoid these sorts of activities.

I want to spend a little time thinking about burnout. What causes it, and how we can avoid it?

Everyone has Limits

I Samuel 30 tells the story of David returning to Ziklag. Upon his arrival, he discovered, to his dismay, that the Amalekites had invaded Philistine territory, burned the town, and taken captive all the people who were present.

David and his men had been gone three days and were already tired from their journey to and from Aphek, where King Agag had mustered his forces. Despite this and their anguish at the loss of their family members and material possessions, David consulted God and decided to pursue to the Amalekites out into the desert.

They had only gone as far as the Brook Besor when a third of his men gave up. Scripture tells us they were “too faint” to cross the brook. They were physically and mentally exhausted. Even if they had been able to hold things together for another day, they would be useless in battle.

So it was that David left them behind and continued to pursue the Amalekites, eventually defeating them with the four hundred men who were able to persevere. Here, we come to the interesting part. The men who had won the victory looked down on the men who had been faint. They said those faint-hearted men could have their families back, but all the spoil would be reserved for those who had won the victory.

In response, David said, “Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

David did not wish to penalize those who had tried but did not have the strength to make it through to the final battle.

Perhaps this speaks of the grace we ought to extend to others who don’t have the strength or energy to continue for a season. Maybe it lets us know that we should extend that same grace to ourselves.

What is Burnout?

There are different definitions for burnout, but it all comes down to a state of physical, mental, or emotional exhaustion related to too much stress over an extended period of time. We tend to think of this stress as work-related. There are too many projects going on at once, not enough help, or an employer who has high expectations.

Stress is stress, and it all adds up. Even if work isn’t stressful, if you have a newborn baby at home, a family member with dementia, or many church responsibilities, you can still reach the place where you have little left to give.

It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph, and you push the accelerator a little harder, and nothing happens. In response, you push the gas pedal even harder, and a screeching noise comes from the engine. Suddenly, the dashboard lights up with funny lights, and the car starts to slow down.

The question is, how can we avoid burnout and what should we do if we realize that we are heading towards it?

Understanding Burnout

Burnout leads to both physical and emotional depletion. The problem with burnout is that even if a particular stressor causes it – say, a situation at work or a family health problem – it will affect numerous other relationships.

People dealing with burnout often exhibit symptoms consistent with depression and anxiety. They may become withdrawn, lack motivation to be involved with church and family activities, or get angry quicker than people who are not dealing with burnout.

There is even a suggestion that burnout can lead to the weakening of our immune systems. This could lead to more colds and viral infections.

Identify Early Signs

We need to know ourselves. There are signs that other people can see in our lives and how we relate to others that we don’t necessarily identify as a problem.

People who are on the edge of burnout feel hopeless. They may hide it from their coworkers, but often, their family members realize that something is wrong. You used to have a sunny disposition, and now you are discouraged, not only about the present but also the future.

You might lack motivation and have low energy levels. In a sense, you are going through the motions and just doing enough to get by – both at work and in your home. This is likely related to your feelings of hopelessness.

You may find that you are more irritable than you used to be. Little things bother or aggravate you, and you find yourself smothering angry retorts.

It is important to realize that you are heading down this road for several reasons. First, you are not the only one who suffers when you are burned out. Your family must deal with you and your “grumpiness.” Also, the longer you go without taking care of things, the harder it is to get back to a place of balance.

As a physician, I see people all the time who “didn’t have time” to get something taken care of until they could no longer ignore it. At this point, it will take a major procedure to set things right. It would have been easier to correct if they came in with the first symptom.

Make a Priority List

Everything in our life has a priority level. People who do not prioritize end up feeling scattered as they try to do everything at once. This is a recipe for disaster. To me, it makes sense to divide our tasks into four buckets:

  1. Things that need to be done relatively quickly
  2. Things that need to be done but can wait a bit
  3. Things that we’d like to do, but don’t need to
  4. Things that we should let go of.

Here might be a good place to mention that just because something needs to be done does not mean you need to do it. Sometimes, someone in your home or workplace could help with one of the tasks on your to-do list.

Once we have made our priority list, we need to do something about it. If you simply assign a priority to everything in your life but continue to try to do everything, it won’t help your situation at all.

The point of this exercise is to figure out what things you can eliminate from your schedule, so you have more space to breathe.

Make First Things First

One of the things that happens when we are overwhelmed is that we stop doing self-care. We grab unhealthy food on the go, stop spending time in prayer and devotions, and quit exercising.

Doing these things takes time, and that is exactly what we think we don’t have when we are living on the margins of our energy. Self-care is extremely important but often gets assigned a priority of zero and is seldom included in a day’s activity.

As we begin to replenish our spiritual nourishment, we must also make sure we take care of our physical health.

Take Time Apart

After feeding the multitudes, Mark 6:46 tells of Jesus, “And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.” Even Jesus had times when He needed to be alone without distractions.

It is easy to focus on the prayer aspect of this passage, and that is important, but let's focus on the solitary aspect of this experience. Jesus even left His closest followers behind during this time of seeking God’s face.

There are times when we need to escape from the pressure of human interactions and find a peaceful place where we can be alone.

Put Down Technology

Part of making rest time truly restful is to eliminate sources of distraction. Phones and electronic tablets are exactly the types of things that can keep our minds from achieving the peace (shalom) that we both desire and need.

Digital burnout is a new term that is being used to describe people who feel apathetic and exhausted from spending hours each day staring at screens. Many workers spend seven or eight hours a day looking at computer screens and then get even more screen time after work.

The funny thing is that the most productive workers are often people who use old-fashioned things like paper calendars and leave phones out of meetings. As wonderful as phones are, they are also immensely distracting for most of us.

So often, we have time away that is simply not restful. The reason is that we continue to receive texts and emails and can still access social media. If you are not someone who can put his phone away and ignore it (it takes a lot of willpower to do this), then leave your phone in another room and create some distance. This will seem stressful, but we can focus on recharging ourselves by creating a screen-free zone.

Build Breaks into Your Day

There is a certain amount of work that must be done each day, and it often feels like too much for the allotted 24 hours. There is certainly no time to stop, stretch, and take a five-minute walk, or at least that's what we tell ourselves.

In reality, if you take a five-minute break every few hours to do something non-work related, you will come back refreshed and more ready to deal with the problems of the day.

Do something healthy during this time. Take a short walk or eat an apple. Chowing down a bag of potato chips or eating a couple candy bars is not likely to produce the desired results.

The problem is often with our own expectations. People who struggle with burnout often have extremely high personal standards and get frustrated when they not measure up to that standard.

Be Intentional about Rest

One of the messages of the Old Testament was the importance of the Sabbath. I have heard many people argue that in the New Testament period, we no longer need to practice the Sabbath. Didn’t Paul say that one day was like the other? Didn’t Jesus defend His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath?

Regardless of what you believe about the importance of keeping the Sabbath, it is still important that we take time to rest. This is the real message that Jesus was conveying when He said that the “Sabbath was created for man, not man for the Sabbath” (Mark 2:27).

Rest is not simply sleeping till 10 am and then doing nothing. Rest is actively making decisions that will help us recharge our depleted batteries. Go out for breakfast with a friend, take a hike, or take a good book and go somewhere without cell service and focus on something other than situations that are depleting you.

Jesus understood the human need for rest, this is why He told His disciples “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while” (Mark 6:31). This time of rest would give them energy for their next time of ministry.

Don’t Buy into Myths

People tell themselves all sorts of lies that can lead to pushing themselves too hard. I’ll list a few of them and some thoughts about each one.

“I’m the only one who can do this task.” This feels true. The other people in our home or workplace are not helping us the way we wish that they would. Sometimes, it simply feels easier to do the task ourselves rather than spend time teaching someone else how to do it. We need to remember that if we died, the people around us would figure out how to get things done. We can assign them some of the tasks today before we die.

“If I just get this job done today, tomorrow will be easier.” I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but each day has 24 hours, and somehow, they always get filled up. I have given up the idea that there is a time in my life coming up soon that will have nothing on the schedule. If a rest comes, it will come because I have made an effort to clear my schedule, not because by some random occurrence, one day, I happen to not have a single task in it.

“God will never give me more than I can handle.” God has promised many things. He has promised that when there is a temptation, He will give us an opportunity to escape it (I Corinthians 10:13). He has also promised that He will never leave us or forsake us (Hebrews 13:5). I do not read anywhere in Scripture that God will keep us from overfilling our lives. He has simply promised that He will give us opportunity to take a different path and will walk beside us on our way.

So often the heavy load we carry is because other people, or even we, ourselves, have put too many things on our task list. Suppose I choose to put too many patients on my schedule and I am feeling exhausted. In that case, it is time for me to take responsibility for what I have done, rather than claiming a mythical promise that God will keep me from overwhelming myself.

“These are all good things that I am doing.” Doctors face this a lot. We want to squeeze one more patient into the schedule and stay just a little later to answer another message because we feel responsible. We hate to think that someone might need to go to the Emergency Department because we did not take care of them when they needed help.

Just because the things in your schedule are “good things” that benefit other people and are building the kingdom, does not mean that you don’t need to cut back in one area or another. If you are feeling emotionally depleted, it is probably time to remove a few items from your to-do list.

Conclusion

There are other things that could be mentioned. Getting support from someone else, meditating on Scripture, and even taking a vacation are all things that can help.

When I read about some of the famous preachers of the past, I see in some of their lives a roller coaster. They pushed themselves to the max, got involved in large numbers of projects, and then had an emotional breakdown. They would take some time off and, a month or two later, launch back into the same activities. This cycle continued for their whole ministry.

Jesus tells us that His yoke is easy, and His burden is light (Matt, 11:28-30). If we are at the point of exhaustion, we need to consider whether we have Jesus’ yoke or if we are laboring under the burden of our own creation.

Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.

Die boodskap was kort. “Dr. Waldron, sal u vir mev. Jones terugbel oor haar laboratoriumuitslae?”

Ek was verbaas. Ek kon nie onthou dat ek enige laboratoriumtoetse vir mev. Jones bestel het nie. Sover ek kon onthou, het sy by ’n spesialis gesien en net ’n operasie vir dikdermkanker gehad. Miskien het hulle die toetse bestel. Maar as dit so is, moes hulle beslis daarvolgens opgevolg het.

Ek het die dossier oopgemaak en in die laboratoriumafdeling gekyk. My oog het vinnig na my pasiënt se nierfunksie gegaan en opgehou. Haar nierfunksie het in die laaste week baie agteruitgegaan.

Ek het haar toe geskakel en daarna haar nierpesialis. Oor die volgende halfuur het haar situasie duidelik geword. Vanweë haar dikdermoperasie het sy baie vloeistof verloor, genoeg dat sy nie kon byhou nie. Dit het op sy beurt haar nierfunksie baie erger gemaak en ook haar kaliumvlakke laat daal.

Om dit reg te maak, sou sy intraveneuse vloeistowwe nodig hê – een of twee keer per week – om by te hou met die vloeistowwe wat sy verloor. Sonder dit sou haar niere heeltemal volstaan en stop.

In ’n sin het mev. Jones te doen gehad met nieruitbranding—’n situasie waar hulle meer uitset as inset kry en daaronder ly.

Terwyl ek hieroor nadink, het my gedagtes na die Doodsee gegaan. Die Doodsee is “dood” omdat dit so ’n hoë vlak van minerale en soute het dat baie min lewende dinge, anders as ’n paar mikroörganismes, daar kan oorleef.

Die rede hiervoor is dat die Doodsee geen uitloop het nie. Die Jordaanrivier mond daarin uit en bring vars water, en sit dan in ’n bekken. Sommige van die water verdamp, en wat oorbly is die soute en minerale in die water.

Oor die duisende jare sedert die val van Sodom en Gomorra het hierdie binnelandse watersentrum een van die soutste plekke op aarde geword. Dit is ’n watersentrum wat nie nuttig is vir besproeiing of ’n plek waar plante en diere kan floreer nie.

Nóg situasie is gesond, tog is dit presies hoe die meeste mense hul lewens leef en tipies na een pool of die ander toe graviteer. Of vul hulle hul skedule tot die maksimum, sonder tyd vir stille besinning, of hulle weier enige pogings om hulle te laat belê in hul tyd en talente en vermy daardie soort dinge.

Ek wil ’n bietjie tyd neem om oor uitbranding te dink. Wat veroorsaak dit, en hoe kan ons dit vermy?

Almal het perke

I Samuel 30 vertel die verhaal van Dawid wat terugkeer na Sikklag. By sy aankoms het hy, tot sy ontsteltenis, gevind dat die Amalekiete in Filistyese gebied ingedring het, die dorp verbrand het en al die mense wat daar was gevange geneem het.

Dawid en sy manne was drie dae weg en was reeds moeg van hul reis heen en terug na Afek, waar koning Agag sy magte versamel het. Ondanks dit en hul hartseer oor die verlies van hul familielede en materiële besittings, het Dawid God geraadpleeg en besluit om die Amalekiete uit die woestyn agterna te jaag.

Hulle het slegs tot by die Besor‑beek gegaan toe ’n derde van sy manne opgegee het. Skrif sê hulle was “te swak” om die beek oor te steek. Hulle was fisies en geestelik uitgeput. Selfs as hulle dit vir nog ’n dag sou kon volhou, sou hulle nutteloos in die geveg wees.

So het Dawid hulle agtergelaat en voortgegaan om die Amalekiete te agtervolg en het hulle uiteindelik met die vier honderd manne wat kon volhard, verslaan. Hier kom ons by die interessante deel. Die manne wat die oorwinning behaal het, het neergebly op die manne wat swak geword het. Hulle het gesê daardie vreeshartige manne kon hul families terug hê, maar al die buit sou gereserveer word vir diegene wat die oorwinning behaal het.

In reaksie het Dawid gesê, “Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

Dawid wou nie diegene wat probeer het, maar nie die krag gehad het om by die finale geveg uit te kom nie, straf nie.

Perhaps this speaks of the grace we ought to extend to others who don’t have the strength or energy to continue for a season. Maybe it lets us know that we should extend that same grace to ourselves.

Wat is uitbranding?

Daar is verskillende definisies vir uitbranding, maar dit kom neer op ’n toestand van fisiese, geestelike of emosionele uitputting wat verband hou met te veel spanning oor ’n verlengde tyd. Ons neig om te dink dat hierdie spanning werkverwant is. Daar is te veel projekte op een slag, nie genoeg hulp nie, of ’n werkgewer wat hoë verwagtinge het.

Spanning is spanning, en dit tel alles op. Selfs as die werk nie stresvol is nie, as jy ’n pasgebore baba by die huis het, ’n familielid met demensie, of baie kerkverpligtinge, kan jy steeds die punt bereik waar jy min oor het om te gee.

Dit is asof jy in ’n voertuig is wat 90 myl per uur ry, en jy trap die versnellingspedaal ’n bietjie harder, maar niks gebeur nie. In reaksie druk jy die petrolpedaal nog harder, en ’n skril geluid kom uit die enjin. Skielik lig die paneelbord op met snaakse ligte, en die motor begin stadig raak.

Die vraag is: hoe kan ons uitbranding vermy en wat moet ons doen as ons besef dat ons daarheen op pad is?

Verstaan uitbranding

Uitbranding lei tot beide fisiese en emosionele uitputting. Die probleem met uitbranding is dat selfs as ’n bepaalde stresor dit veroorsaak – sê ’n situasie by die werk of ’n gesinsgesondheidsprobleem – dit talle ander verhoudings sal beïnvloed.

Mense wat met uitbranding sukkel, toon dikwels simptome wat ooreenstem met depressie en angs. Hulle kan teruggetrokke raak, gebrek aan motivering hê om by kerk‑ en gesinsaktiwiteite betrokke te raak, of vinniger kwaad raak as mense wat nie met uitbranding te doen het nie.

Daar is selfs ’n voorstel dat uitbranding tot die verswakking van ons immuunstelsels kan lei. Dit kan tot meer verkoues en virusinfeksies lei.

Identifiseer vroeë tekens

Ons moet onsself ken. Daar is tekens wat ander mense in ons lewens en in hoe ons met ander omgaan kan sien wat ons nie noodwendig as ’n probleem identifiseer nie.

Mense wat op die rand van uitbranding is, voel hopeloos. Hulle mag dit vir hul kollegas wegsteek, maar dikwels besef hul familielede dat iets verkeerd is. Jy het vroeër ’n sonnige geaardheid gehad, en nou is jy ontmoedig, nie net oor die hede nie maar ook oor die toekoms.

Jy mag ’n gebrek aan motivering hê en lae energievlakke ervaar. In ’n sin gaan jy deur die bewegings en doen net genoeg om deur te kom – beide by die werk en by die huis. Dit hou waarskynlik verband met jou gevoelens van hopeloosheid.

Jy mag vind dat jy meer prikkelbaar is as voorheen. Klein dinge pla of erger jou, en jy vind jouself terughou van woedende terugslae.

Dit is belangrik om te besef dat jy hierdie pad afgaan om verskeie redes. Eerstens is jy nie die enigste een wat ly wanneer jy uitgebrand is nie. Jou gesin moet met jou en jou “mierigheid” besig wees. Ook, hoe langer jy aanhou sonder om dinge reg te maak, hoe moeiliker is dit om terug te kom na ’n plek van balans.

As dokter sien ek voortdurend mense wat “nie tyd gehad het” om iets reg te maak totdat hulle dit nie meer kon ignoreer nie. Op daardie punt sal ’n groot prosedure nodig wees om dinge reg te stel. Dit sou makliker gewees het om dit reg te stel as hulle met die eerste simptoom gekom het.

Maak ’n prioriteitslys

Alles in ons lewe het ’n prioriteitsvlak. Mense wat nie prioritiseer nie, eindig gevoel gekruimel terwyl hulle probeer om alles op ’n slag te doen. Dit is ’n resep vir rampspoed. Vir my maak dit sin om ons take in vier emmers te verdeel:

  1. Dinge wat redelik vinnig gedoen moet word
  2. Dinge wat gedoen moet word maar ’n bietjie kan wag
  3. Dinge wat ons graag wil doen, maar nie hoef te doen nie
  4. Dinge wat ons moet laat gaan.

Hier kan dit ’n goeie plek wees om te noem dat net omdat iets gedoen moet word, beteken nie jy moet dit doen nie. Soms kan iemand in jou huis of werkplek help met een van die items op jou to‑do lys.

Sodra ons ons prioriteitslys gemaak het, moet ons iets daaraan doen. As jy eenvoudig ’n prioriteit aan alles in jou lewe toeskryf maar voortgaan om te probeer om alles te doen, sal dit glad nie jou situasie help nie.

Die punt van hierdie oefening is om uit te werk watter dinge jy van jou skedule kan verwyder, sodat jy meer ruimte het om asem te haal.

Maak die belangrikste dinge eerste

Een van die dinge wat gebeur wanneer ons oorlaai is dat ons ophou met selfversorging. Ons gryp ongesonde kos terwyl ons onderweg is, stop om tyd in gebed en devosies deur te bring, en hou op om te oefen.

Om hierdie dinge te doen neem tyd, en dit is presies wat ons dink ons nie het nie wanneer ons op die rand van ons energie leef. Selfversorging is uiters belangrik maar word dikwels ’n prioriteit van nul gegee en selde in ’n dag se aktiwiteit ingesluit.

Soos ons begin om ons geestelike voeding weer aan te vul, moet ons ook seker maak dat ons vir ons fisiese gesondheid sorg.

Neem tyd alleen

Na die voeding van die skare vertel Markus 6:46 dat Jesus, “And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.” Selfs Jesus het tye gehad wanneer Hy alleen sonder afleidings moes wees.

Dit is maklik om op die gebedaspek van hierdie gedeelte te fokus, en dit is belangrik, maar kom ons fokus op die eensame aspek van hierdie ervaring. Jesus het selfs Sy naaste volgelinge agtergelaat tydens hierdie tyd van die soeke na God se aangesig.

Daar is tye wanneer ons van die druk van menslike interaksies moet ontvlug en ’n vreedsame plek vind waar ons alleen kan wees.

Sit tegnologie neer

’n Deel van om rusregtig ontspannend te maak, is om bronne van afleiding uit te skakel. Telefone en elektroniese tablette is presies die soort dinge wat ons gedagtes kan verhinder om die vrede (shalom) te bereik wat ons begeer en nodig het.

Digitale uitbranding is ’n nuwe term wat gebruik word om mense te beskryf wat apaties en uitgeput voel van ure wat hulle elke dag na skerms staar. Baie werkers spandeer sewe of agt uur per dag voor rekenaarskerms en kry dan nog meer skermtyd ná werk.

Die snaakse ding is dat die mees produktiewe werkers dikwels mense is wat ou‑style dinge soos papierkalenders gebruik en telefone uit vergaderings hou. Hoe wonderlik telefone ook al is, hulle is vir die meeste van ons ook geweldig afleidend.

So dikwels het ons afwesighede wat eenvoudig nie rusgewend is nie. Die rede is dat ons steeds teksboodskappe en e‑posse ontvang en steeds toegang tot sosiale media het. As jy nie iemand is wat sy telefoon kan wegsit en ignoreer nie (dit verg baie selfbeheer om dit te doen), sit jou telefoon dan in ’n ander kamer en skep afstand. Dit sal stresvol lyk, maar ons kan daarop fokus om onsself op te laai deur ’n skermvrye gebied te skep.

Bou pouses in jou dag in

Daar is ’n sekere hoeveelheid werk wat elke dag gedoen moet word, en dit voel dikwels te veel vir die toegekende 24 uur. Daar is beslis geen tyd om te stop, strek en ’n vyf‑minute loopie te neem nie, of so sê ons vir onsself.

In werklikheid, as jy elke paar uur ’n vyf‑minute pouse neem om iets nie‑werkverwants te doen, sal jy verfris terugkom en meer gereed wees om die probleme van die dag te hanteer.

Doen iets gesond gedurende hierdie tyd. Neem ’n kort stap of eet ’n appel. Om ’n sak chips te vreet of ’n paar sjokoladebalkies in te sluk, sal waarskynlik nie die verlangde resultate lewer nie.

Die probleem lê dikwels by ons eie verwagtinge. Mense wat met uitbranding sukkel, het dikwels uiters hoë persoonlike standaarde en raak gefrustreerd wanneer hulle nie aan daardie standaard voldoen nie.

Wees doelgerig oor rus

Een van die boodskappe van die Ou Testament was die belangrikheid van die Sabbat. Ek het baie mense gehoor argumenteer dat in die Nuwe Testamentlike tydperk ons nie meer die Sabbat hoef te beoefen nie. Het Paulus nie gesê dat een dag soos die ander is nie? Het Jesus nie Sy dissipels verdedig vir die pluk van koring op die Sabbat nie?

Ongeag wat jy glo oor die belangrikheid om die Sabbat te hou, is dit steeds belangrik dat ons tyd neem om te rus. Dit is die werklike boodskap wat Jesus oorgedra het toe Hy gesê het dat die “Sabbat geskape is vir die mens, nie die mens vir die Sabbat nie” (Markus 2:27).

Rus beteken nie bloot slaap tot 10:00 vm en dan niks doen nie. Rus is aktief besluite neem wat ons sal help om ons uitgeputte batterye weer op te laai. Gaan ontbyt toe met ’n vriend, doen ’n staptog, of neem ’n goeie boek en gaan na ’n plek sonder selfoondekking en fokus op iets anders as situasies wat jou uitput.

Jesus het die menslike behoefte aan rus verstaan; dit is hoekom Hy vir Sy dissipels gesê het: “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while” (Markus 6:31). Hierdie tyd van rus sou hulle energie gee vir hulle volgende bedieningstyd.

Glo nie mites nie

Mense vertel hulself allerhande leuens wat daartoe kan lei dat hulle te hard druk. Ek gaan ’n paar hiervan noem en ’n paar gedagtes oor elkeen.

“Ek is die enigste een wat hierdie taak kan doen.” Dit voel waar. Ander mense in ons huis of werkplek help nie op die manier wat ons sou wou hê hulle moet nie. Soms is dit eenvoudig makliker om die taak self te doen as om tyd te spandeer om iemand anders te leer hoe om dit te doen. Ons moet onthou dat as ons sou sterf, die mense om ons sou uitwerk hoe om dinge gedoen te kry. Ons kan hulle vandag al sommige van die take toewys voordat ons sterf.

“As ek net hierdie taak vandag klaarmaak, sal môre makliker wees.” Ek haat om die draer van slegte nuus te wees, maar elke dag het 24 uur, en op een of ander manier word hulle altyd volgepak. Ek het opgehou met die idee dat daar ’n tyd in my lewe binnekort sal kom wat niks op die skedule het nie. As ’n rus kom, sal dit kom omdat ek moeite gedoen het om my skedule skoon te maak, nie omdat deur ’n toevallige omstandigheid een dag geen taak inhou nie.

“God sal my nooit meer gee as wat ek kan hanteer nie.” God het baie dinge belowe. Hy het belowe dat wanneer daar ’n versoeking is, Hy vir ons ’n uitweg sal gee (I Korintiërs 10:13). Hy het ook belowe dat Hy ons nooit sal verlaat of in die steek sal laat nie (Hebreërs 13:5). Ek lees nêrens in die Skrif dat God ons sal voorkom om ons lewens te oorvul nie. Hy het eenvoudig belowe dat Hy vir ons ’n geleentheid sal gee om ’n ander pad te neem en langs ons sal loop op ons pad.

So dikwels is die swaar las wat ons dra omdat ander mense, of selfs ons self, te veel dinge op ons take‑lys gelaai het. Stel ek kies om te veel pasiënte op my skedule te sit en ek voel uitgeput, dan is dit tyd vir my om verantwoordelikheid te neem vir wat ek gedoen het, eerder as om ’n mitiese belofte te maak dat God my sal keer om myself te oorweldig.

“Dit is alles goeie dinge wat ek doen.” Dokters ervaar dit baie. Ons wil nog een pasiënt inpas en net ’n bietjie later bly om nog ’n boodskap te beantwoord omdat ons ons verantwoordelik voel. Ons haat om te dink dat iemand na die Spoedafdeling moet gaan omdat ons nie vir hulle gesorg het toe hulle hulp nodig gehad het nie.

Net omdat die dinge op jou skedule “goeie dinge” is wat ander mense bevoordeel en die koninkryk bou, beteken dit nie dat jy nie op een of ander gebied moet terugskaal nie. As jy emosioneel uitgeput voel, is dit waarskynlik tyd om ’n paar items van jou to‑do lys te verwyder.

Gevolgtrekking

Daar is ander dinge wat genoem kan word. Ondersteuning van iemand anders kry, mediteer oor Skrifgedeeltes, en selfs vakansie neem is alles dinge wat kan help.

Wanneer ek lees oor van die beroemde predikers van die verlede, sien ek in sommige van hul lewens ’n rollercoaster. Hulle het hulself tot die maksimum gedruk, by groot getalle projekte betrokke geraak, en toe ’n emosionele ineenstorting gehad. Hulle sou tyd neem en, ’n maand of twee later, weer in dieselfde aktiwiteite begin. Hierdie siklus het gedurende hul hele bediening voortgeduur.

Jesus sê dat Sy juk sag is en Sy las lig (Matt. 11:28-30). As ons by die punt van uitputting is, moet ons oorweeg of ons Jesus se juk het of onder die las van ons eie skepping werk.

Jesus ken ons perke. Hy wil hê ons moet balans hê, sodat ons nie net krag het vir vandag nie maar ook vir môre, volgende week en volgende jaar – totdat Hy weer kom.

It was one of those Sunday afternoons in late spring when the sun was finally shining warmly. It was the time of year when little boys seem to have plenty of extra energy. Little Davy was sitting on the road bank with some neighborhood boys who had stopped by. He felt like jumping up and down in anticipation of the upcoming race.

Two older boys, Big David and Paul, showed up with brand-new bicycles. These were not the ordinary bicycles the other boys had. They were beautiful Vista bicycles with gleaming new paint, shiny chrome fenders, and three speeds. These bicycles glided smoothly on the chip-and seal road without a rattle. With new ball bearings, they whizzed along with hardly any effort being applied to the pedals. Even though there did not seem to be much difference between the bicycles, Big David’s was a gleaming chestnut brown, and Paul’s a sparkling metal flake blue.

“Well,” Big David began to brag, “With my longer legs, and freshly sprayed WD40, my bike is sure to be the fastest.”

“No,” challenged Paul, “my shorter legs can pump faster, and Schwinn’s high-test bicycle oil by far outperforms WD40, which really is only for squeaks.”

“A race! A race!” the other boys said, “Why not settle it with a race?”

“Okay,” Big David said, “We’ll have a race and see whose bike is really the fastest.”

“You bet!” Paul agreed. “We’ll start at the top of Billy’s hill and race all the way down to the bottom,” he said, pointing to the road bank where the other boys were sitting.

One, two, three, GO and they were off! Down the hill they came, pedaling for all they were worth.

“Go Paul!” and “Go Big David!” shouted the boys at the bottom of the hill. All the commotion woke up Little Davy’s rat terrier dog, Nellie. Yapping loudly, Nellie zoomed around the silo as fast as her four little legs could carry her. She headed straight for Big David’s bicycle in the front, barking loudly to try to make it stop. Poor Nellie did not realize another bicycle was trying to pass up the first one.

Thump, the passing bicycle hit the dog! Crash, bang, the two bicycles ran into each other!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Two boys flew over the handlebars and landed hard on the road. Those shining bicycles were no longer gleaming. They were lying on a heap, scratched and streaked with tar. Nellie limped back beside the silo and stayed lying there for several hours.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.

Ilikuwa moja ya ile jioni za Jumapili mwishoni mwa spring wakati jua hatimaye lilikuwa likangaza kwa joto. Ilikuwa msimu ambapo wavulana wadogo wanaonekana kuwa na nishati ya ziada. Wavulana wawili wakubwa, David Mzito na Paul, walikuja na baiskeli mpya kabisa. Hizi hazikuwa baiskeli za kawaida walizokuwa nazo wavulana wengine. Zilikuwa baiskeli za Vista zenye rangi mpya inayong'aa, fenderi za chrome zinang'aa, na gia tatu. Baiskeli hizi zilitembea kwa utulivu barabarani bila kutetemeka. Kwa mabeji mapya ya ngoma, zilienda kwa kasi bila kuhitaji juhudi nyingi kupiga mguu kwenye pedal. Ingawa haikuonekana kuwa na tofauti kubwa kati ya baiskeli hizo, baiskeli ya David Mzito ilikuwa ya rangi ya kahawia yenye mwanga, na ya Paul ilikuwa ya bluu yenye chembe za chuma zinazoangaza.

“Naam,” David Mzito alianza kujisifu, “kwa miguu yangu mirefu, na WD40 iliyotiwa tena, baiskeli yangu hakika itakuwa ya kasi zaidi.”

“Hapana,” Paul alipingana, “miguu yangu mifupi inaweza kupiga kwa kasi zaidi, na mafuta ya baiskeli ya Schwinn yanafanya kazi bora kuliko WD40, ambayo kwa kweli ni kwa midundo tu.”

“Mbio! Mbio!” wavulana wengine walisema, “Kwanini tusitakie suluhisho kwa mbio?”

“Sawa,” David Mzito alisema, “Tutafanya mbio na kuona baiskeli ya nani ndiyo kweli ya kasi zaidi.”

“Ukipenda!” Paul alikubali. “Tutaanza kilele cha kilima cha Billy na kukimbia mpaka chini kabisa,” alisema, akielekeza kwa kando ya barabara ambapo wavulana wengine walikuwa wamekaa.

Mmoja, mbili, tatu, ANZA na walianza! Walishuka mlima wanapiga pedali kwa nguvu zao zote.

“Endelea Paul!” na “Endelea David Mzito!” wavulana walilia chini ya kilima. Huo wote msongamano ulimwamsha mbwa wa Davy mdogo, terrier yake Nellie. Akitikisa kwa mbwa, Nellie alizunguka silo kwa kasi kama miguu yake minne ilivyoweza kumchukua. Alielekea moja kwa moja kwenye baiskeli ya mbele ya David Mzito, akitukia kwa nguvu kujaribu kuifanya isimame. Nellie maskini hakuelewa kuwa baiskeli nyingine ilikuwa inajaribu kumpita ile ya kwanza.

Thump, baiskeli iliyompita ilimpiga mbwa! Crash, bang, baiskeli mbili zilikumbana!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Wavulana wawili waliruka juu ya bega la baiskeli na kuanguka kwa nguvu kwenye barabara. Hizo baiskeli zilizoang'aa hazkukuwepo tena. Ziliwekwa kwenye rundo, zimechafuka na kukunja madoa ya tar. Nellie alirudi akiwekeka karibu na silo na akaendelea kulala pale kwa masaa kadhaa.

Wavulana wengine walisimama kando na kinywa wazi. Haraka, walikimbia kwa wavulana wakubwa wawili waliokuwa wamelala karibu na baiskeli zao mpya. “Mko sawa?” waliuliza.

“Nitagona,” Paul alisema taratibu, “lakini hakuna mbio tena. Nani anayejali hata baiskeli ya nani ni ya kasi zaidi.”

Ingawa Davy mdogo sasa ni babu, hajatoweka kumbukumbu za mbio za baiskeli siku ile ya Jumapili zamani, wakati David Mzito na Paul waligundua kuwa kujisifu na kuonyesha kwa kiburi kawaida huishia kwa ajali.

It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

זה היה ה"עולם המושלם" כפי שאדם וחוה נהנו ממנו מדי יום עם בוראם. הגן היפה, שעוצב, נברא וניטע בידיו של האל עצמו, היה מושלם בכל היבט. כולנו יודעים שלא נשאר כך לזמן רב. בגלל זכות הבחירה שנתן האל לכל האנושות, שניהם מוקדם הופנו לבחירה רעה. חוה, אף שהולמה על ידי השטן בדמות הנחש, האמינה לשקר ובחרה לעבור על ציווי האל, ועשתה את הדבר היחיד שאלוהים בקשה ממנה באהבה שלא לעשותו. אך כאשר הביאה את הפרי לאדם, הוא לא הוטעה. הוא ידע שזה היה רע. האל לא הופתע אך, על אף זאת, התאכזב מאוד. בראשית ג', אנו קוראים את הסיפור העצוב של גירוש האנושות מהגן, נחסמה מפני עץ החיים, ונקראה הקללה על חטאם של אדם וחוה. זה נראה כה חשוך וחסר תקווה. אף שהיה רק אדם אחד שחטא, הקללה עברה לכל העולם הנברא, כולל האדמה, הצמחים והחיות. חשבו איתי על מה שצמח יחד עם קללה אדירה זו.

  1. מחלה
  2. צער וכאב
  3. שחיקה והרס
  4. שליטת צמחים מסוימים כמו קוצים ודרדרים
  5. מוות
  6. התפרקות וריקבון

נתייחס אליהם היום כששת ה"ד" של הקללה.

מחלה

ימיו הטהורים של העולם, של בריאות נצחית ומושלמת, חלפו. המחלה נכנסה לתמונה כחלק מקללת החטא. בני האדם, הציפורים, החיות והצמחים כולם התחילו לחוות את השפעות המחלה והחולי. אך האל היה נאמן בכך שנתן הוראות שעזרו לאדם לדעת כיצד להימנע מהרבה מחלות שניתן למנוע על ידי ניקיון וצייתנות פשוטה. לדוגמה, צו האל לכבד את כוונתו המקורית בנישואין, לשמור על טהרה, להימנע ממחלות פוטנציאליות רבות, ועוד. הוא גם התעניין במצבנו הרוחני. האל מעולם לא תכנן שהאנושות תישא אשמה. הוא רוצה שנהיה ונשמור על מצפון נקי כי הוא יודע שמצפון אשם יכול להחלים אותך!

חלק מהמחלות הללו יהיו בלתי נמנעות, אך רבות מהן יכולות להימנע על ידי בניית חיסון. האל גם היה נאמן בעיצוב בני האדם, הצמחים והחיות עם מיקרוביום מתחדש (מיליארדי בקטריות מועילות) ומערכת חיסון מערכתית, המסייעת לנו להילחם במחלות. מדהים כיצד כל צמח נראה שיש לו תכונות תזונתיות או מרפאות מועילות. כמה נאמן היוצר!

צער וכאב

אני משער שלא היה סיבה אמיתית לכאב בגן עדן, אך חווינו כאב מאז יום הגירוש שלהם. כאב אכן חלק מחיי רבים מאיתנו. ישנם סוגים רבים של כאב. אבל, צער, אבל ודחייה הם כאבים רגשיים שבאים עם הקללה. כאבים פיזיים כגון כאבים, מיגרנות, שרירים כואבים, קרעים ברצועות, גידים נגועים, מפרקים שחוקים ודם נשבר הם חלק מהכאבים הפיזיים שניתקל בהם לפעמים לפני נשימתנו האחרונה. שוב, האל היה נאמן בעזרה לבני האדם להבין מה לעשות כדי להקל על כמה מכאבי החיים והצער. מאז ימי קדם, צמחים, עשבים ותרופות אחרות עזרו לאנשים להתמודד עם כאב וצער. עד היום יש לנו צמחים רבים שימושיים שעוזרים לנו בכאב.

אחד הדברים היפים ביותר שניתן לחוות על פני אדמה הוא לידת תינוק. ועדיין, הלידה בדרך כלל מלווה בכאב רב. אף שאיננו יכולים לבטל כאב מבטיח זה, האל היה נאמן בכך שסיפק וגילה לנו שימוש בעשבים רבים לפני, במהלך ואחרי הלידה כדי להקל על הכאב ולהאיץ את ההתאוששות. הוא לא היה חייב לעשות זאת עבורנו. האנושות באמת לא ראויה לרחמים. איזה יוצר נאמן!

שחיקה והרס

אין צורך לחקור היסטוריה רבות כדי לראות את עקרון זה פועל. רוח, גשם ושמש כולם משפיעים ומשחיתים דברים רבים. בין אם נדון על גדות נחלים מאובקות, סלעים שחוקו ונסלחו בנהר, או על עץ שהואשף על ידי הרוח — אלו כולם אלמנטים טבעיים של הרס. אך הוסף לזה מה שהאדם עשה לצמחים, לחיות, לאדמה ולזה את זה את. בין אם השפעות ההרס ההרסניות במלחמות האיומות או פרקטיקות אנוכיות וחמדניות בזמן שלום, האדם הוא יצור הרסני ביותר. האל נתן לאנושות שליטה על כל הבריאה. אך לעתים קרובות מדי, אנו מפרשים זאת בטעות כהחזקת העולם הזה בבעלותנו ויכולת לעשות בו כרצוננו. מי שהכריז "הארץ היא ליהוה" לא מסכים עם הרעיון שבני אדם הם דבר אחר משומרי הבית של יצירת האל. אכן רע לעשות בעבודה בהם של כיבוד הנברא או כל דבר בה. אך כשם זה רע להיות לא תודתי ואדיש לבריאת בוראנו! עם זאת, האל תכנן באמונה את עולמו עם יכולות התחדשות בתוך הקללה הזו. יברך בוראנו החנון!

שליטת קוצים ודרדרים

כל מי שאי פעם גנן גילה במהרה את המציאות של המאבק בעשבים שוטים. בהגינות, כל צמח שצומח במקום שאינו רצוי הוא "עשב". רבים מהעשבים יכולים להיות צמחים מועילים מאוד אם רק נדע מה להשתמש בהם. חלק מהצמחים שאנו קוראים להם עשבים הם למעשה מזינים ובריאים ברגע שנבין אילו מהם אכילים ואיך להכינם. היום, נרצה לחשוב על קוצים ודרדרים. עלינו להניח שנוצרו בימי היצירה הראשונים, לא לאחר שהקללה הוכרזה. נראה כי יכולתם לעלות על התבואה המועילה גדלה לאחר הקללה. גם בחלק זה של הקללה אנו רואים שהאל ברחמיו דואג לנו.

אנו מגדלים את הארטישוק על־מנת עלי המרירות שלו, המשמשים להכנת מרירים לעיכול. חשבו על זה: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, עלה פטל ושורשי פטל שחור הם רק כמה דוגמאות לחברים של אותם "עשבים קוצניים" המשמשים לתועלות רפואיות ומזון אחרות. כמה טוב מאלוהים לתת לנו תועלות בתוך הקללה עצמה!

מוות

זו ה"ד" שאותנו רובנו מעדיפים לא לדבר עליה. במציאות, כשאנו נושמים נשימה ראשונה, אנו קרובים נשימה אחת למוות. אף על פי שכל הצמחים, החיות והאנשים בסופו של דבר ימותו, עדיין איננו מרגישים נוח עם זה. זה לגמרי טבעי שיש לנו רצון לחיות, ואם אין לנו — עלינו לבקש עזרה כדי לברר מדוע.

באמת, למוות אין גיל. במהלך חייי עזרתי לקבור תינוקות נולדים מתים, אנשים עד גיל 96, ואת כל הגילאים שביניהם. אנו קוראים על גן־עדן משוחזר ויפהפה שראה השליח יוחנן בתגלית, כאשר הוא מתאר את השמים. חלק מהדברים שהוא מזכיר הם: אין מחלה, אין צער, אין פרידה, אין דמעות, אין יותר סבל, ואין מוות. בדרך מסוימת, החיים הם רק תקופת הריון לנצחיות. איננו יכולים להישאר כאן, כמו התינוק ברחם שאינו יכול להחליט שאינו רוצה להיכנס לעולם האמיתי. עם כל צערנו ופיתויים, גופינו נשחקים ומתכלים. עם כל האלימות, החטא והרשע מסביבנו, האם באמת היינו רוצים להישאר כאן במצב הזה לנצח? במקום זאת, אנו שבים לאדמה שממנה נבראנו, אפר לאפר ואבק לאבק, ממתינים לתחיית המתים הסופית. האם לא היה זה חנון מאלוהינו הנאמן שלא לאפשר לאדם החוטא לאכול מעץ החיים במצבו החוטא והמת? האם אנו יכולים לראות ולהיות אסירי תודה על נאמנות האל שסיפק מוות פיזי?

בתוך הקללה שניתנה לחוה, מתגלה הנבואה הראשונה על המשיח: "ואשים איבה בינך ובין האשה ובין זרעך ובין זרעָהּ; הוא ישופך בראש ואתה תשופנו בעקב" (בראשית ג':15). הוא מנצח המוות! הלל לאל על נאמנותו.

התפרקות וריקבון

התפרקות וריקבון הם עוד "ד" של הקללה. אגוז נופל לקרקע ונבט צץ בקרוב. בעוד כמה שנים יהיה שיח קטן. השנים חולפות, וסנאים אוספים את הבלוטים שנופלים לקרקע בכל סתיו. אז, כאשר הוא עץ אלון רב עוצמה הוא תופס וירוס, מת, ובמשך כמה שנים נפל על ידי סופת רוח. כאן הוא שב לאדמה כשהוא מתפורר ומתפרק. מאז הקללה, כל דבר נרקב ומתפרק. בהתחשב בכל הצמחים, החיות והאנשים שנפלו במהלך 6,000 השנים האחרונות, האם לא טוב מאלוהים שתכנן התפרקות וריקבון? איך העולם הזה היה נראה אם כל השאריות של 6,000 שנים היו עדיין מוטלות סביבנו? הארץ הייתה מכוסה בעצים מתים וגופות! זה אולי קשה לתפוס, אך האל תכנן ממלכות שלמות בבריאה רק כדי להשיג זאת לפני שזה אפילו היה נחוץ כי הוא צפה את הצורך. ממלכות השמרים, העובש והפטריות, ממלכות הבקטריות, האנזימים וחיי צמחים וחיות מיקרוסקופיים מסייעים לפרק את סיבי החיים ולהפכם לדשן מושלם להשלמת מעגל החיים ולסיפוק הדור הבא. קרקע אורגנית בריאה מכילה כ־8 מיליארד מיקרובים בכפית אחת. זו עוד סיבה לכך שחשוב לכבד את האדמה, לא להשתמש בכימיקלים קשים.

האם אי פעם חשבתם על המבול הגדול של נח? דמיינו את מיליוני הטונות של חומר צמחי, חייתי ואנושי צפים לפני שישקעו וייקברו במהירות בסדימנט כשהמים נסוגו. זה יצר את התנאים האידיאליים לעשיית פחם ושאר דלקים מאובנים שאנו משתמשים בהם היום. שם הם היו, עמוק בתוך האדמה, עד היום שנמצאו. עד היום הם עדיין נמצאים בשימוש.

יהי רצון שנהיה מנהלים אחראים ונאמנים של אדמת האדון!

"כי־ציפיית הבריאה בערגה מחכה לגלות בני האלהים. כי הבריאה הושמה לשווא — לא מרצונה, אלא על־ידי זה שהשימה אותה בתקוה; כי גם הבריאה תתחלל משעבוד ההשחתה אל לחופש הכבוד של בני האלהים. כי אנחנו יודעים שהבריאה כולה משתפלת ומתאנקת יחד עד עכשיו; ולא הם לבדם, כי גם אנחנו, אשר יש לנו את פירות הראשונים של הרוח, גם אנחנו עצמנו מתאנקים בקרבנו, מחכים לאומנות — לכלומר לגאולת גופנו" (רומאים ח':19-23).

The message was brief. “Dr. Waldron, would you call Mrs. Jones back about her labs?”

I was puzzled. I didn’t remember ordering any labs for Mrs. Jones. As far as I could remember, she was seeing a specialist and just had surgery for colon cancer. Maybe they had ordered the labs. But if so, they certainly should have followed up on them.

I opened the chart and looked in the lab section. Quickly my eye went to my patient’s kidney function and stopped. Her kidney function had declined a huge amount in the last week.

I called her and then her kidney specialist. Over the next half hour, her situation came into view. Because of her colon surgery, she was losing a lot of fluid, enough that she couldn’t keep up. This, in turn, was making her kidney function a lot worse, along with dropping her potassium level.

To take care of it, she would need IV fluids – once or twice a week – to keep up with the fluids she was losing. Without that, her kidneys would shut down completely.

In a sense, Mrs. Jones was dealing with kidney burnout—a situation where they were putting out more than they were taking in and suffering as a result.

As I was thinking about this, my mind went to the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea is “Dead” because it has such a high level of minerals and salts that very few, other than a few microorganisms, can survive.

The reason for this is that the Dead Sea has no outlet. The Jordan River drains into it, carrying fresh water, and then sits in a basin. Some of the water evaporates, and what remains are the salts and minerals in the water.

Over the thousands of years since the fall of Sodom and Gomorrah, this inland body of water has become one of the saltiest places on earth. It is a body of water that is neither useful for irrigation nor a place where plants and animals can thrive.

Neither situation is healthy, yet this is exactly how most people live their lives, typically gravitating towards one pole or the other. Either they fill their schedule to the maximum, leaving no time for quiet reflection, or they resist any efforts to get them to invest their time and talents and avoid these sorts of activities.

I want to spend a little time thinking about burnout. What causes it, and how we can avoid it?

Everyone has Limits

I Samuel 30 tells the story of David returning to Ziklag. Upon his arrival, he discovered, to his dismay, that the Amalekites had invaded Philistine territory, burned the town, and taken captive all the people who were present.

David and his men had been gone three days and were already tired from their journey to and from Aphek, where King Agag had mustered his forces. Despite this and their anguish at the loss of their family members and material possessions, David consulted God and decided to pursue to the Amalekites out into the desert.

They had only gone as far as the Brook Besor when a third of his men gave up. Scripture tells us they were “too faint” to cross the brook. They were physically and mentally exhausted. Even if they had been able to hold things together for another day, they would be useless in battle.

So it was that David left them behind and continued to pursue the Amalekites, eventually defeating them with the four hundred men who were able to persevere. Here, we come to the interesting part. The men who had won the victory looked down on the men who had been faint. They said those faint-hearted men could have their families back, but all the spoil would be reserved for those who had won the victory.

In response, David said, “Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand. For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.” (I Samuel 30:23,24)

David did not wish to penalize those who had tried but did not have the strength to make it through to the final battle.

Perhaps this speaks of the grace we ought to extend to others who don’t have the strength or energy to continue for a season. Maybe it lets us know that we should extend that same grace to ourselves.

What is Burnout?

There are different definitions for burnout, but it all comes down to a state of physical, mental, or emotional exhaustion related to too much stress over an extended period of time. We tend to think of this stress as work-related. There are too many projects going on at once, not enough help, or an employer who has high expectations.

Stress is stress, and it all adds up. Even if work isn’t stressful, if you have a newborn baby at home, a family member with dementia, or many church responsibilities, you can still reach the place where you have little left to give.

It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph, and you push the accelerator a little harder, and nothing happens. In response, you push the gas pedal even harder, and a screeching noise comes from the engine. Suddenly, the dashboard lights up with funny lights, and the car starts to slow down.

The question is, how can we avoid burnout and what should we do if we realize that we are heading towards it?

Understanding Burnout

Burnout leads to both physical and emotional depletion. The problem with burnout is that even if a particular stressor causes it – say, a situation at work or a family health problem – it will affect numerous other relationships.

People dealing with burnout often exhibit symptoms consistent with depression and anxiety. They may become withdrawn, lack motivation to be involved with church and family activities, or get angry quicker than people who are not dealing with burnout.

There is even a suggestion that burnout can lead to the weakening of our immune systems. This could lead to more colds and viral infections.

Identify Early Signs

We need to know ourselves. There are signs that other people can see in our lives and how we relate to others that we don’t necessarily identify as a problem.

People who are on the edge of burnout feel hopeless. They may hide it from their coworkers, but often, their family members realize that something is wrong. You used to have a sunny disposition, and now you are discouraged, not only about the present but also the future.

You might lack motivation and have low energy levels. In a sense, you are going through the motions and just doing enough to get by – both at work and in your home. This is likely related to your feelings of hopelessness.

You may find that you are more irritable than you used to be. Little things bother or aggravate you, and you find yourself smothering angry retorts.

It is important to realize that you are heading down this road for several reasons. First, you are not the only one who suffers when you are burned out. Your family must deal with you and your “grumpiness.” Also, the longer you go without taking care of things, the harder it is to get back to a place of balance.

As a physician, I see people all the time who “didn’t have time” to get something taken care of until they could no longer ignore it. At this point, it will take a major procedure to set things right. It would have been easier to correct if they came in with the first symptom.

Make a Priority List

Everything in our life has a priority level. People who do not prioritize end up feeling scattered as they try to do everything at once. This is a recipe for disaster. To me, it makes sense to divide our tasks into four buckets:

  1. Things that need to be done relatively quickly
  2. Things that need to be done but can wait a bit
  3. Things that we’d like to do, but don’t need to
  4. Things that we should let go of.

Here might be a good place to mention that just because something needs to be done does not mean you need to do it. Sometimes, someone in your home or workplace could help with one of the tasks on your to-do list.

Once we have made our priority list, we need to do something about it. If you simply assign a priority to everything in your life but continue to try to do everything, it won’t help your situation at all.

The point of this exercise is to figure out what things you can eliminate from your schedule, so you have more space to breathe.

Make First Things First

One of the things that happens when we are overwhelmed is that we stop doing self-care. We grab unhealthy food on the go, stop spending time in prayer and devotions, and quit exercising.

Doing these things takes time, and that is exactly what we think we don’t have when we are living on the margins of our energy. Self-care is extremely important but often gets assigned a priority of zero and is seldom included in a day’s activity.

As we begin to replenish our spiritual nourishment, we must also make sure we take care of our physical health.

Take Time Apart

After feeding the multitudes, Mark 6:46 tells of Jesus, “And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.” Even Jesus had times when He needed to be alone without distractions.

It is easy to focus on the prayer aspect of this passage, and that is important, but let's focus on the solitary aspect of this experience. Jesus even left His closest followers behind during this time of seeking God’s face.

There are times when we need to escape from the pressure of human interactions and find a peaceful place where we can be alone.

Put Down Technology

Part of making rest time truly restful is to eliminate sources of distraction. Phones and electronic tablets are exactly the types of things that can keep our minds from achieving the peace (shalom) that we both desire and need.

Digital burnout is a new term that is being used to describe people who feel apathetic and exhausted from spending hours each day staring at screens. Many workers spend seven or eight hours a day looking at computer screens and then get even more screen time after work.

The funny thing is that the most productive workers are often people who use old-fashioned things like paper calendars and leave phones out of meetings. As wonderful as phones are, they are also immensely distracting for most of us.

So often, we have time away that is simply not restful. The reason is that we continue to receive texts and emails and can still access social media. If you are not someone who can put his phone away and ignore it (it takes a lot of willpower to do this), then leave your phone in another room and create some distance. This will seem stressful, but we can focus on recharging ourselves by creating a screen-free zone.

Build Breaks into Your Day

There is a certain amount of work that must be done each day, and it often feels like too much for the allotted 24 hours. There is certainly no time to stop, stretch, and take a five-minute walk, or at least that's what we tell ourselves.

In reality, if you take a five-minute break every few hours to do something non-work related, you will come back refreshed and more ready to deal with the problems of the day.

Do something healthy during this time. Take a short walk or eat an apple. Chowing down a bag of potato chips or eating a couple candy bars is not likely to produce the desired results.

The problem is often with our own expectations. People who struggle with burnout often have extremely high personal standards and get frustrated when they not measure up to that standard.

Be Intentional about Rest

One of the messages of the Old Testament was the importance of the Sabbath. I have heard many people argue that in the New Testament period, we no longer need to practice the Sabbath. Didn’t Paul say that one day was like the other? Didn’t Jesus defend His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath?

Regardless of what you believe about the importance of keeping the Sabbath, it is still important that we take time to rest. This is the real message that Jesus was conveying when He said that the “Sabbath was created for man, not man for the Sabbath” (Mark 2:27).

Rest is not simply sleeping till 10 am and then doing nothing. Rest is actively making decisions that will help us recharge our depleted batteries. Go out for breakfast with a friend, take a hike, or take a good book and go somewhere without cell service and focus on something other than situations that are depleting you.

Jesus understood the human need for rest, this is why He told His disciples “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while” (Mark 6:31). This time of rest would give them energy for their next time of ministry.

Don’t Buy into Myths

People tell themselves all sorts of lies that can lead to pushing themselves too hard. I’ll list a few of them and some thoughts about each one.

“I’m the only one who can do this task.” This feels true. The other people in our home or workplace are not helping us the way we wish that they would. Sometimes, it simply feels easier to do the task ourselves rather than spend time teaching someone else how to do it. We need to remember that if we died, the people around us would figure out how to get things done. We can assign them some of the tasks today before we die.

“If I just get this job done today, tomorrow will be easier.” I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but each day has 24 hours, and somehow, they always get filled up. I have given up the idea that there is a time in my life coming up soon that will have nothing on the schedule. If a rest comes, it will come because I have made an effort to clear my schedule, not because by some random occurrence, one day, I happen to not have a single task in it.

“God will never give me more than I can handle.” God has promised many things. He has promised that when there is a temptation, He will give us an opportunity to escape it (I Corinthians 10:13). He has also promised that He will never leave us or forsake us (Hebrews 13:5). I do not read anywhere in Scripture that God will keep us from overfilling our lives. He has simply promised that He will give us opportunity to take a different path and will walk beside us on our way.

So often the heavy load we carry is because other people, or even we, ourselves, have put too many things on our task list. Suppose I choose to put too many patients on my schedule and I am feeling exhausted. In that case, it is time for me to take responsibility for what I have done, rather than claiming a mythical promise that God will keep me from overwhelming myself.

“These are all good things that I am doing.” Doctors face this a lot. We want to squeeze one more patient into the schedule and stay just a little later to answer another message because we feel responsible. We hate to think that someone might need to go to the Emergency Department because we did not take care of them when they needed help.

Just because the things in your schedule are “good things” that benefit other people and are building the kingdom, does not mean that you don’t need to cut back in one area or another. If you are feeling emotionally depleted, it is probably time to remove a few items from your to-do list.

Conclusion

There are other things that could be mentioned. Getting support from someone else, meditating on Scripture, and even taking a vacation are all things that can help.

When I read about some of the famous preachers of the past, I see in some of their lives a roller coaster. They pushed themselves to the max, got involved in large numbers of projects, and then had an emotional breakdown. They would take some time off and, a month or two later, launch back into the same activities. This cycle continued for their whole ministry.

Jesus tells us that His yoke is easy, and His burden is light (Matt, 11:28-30). If we are at the point of exhaustion, we need to consider whether we have Jesus’ yoke or if we are laboring under the burden of our own creation.

Jesus knows our limitations. He wants us to have balance, living in such a way that we not only have strength for today but also for tomorrow, next week, and next year – till He comes again.
