It was the proverbial “perfect world” that Adam and Eve enjoyed daily with their Creator. The beautiful garden, designed, created, and hand-planted by God Himself, was perfect in every way. We all know that it didn’t stay like that for very long. Because of the privilege of choice that God gave to all mankind, they both soon made the wrong choice. Eve, although deceived by Satan in the form of the serpent, believed the lie and chose to disobey God, doing the only thing that God had lovingly asked her not to do. But when she brought the fruit to Adam, he wasn’t deceived. He knew it was wrong. God was not surprised but, nevertheless, was very disappointed. In Genesis 3, we read the sad account of mankind being expelled from the garden, barred from the tree of eternal life, and the curse being pronounced because of Adam and Eve’s sin. It seemed so dark and hopeless. Even though it was only one man who sinned, the curse passed on to all of the created world, including the earth, plants, and animals. Just consider with me what all came along with this mighty curse.

  1. Disease
  2. Distress and Pain
  3. Deterioration and destruction
  4. Dominance of certain plants like thorns and thistles
  5. Death
  6. Decomposition and Decay

We’ll refer to them today as the six “D’s” of the curse.

Disease

The world’s pristine days of eternal, perfect health were past. Disease entered the picture as part of the curse of sin. The children of men, the birds, beasts, and the plants would all begin to experience the effects of sickness and disease. But God was faithful by providing instructions that helped man to know how to avoid many preventable sicknesses by cleanliness and simple obedience. For example, God’s command to honor His original intent in marriage, maintain purity, avoid multiple potential diseases, etc. He was also interested in our spiritual condition. God never designed mankind to bear guilt. He wants us to have and keep our conscience clear because He knows that a guilty conscience can make you sick!

Some of these sicknesses would be unavoidable, but many could be prevented by building immunity. God was also faithful in designing people, plants, and animals with a regenerative microbiome (billions of helpful bacteria) and a systemic immune system, which helps us fight off diseases. It is amazing how each plant seems to have certain dietary or healing properties that are beneficial. How faithful a Creator!

Distress and Pain

I suspect there was no real reason for any pain in the Garden of Eden, but we have experienced pain ever since the day of their exit. Pain is indeed a part of many of our lives. There are many types of pain. Grief, sorrow, and rejection are all emotional pains that come with the curse. Aches, migraines, sore muscles, torn ligaments, infected tendons, worn joints, and broken bones are a few of the physical pains that we may experience sometime before our last breath. Again, God has been faithful in helping mankind understand what to do to relieve some of life’s pains and distresses. From ancient times, plants, herbs, and other remedies have helped people deal with pain and distress. To this day, we have many useful plants that help us with pain.

One of the most beautiful things that can be experienced on earth is the birth of a child. Yet birth is generally accompanied by much pain. Although we can’t eliminate this promised pain, God has been faithful in providing and revealing to us the use of many herbs for use before, during, and after birth to ease the pain and hasten recovery. He didn’t have to do that for us. Mankind really deserves no mercy. What a faithful Creator!

Deterioration and destruction

We don’t need to study history much to see this principle at work. Wind, rain, and sun all have deteriorating effects on many things. Whether we consider an eroded stream bank, the rocks worn smooth in the riverbed, or the tree blown over by the wind, these are all natural elements of destruction. But add to that what man has done to the plants, animals, the soil, and each other. Whether the devastating effects of destruction during the awful wars or self-centered and greedy practices during peace, man is a very destructive creature. God granted mankind dominion over all of creation. However, too often, we falsely interpret that to mean that we own this sphere called earth and can do whatever we want to with it. He who declared, “The earth is the Lord’s,” doesn’t agree with the idea that men are something other than stewards of God’s creation. It is indeed wicked to worship the created world or anything in it. But it is equally wicked to be unthankful and careless with our Creator’s creation! Nevertheless, God has faithfully designed His earth with regenerative capabilities in the midst of this curse. Bless our gracious Maker!

Dominance of Thorns and Thistles

Anyone who has ever gardened soon found the reality of the battle with weeds. In all fairness, any plant growing where it isn’t desired is a “weed.” Many weeds can be very beneficial plants if we only know what to use them for. Some of the plants that we call weeds are actually quite nutritious and healthy once we understand which ones are edible and how to prepare them. Today, we want to think about thorns and thistles. We need to assume they were created on the first six days, not after the curse was pronounced. It seems that their ability to outgrow the useful crops increased after the curse. Even in this part of the curse, we see God mercifully providing for us.

We grow the artichoke for its bitter leaves, which are used to make digestive bitters. Think about it: Blessed Thistle, Milk Thistle, Teasel, Raspberry Leaf, and Blackberry roots are only a few examples of members of these “thorny weeds” used for medicinal and other food benefits. How good of God to give us benefits in the middle of the very curse!

Death

This is the one “D” that most of us would rather not talk about. In reality, when we take our first breath, we are one breath closer to death. Although all plants, animals, and people will eventually die, we still don’t feel comfortable with it. It is quite normal for us to have a will to live, and if we don’t, we should seek some help to find out why.

Indeed, death has no age. In my lifetime, I have helped bury stillborn babies, people as old as 96 years old, and every age in between. We read of the beautiful paradise restored, seen by the Apostle John in Revelation, as he describes Heaven. Some of the things he mentions are no sickness, no sorrow, no separation, no tears, no more suffering, and no death. In a way, life is only a gestation period for eternity. We can’t stay here, just like the baby in the womb can’t decide that it doesn’t want to enter the real world. With all our sorrows and temptations, our bodies wear out and decay. With all the violence, sin, and wickedness around us, would we really want to stay here in this condition forever? Rather, we return to the soil that we were made from, ashes to ashes and dust to dust, awaiting the final resurrection. Wasn’t it gracious of our faithful God not to allow sinful man to eat of the tree of life in his current sinful, dying state? Can we see and be grateful for God’s faithfulness in providing physical death?

In the midst of the curse given to Eve, the first prophecy of the Messiah is revealed. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Genesis 3:15). He is the conqueror of death! Praise God for His Faithfulness.

Decomposition and Decay

Decomposition and Decay are another “D” of the curse. A nut falls to the ground, and a sprout soon appears. In a few years, it will be a small sapling. Years go by, and squirrels gather the acorns that fall to the ground each autumn. Then as a mighty oak it contracts a virus, dies, and in a few years is brought to the ground by a windstorm. Here, it returns to the soil as it decays and decomposes. Ever since the curse, everything rots and decays. Considering all the plants, animals, and people that have died in the last 6,000 years, isn’t it good of God to have designed decomposition and decay? What would this world look like if all the debris of 6,000 years were still lying around? The earth would be covered with dead trees and corpses! This may be hard to realize, but God designed entire kingdoms in creation just to accomplish this before it was even needed because He foresaw the need. The kingdoms of yeast, mold, and fungus, the kingdoms of bacteria, enzymes, and microscopic plant and animal life all help break down the fiber of life and make it into the perfect fertilizer for the completion of the life cycle and provision for the next generation. Healthy organic soil has about 8 billion soil microbes in a single tablespoon. This is another reason why it is so important to treat the soil with respect, not harsh chemicals.

Have you ever considered the great flood of Noah? Imagine the millions of tons of plant, animal, and human matter floating around before finally settling to the bottom and quickly being buried in sediment as the waters receded. This produced the ideal conditions to make coal and the other fossil fuels that we use today. There it was, deep within the earth, until the day it was discovered. To this day, it is still being used.

May we be responsible and faithful stewards of the Lord’s earth!

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected the same in hope. Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our bodies” (Romans 8:19-23).

Es war die sprichwörtlich „vollkommene Welt“, die Adam und Eva täglich mit ihrem Schöpfer genossen. Der schöne Garten, von Gott selbst entworfen, geschaffen und von Hand gepflanzt, war in jeder Hinsicht vollkommen. Wir alle wissen, dass es nicht sehr lange so blieb. Wegen des Entscheidungsprivilegs, das Gott der ganzen Menschheit gab, trafen sie beide bald die falsche Wahl. Eva, obwohl sie in der Gestalt der Schlange von Satan getäuscht wurde, glaubte die Lüge und entschied sich, Gott zu ungehorsam zu sein, indem sie genau das tat, wozu Gott sie liebevoll nicht aufgefordert hatte. Als sie die Frucht zu Adam brachte, war er jedoch nicht getäuscht. Er wusste, dass es falsch war. Gott war nicht überrascht, aber dennoch sehr enttäuscht. In Genesis 3 lesen wir den traurigen Bericht, dass die Menschheit aus dem Garten vertrieben, vom Baum des Lebens ausgeschlossen und der Fluch ausgesprochen wurde wegen der Sünde Adams und Evas. Es schien so dunkel und hoffnungslos. Obwohl nur ein Mann gesündigt hatte, ging der Fluch auf die gesamte geschaffene Welt über, einschließlich der Erde, der Pflanzen und der Tiere. Überlege mit mir, was alles mit diesem mächtigen Fluch einherging.

  1. Krankheit
  2. Leiden und Schmerz
  3. Verfall und Zerstörung
  4. Vorherrschaft bestimmter Pflanzen wie Dornen und Disteln
  5. Tod
  6. Zersetzung und Verwesung

Wir werden sie heute die sechs „D“ des Fluchs nennen.

Krankheit

Die unberührten Tage ewiger, vollkommener Gesundheit der Welt waren vorbei. Krankheit trat als Teil des Fluchs der Sünde in Erscheinung. Die Kinder der Menschen, die Vögel, die Tiere und die Pflanzen würden alle beginnen, die Auswirkungen von Krankheit und Erkrankung zu erfahren. Aber Gott war treu, indem er Anweisungen gab, die dem Menschen halfen zu wissen, wie er viele vermeidbare Krankheiten durch Sauberkeit und einfachen Gehorsam vermeiden konnte. Zum Beispiel Gottes Gebot, seine ursprüngliche Absicht in der Ehe zu ehren, Reinheit zu bewahren, mehrere potenzielle Krankheiten zu vermeiden usw. Er war auch an unserem geistlichen Zustand interessiert. Gott hat die Menschheit niemals dazu entworfen, Schuld zu tragen. Er will, dass wir ein klares Gewissen haben und bewahren, weil er weiß, dass ein schuldiges Gewissen einen krank machen kann!

Einige dieser Krankheiten wären unvermeidlich, aber viele konnten durch Aufbau von Immunität verhindert werden. Gott war auch treu darin, Menschen, Pflanzen und Tiere mit einem regenerativen Mikrobiom (Milliarden hilfreicher Bakterien) und einem systemischen Immunsystem zu gestalten, das uns hilft, Krankheiten abzuwehren. Es ist erstaunlich, wie jede Pflanze scheinbar bestimmte ernährungsphysiologische oder heilende Eigenschaften hat, die nützlich sind. Welch treuer Schöpfer!

Leiden und Schmerz

Ich vermute, im Garten Eden gab es keinen wirklichen Grund für Schmerz, aber seit dem Tag ihres Ausgangs erleben wir Schmerzen. Schmerz ist in der Tat ein Teil vieler unserer Leben. Es gibt viele Arten von Schmerz. Trauer, Kummer und Zurückweisung sind alles emotionale Schmerzen, die mit dem Fluch einhergehen. Schmerzen, Migräne, Muskelkater, gerissene Bänder, infizierte Sehnen, abgenutzte Gelenke und gebrochene Knochen sind einige der körperlichen Schmerzen, die wir irgendwann vor unserem letzten Atemzug erleben können. Wieder einmal war Gott treu darin, der Menschheit zu helfen zu verstehen, was zu tun ist, um einige der Schmerzen und Leiden des Lebens zu lindern. Seit alter Zeit haben Pflanzen, Kräuter und andere Heilmittel den Menschen geholfen, mit Schmerz und Leid umzugehen. Bis heute haben wir viele nützliche Pflanzen, die uns bei Schmerzen helfen.

Eines der schönsten Dinge, die auf Erden erlebt werden können, ist die Geburt eines Kindes. Doch die Geburt ist im Allgemeinen mit viel Schmerz verbunden. Obwohl wir diesen verheißenen Schmerz nicht beseitigen können, war Gott treu darin, uns die Verwendung vieler Kräuter vor, während und nach der Geburt zu geben und offenzulegen, um den Schmerz zu lindern und die Genesung zu beschleunigen. Er musste das nicht für uns tun. Die Menschheit verdient wirklich keine Barmherzigkeit. Welch ein treuer Schöpfer!

Verfall und Zerstörung

Wir müssen die Geschichte nicht lange studieren, um dieses Prinzip in Aktion zu sehen. Wind, Regen und Sonne wirken sich alle zerstörerisch auf viele Dinge aus. Ob wir nun ein erodiertes Flussufer, die im Flussbett glattgeschliffenen Steine oder den vom Wind entwurzelten Baum betrachten, dies sind alles natürliche Elemente der Zerstörung. Aber fügt man hinzu, was der Mensch den Pflanzen, Tieren, dem Boden und einander angetan hat. Ob die verheerenden Zerstörungen in schrecklichen Kriegen oder selbstsüchtige und gierige Praktiken in Friedenszeiten — der Mensch ist ein sehr zerstörerisches Geschöpf. Gott gab der Menschheit Herrschaft über die ganze Schöpfung. Zu oft interpretieren wir das jedoch fälschlich so, dass wir diese Sphäre namens Erde besitzen und damit tun können, was wir wollen. Der, der erklärte: „Die Erde ist des HERRN“, stimmt nicht mit der Vorstellung überein, dass Menschen etwas anderes seien als Verwalter von Gottes Schöpfung. Es ist in der Tat böse, die geschaffene Welt oder irgendetwas darin anzubeten. Aber es ist ebenso böse, undankbar und nachlässig mit der Schöpfung unseres Schöpfers umzugehen! Dennoch hat Gott seinen Erdboden treu mit regenerativen Fähigkeiten ausgestattet, mitten in diesem Fluch. Gesegnet sei unser gnädiger Schöpfer!

Vorherrschaft von Dornen und Disteln

Wer jemals gegärtnert hat, hat bald die Realität des Kampfes mit Unkraut bemerkt. Um fair zu sein: Jede Pflanze, die an einem Ort wächst, an dem sie nicht erwünscht ist, ist ein „Unkraut“. Viele Unkräuter können sehr nützlich sein, wenn wir nur wüssten, wofür man sie verwenden kann. Einige Pflanzen, die wir Unkraut nennen, sind tatsächlich ziemlich nahrhaft und gesund, sobald wir wissen, welche essbar sind und wie man sie zubereitet. Heute wollen wir über Dornen und Disteln nachdenken. Wir müssen annehmen, dass sie in den ersten sechs Tagen geschaffen wurden, nicht erst nach dem Aussprechen des Fluchs. Es scheint, dass ihre Fähigkeit, die nützlichen Feldfrüchte zu überwuchern, nach dem Fluch zugenommen hat. Selbst in diesem Teil des Fluchs sehen wir, dass Gott barmherzig für uns sorgt.

Wir bauen die Artischocke wegen ihrer bitteren Blätter an, die zur Herstellung von Verdauungsbitterstoffen verwendet werden. Denk daran: Blessed Thistle (Gesegnete Distel), Mariendistel, Karde, Himbeerblatt und Brombeerwurzeln sind nur einige Beispiele von Mitgliedern dieser „stacheligen Unkräuter“, die für medizinische und andere Nahrungszwecke verwendet werden. Wie gut von Gott, uns mitten im Fluch Nutzen zu geben!

Tod

Das ist das eine „D“, über das die meisten von uns lieber nicht sprechen würden. In Wirklichkeit sind wir mit jedem Atemzug einen Atemzug näher am Tod. Obwohl alle Pflanzen, Tiere und Menschen schließlich sterben werden, fühlen wir uns dennoch unbehaglich dabei. Es ist ganz normal, dass wir einen Willen zu leben haben, und wenn wir ihn nicht haben, sollten wir Hilfe suchen, um herauszufinden, warum.

Der Tod kennt tatsächlich kein Alter. In meinem Leben habe ich geholfen, totgeborene Kinder zu begraben, Menschen bis zu 96 Jahren und jedes Alter dazwischen. Wir lesen von dem schönen wiederhergestellten Paradies, das der Apostel Johannes in der Offenbarung sieht, wenn er den Himmel beschreibt. Einige der Dinge, die er erwähnt, sind keine Krankheit, kein Kummer, keine Trennung, keine Tränen, kein weiteres Leiden und kein Tod mehr. In gewisser Weise ist das Leben nur eine Tragezeit für die Ewigkeit. Wir können nicht hierbleiben, genauso wie das Kind im Mutterleib nicht entscheiden kann, dass es nicht in die wirkliche Welt eintreten will. Trotz all unserer Sorgen und Versuchungen verschleißen und verfallen unsere Körper. Bei all der Gewalt, Sünde und Bosheit um uns herum, würden wir wirklich für immer in diesem Zustand bleiben wollen? Vielmehr kehren wir zu dem Boden zurück, aus dem wir gemacht wurden, Asche zu Asche und Staub zu Staub, in Erwartung der endgültigen Auferstehung. War es nicht gnädig von unserem treuen Gott, dem sündigen Menschen nicht zu erlauben, in seinem gegenwärtigen sündigen, sterbenden Zustand vom Baum des Lebens zu essen? Können wir Gottes Treue in der Gewährung des physischen Todes sehen und dafür dankbar sein?

Mitte des Fluchs, der Eva gegeben wurde, offenbart sich die erste Prophezeiung des Messias. „Und ich will Feindschaft setzen zwischen dir und der Frau und zwischen deinem Samen und ihrem Samen; er wird dir den Kopf zertreten, und du wirst ihm die Ferse verletzen“ (Genesis 3,15). Er ist der Bezwinger des Todes! Preis sei Gott für seine Treue.

Zersetzung und Verwesung

Zersetzung und Verwesung sind ein weiteres „D“ des Fluchs. Eine Nuss fällt zu Boden, und bald erscheint ein Keim. In einigen Jahren wird es ein kleiner Setzling sein. Jahre vergehen, und Eichhörnchen sammeln die Eicheln, die jeden Herbst zu Boden fallen. Dann, als mächtige Eiche, fängt sie sich einen Virus ein, stirbt, und in wenigen Jahren wird sie durch einen Sturm zu Fall gebracht. Hier kehrt sie als sie verrottet und zerfällt zum Boden zurück. Seit dem Fluch verrottet und verfällt alles. Wenn man bedenkt, wie viele Pflanzen, Tiere und Menschen in den letzten 6.000 Jahren gestorben sind, ist es nicht gut von Gott, Zersetzung und Verwesung entworfen zu haben? Wie würde diese Welt aussehen, wenn all die Überreste von 6.000 Jahren noch herumliegen würden? Die Erde wäre bedeckt mit toten Bäumen und Leichen! Das mag schwer zu erkennen sein, aber Gott hat ganze Reiche in der Schöpfung entworfen, nur um dies zu vollbringen, noch bevor es überhaupt nötig war, weil er die Not sah. Die Reiche der Hefen, Schimmelpilze und Pilze, die Reiche der Bakterien, Enzyme und mikroskopischen Pflanzen- und Tierleben helfen alle, die Fasern des Lebens zu zersetzen und in den perfekten Dünger zur Vollendung des Lebenszyklus und zur Versorgung der nächsten Generation zu verwandeln. Gesunder organischer Boden hat etwa 8 Milliarden Bodenmikroben in einem einzigen Esslöffel. Dies ist ein weiterer Grund, warum es so wichtig ist, den Boden mit Respekt zu behandeln und nicht mit scharfen Chemikalien.

Hast du jemals an die große Flut Noahs gedacht? Stell dir die Millionen Tonnen pflanzlicher, tierischer und menschlicher Materie vor, die umherschwammen, bevor sie endlich absanken und schnell von Sediment bedeckt wurden, als die Wasser zurückgingen. Dies schuf die idealen Bedingungen zur Bildung von Kohle und anderen fossilen Brennstoffen, die wir heute nutzen. Dort lag es, tief in der Erde, bis zu dem Tag, an dem es entdeckt wurde. Bis heute wird es noch verwendet.

Mögen wir verantwortungsvolle und treue Verwalter der Erde des Herrn sein!

„Denn das sehnsüchtige Harren der Kreatur wartet auf die Offenbarung der Kinder Gottes. Denn die Kreatur ist der Vergänglichkeit unterworfen worden — nicht freiwillig, sondern um desjenigen willen, der sie unterworfen hat — auf Hoffnung hin, dass auch die Kreatur selbst frei werden wird von der Knechtschaft der Vergänglichkeit zu der herrlichen Freiheit der Kinder Gottes. Denn wir wissen, dass die ganze Schöpfung bis jetzt mit uns zusammen seufzt und in Wehen liegt. Und nicht nur sie, sondern auch wir selbst, die wir die Erstlinge des Geistes haben, seufzen in uns selbst und warten auf die Sohnschaft, auf die Erlösung unseres Leibes“ (Römer 8,19–23).

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

Da jeg ble omvendt, hadde jeg aldri hørt begrepet anabaptist. Jeg hadde aldri hørt mye om å vitne for andre. Jeg husker at jeg tenkte på alle vennene mine som ikke visste noe om det som nettopp hadde skjedd meg. Kjæresten min gjennom sju år forsto det ikke. Én tanke gikk stadig gjennom hodet mitt: «Jeg må fortelle dem!» Noe godt hadde skjedd meg, og alle måtte vite at det samme kunne skje dem! Jeg husker en gang da broren min og jeg tenkte på et sted hvor vi kunne fortelle mange mennesker om Jesus. Vi bestemte oss for å gå på en major league baseball-kamp. Jeg var nervøs, jeg var redd, og jeg vil aldri glemme hva som skjedde. Jeg hadde aldri talt for en stor forsamling før, men da jeg åpnet munnen, fylte Gud den.

Jeg gikk ikke bare og snakket med folk jeg ikke kjente. Når jeg så en gammel venn, fortalte jeg dem hva som hadde hendt meg. De sa vanligvis at de hadde hørt det før og forsøkte å overbevise meg om å slå meg til ro og ta det med ro. Jeg vil være den første til å innrømme at jeg gjorde noen feil de første årene. Jeg la merke til, til min forbauselse, at mens mange mennesker ikke likte meg, var det de som sa de var kristne som så ut til å mislike meg mest. En dag besøkte jeg en eldre mann som sa han hadde vært kristen mesteparten av livet. Under samtalen pekte han opp mot en lyspære og sa: «Ser du den lyspæren? Den snakker ikke.» Jeg ble sjokkert. Han fortalte meg at, ja, selv om Jesus sier at vi er verdens lys, skal lysene skinne stille. De taler ikke.

Jeg ble forbløffet. Var dette sant? Jeg dro hjem for å gjøre en bibelstudie. Det tok ikke lang tid før jeg fant vers som Matteus 4:23, «Og Jesus vandret omkring i hele Galilea, og lærte i deres synagoger, og forkynte evangeliet om riket, og helbredet alle slags sykdommer og alle slags plager blant folket.» Så i Matteus 9, da Jesus «så folkemengdene, fikk han medlidenhet med dem, for de var trett og hjelpeløse som får uten hyrde. Og han sier til sine disipler: Høsten er stor, men arbeiderne få; be derfor høstens Herre, at han sender ut arbeidere i sin høst» (Matteus 9,36–38).

Det virker for meg som om hvor enn Jesus gikk, talte Han med folk om riket. Jeg har sett folk vitne om Gud, men noen ganger på en støtende måte. Men betyr det at vi ikke skal vitne? Hvis du leser Apostlenes gjerninger, er det nesten det eneste du ser—evangeliet går ut! I ett tilfelle fanget myndighetene disiplene og sa at de kunne gå fri hvis de bare ville være stille. Men disiplene sa at det kunne de ikke. «For vi kan ikke la være å tale om det vi har sett og hørt» (Apg. 4:20). Senere ble de taus—ved døden.

En tid senere hørte jeg om disse menneskene kalt anabaptister. Da jeg studerte dem, begynte jeg å se hvordan også de nektet å være tause. Jeg bestilte et eksemplar av The Martyr’s Mirror og ble forbløffet da jeg leste om disse menneskene som levde som disiplene. De oppfylte det Jesus sa: «Og dere skal bli hatet av alle for mitt navns skyld; men den som blir stående til enden, skal bli frelst» (Matt. 10:22). Og i Romerne 8:36, «Slik det står skrevet: For din skyld blir vi slaktet hele dagen, vi regnes som sauer til slakting.»

Kjære brødre og søstre, jeg tror ilden holder på å slukne. Jeg hører mange av våre anabaptistfolk snakke om å leve et stille og fredelig liv. Jesus sier i lignelsen om såmannen: «Men den som fikk såkorn i tornebuskene, er den som hører ordet; og verdens bekymringer og rikdommens bedrag kveler ordet, og han blir uten frukt» (Matt. 13:22). Kan det være der mange av oss er? Vi lever i det frie landet Amerika hvor penger virker lette å skaffe. Er det mulig at vi har blitt lurt av vår egen rikdom og verdens bekymringer? Har vi blitt lik verden for å unngå å bli forfulgt av den?

For mange år siden flyktet en gruppe anabaptister fra forfølgelse og flyttet til et land hvor det var mindre undertrykkelse. De åpnet en møbelbutikk for å forsørge seg, men de klarte ikke å selge møbler fordi de var de fryktede anabaptistene. Snart ble situasjonen desperat fordi de ikke hadde penger til å kjøpe mat. En dag kom en velstående mann inn i butikken. Alle arbeiderne stanset det de gjorde. De tenkte: «Kanskje denne mannen kjøper noe, så vi kan spise!» En gammel bror gikk bort til den mulige kunden og spurte om han kjente Jesus. Etter en kort samtale stormet mannen ut av butikken i raseri. De sultne arbeiderne spurte den gamle mannen hvorfor han hadde skremt bort deres eneste sjanse til et salg. Han forklarte at for denne mannen å kjenne Jesus var langt viktigere enn at de skulle tjene litt penger.

I de tidlige anabaptistenes tankesett var evangeliet om Jesus det viktigste. Som i Apostlenes gjerninger kunne de ikke la være å tale om det de hadde sett og hørt. Og de ble også «slaktet hele dagen».

Så hva gjør vi med verset om et stille og fredelig liv? Verset finnes i 1 Timoteus 2:1–2: «Jeg formaner derfor først av alt at forbønner, bønner, ukrenkelige bønner og takksigelser holdes for alle mennesker, for konger og alle som sitter i høye stillinger, for at vi kan føre et stille og fredelig liv i all gudsfrykt og verdighet.» Hva mente apostelen Paulus da han skrev dette? Mente han at vi skulle være tause om evangeliet og aldri utfordre en synder? Det er vanskelig å tro at Paulus forteller oss å gjøre noe han aldri gjorde, noe Kristus selv aldri gjorde. Faktisk var ingen i Skriftene som fulgte Gud stille om sin tro. I tallrike beretninger om tidlige kristne som ble arrestert på grunn av sin tro, ba myndighetene dem om å være stille! Men de nektet, akkurat som disiplene. De valgte også døden fremfor et stille og fredelig liv.

En ung anabaptist som ble arrestert, etterlot sin kjære kone som ventet deres første barn. Myndighetene ventet til barnet ble født og brakte så spedbarnet til den nye faren i fengselet. De sa at han nå var far og kunne dra hjem for å være med sin kone og sønn. Han kunne til og med fortsette å tro på samme måte, men han måtte holde munn og ikke tale imot synd i statskirken. Den unge faren avslo. For ham var det ikke et alternativ å være stille. De brant ham på bålet.

Så hva betyr 1 Timoteus 2:1–2? Det synes som om de kristne i Bibelen og den tidlige kirke var opptatt av å spre evangeliet, opptatt av Kristi kirke. De gikk omkring og forkynte evangeliet, holdt møter i fjellene, i skogene, eller hvor som helst folk kom. Det var deres liv. I verset i 1 Timoteus 2 sier Paulus at vi bør be om at myndighetene lar oss leve i fred så vi kan spre evangeliet. Kristne bør være ute og spre ordet og trenge inn i riket. Vår bønn er at myndighetene lar oss leve i fred mens vi tjener Fredsfyrsten.

I dag er det lett å være kristen hvis du slår deg til ro og lever et stille og fredelig liv, uten å noen gang utfordre en synder eller korrigere en bror. Men hvem sa at det ville være lett?

Da vi bodde i Haiti, lærte vi vår menighet om kostnaden ved å følge Jesus. Det var utrolig å høre haitienes vitnesbyrd om å anvende Jesu undervisning i sitt liv. Én gang fortalte to medlemmer at de var i ferd med å miste jobbene fordi de fulgte evangeliet. Å høre dem stå fast for å følge sannheten gjorde meg glad. En annen søster i menigheten fortalte meg at skolen barna hennes gikk på hadde uniform, og jentene var pålagt å bruke bukser. Da hun sendte datteren sin på skolen i en beskjeden kjole, kom hun hjem med en lapp fra rektoren om at hun ikke skulle komme tilbake iført det plagget.

1 Peter 4:14 sier: «Hvis dere blir smyttet for Kristi navn skyld, så er dere salige; for Guds herlighets Ånd og hans Ånd hviler over dere. På deres side blir han spottet, men på deres side blir han herliggjort.»

Sann glede kommer av lidelse. Lidelse kommer av å adlyde Jesus. Er vi for opptatt med trivielle saker mens verden går til helvete? La oss følge Jesus som de tidlige kristne, hvor folk ikke kunne fornekte at Guds kraft virket i dem. Vi har noe alle trenger. Hva venter vi på? La oss gjenforenes, samles igjen, fornekte oss selv, ta opp korset og følge Ham!

Can I have a fulfilled heart if there is a vision, a hope, and or a dream in my life that lies barren and unrealized? Must I go through life carrying a cross of pain and loneliness while God answers the prayers of my friends and gives them the desires of their hearts? Is something wrong with me? Is my faith too weak? Have I not prayed enough, surrendered enough, been obedient enough? What is life all about? Why don’t I have peace and joy? Does God have a plan and a purpose for me?

“Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore” (Psalms 16:11).

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper” (Psalms 1:3).

God has a path provided for each of us that will lead to a fulfilled heart. In God’s presence, there is fullness of joy! God’s desire is that your heart would be like a riverside tree, filled with life, health, strength, and fruit. He desires that you experience grace, joy, and peace, in your everyday life. God wants to fill your heart with his desires and purposes. He longs for you to seek after his will and plan. If you walk on his pathway, you will be filled with blessing and grace. This does not mean that every desire that you may have comes to pass (I don’t think that will ever happen for anyone in this life) but rather that your heart is full of the blessings of God. Your heart does not need to feel like a desert, the Water of Life can fill it.

“But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Where does Fulfillment Begin?

Fulfillment starts in your relationship with God. Does He feel cold and distant to you, or do you find joy and peace in praying and walking with him? Do you know that your sins are forgiven and that you are accepted as His child? Do you obey God with a willing heart or are there areas in your life where you resist his will as revealed in the Bible? Walking in the love and grace of God is the most important thing you can do in life. This is the first step on the pathway to a fulfilled heart.

If you are struggling in your relationship with God and are not sure of his love, forgiveness, and acceptance, here are some directions from the Bible for you.

“But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) 7 Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) 8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

You should never think that Christ is in some unapproachable place, and unavailable to you. Christ is made known to you by the Bible, his Holy Spirit, and by his creation. Unbelief, sin, disobedience, and unforgiveness to others can keep you from experiencing his love and grace. Opening your heart to Him by faith, believing in your heart, and confessing with your mouth the Lord Jesus, will restore your relationship with God. He will wash away your sin and receive you as his child. Christ came to this earth to reconcile us to God. He paid the price of our sin and guilt. We can receive his gift of salvation through faith and repentance. Faith is simply hearing the Word of God and receiving it into our hearts.

As we receive the Word of God into our hearts, it enables us to be obedient to his will. We choose to believe all that God has spoken to us in the Bible. We let go of all our doubts and embrace His Word. Repentance is turning away from our own selfish will and our sinful ways and choosing to obey God and his Word. In 1 John 1:9 God has said that if we confess our sins, He will forgive us. Do you truly believe this? Is it hard for you to accept that he will forgive you? It is impossible for God to lie, therefore his Word and promises can always be trusted.

Practical ways to walk with God

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

There are spiritual prerequisites needed to walk with God. If we don’t have a right heart, these practical things won’t actually help us walk with God. It will only be an empty activity with no real meaning and little benefit.

With our hearts full of faith and love we need to believe everything in the Bible. We need to believe all its history, everything it says about the man, Jesus, all the prophecies, and all the direction God gives us in the Word.

We also need a surrendered heart and choose to follow and obey God in everything. There is no area in which we choose to neglect or disobey. We need to have confessed our sins and be born again by the Spirit of God.

Pray. For yourself, God’s kingdom, your family, the church, neighbors, widows and widowers, orphans, missionaries, governments, and the sick. Pray for people who have lost loved ones, hungry people, people in prison, and people who need salvation. Pray for God to send workers into the vineyard.

Study the Word. Memorize it and read it to others. Discuss it.

Sing praises to God! God has been so merciful to you. Rejoice in your salvation!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Contentment

Another big step in the pathway to a fulfilled heart is contentment. You can never be fulfilled if you aren’t content in knowing that you are in the will of God.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

What is covetousness? My definition of covetousness is having a strong desire for something that is outside of God’s will for me right now. Normally, covetousness will drive you to violate scripture and God’s will, to try to obtain the thing you have a desire for. For instance, if you are covetous of money, you will tend to do unethical things or neglect to follow the direction in the Bible in your pursuit of money. You may cheat, steal, scam, overcharge, or become a workaholic and neglect God, family, church, or the needy.

God has given us desires, and it is a good thing to pursue them if our heart is surrendered, seeking God’s will and pursuing it according to the direction given in the Bible. Seek to move forward, but never force your own will. Be open to the people that God has put in your life for direction.

You may be at the age when your friends are getting married. You also desire to get married, but all the doors slam shut in your face. It seems like God reveals his will to others but not you. Know that an unanswered prayer is an answer for you right here, right now.

God reveals his will to you day by day and moment by moment. Married people don’t know the long-term will of God for their lives any more than unmarried people. The reality is that my family could be taken away from me in an instant. No one is promised anything earthly for tomorrow. God promises us spiritual blessings but not physical or earthly ones.

Be careful with your expectations. You can create many hardships for yourself if you are very strong in your expectations. As an example, Matthew 20 has the story of the householder who promised his workers a penny for a day’s work. Later in the day, he hired other workers. In the evening, he was paying his workers, starting with the ones hired last, and gave them each a penny. Because of his generosity, the first workers expected more than he had promised them. Since they expected him to give them more than a penny, they murmured against him. Never have strong expectations for things that God hasn’t promised in the Bible, even if you feel like God has revealed it to you by his Spirit. It is far better to have a humble, open heart to God, family, and the brotherhood.

Fellowship

Fellowship with God’s people is another important step in the pathway to fulfillment. Don’t isolate yourself, but rather make yourself a part of God’s people.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

It can be easy to fall into the trap of feeling like you are different from everyone else and don’t fit in. Remember that everyone is unique, and together we make up the body of Christ. You are an important member and have gifts and abilities that are needed in your local fellowship. Spend time with people and find ways to be a blessing and help others.

Identity

Embrace your identity. You may wonder, who am I? Where do I fit in? This can be especially difficult if you have a strong desire to be married but are not. You might see others as becoming something that you desire to be but are not.

You might wonder, what is wrong with me that I am not married? This is wrong thinking. The reality is that there are many married people who are in a worse place than you. Be open when those around you have thoughts about changes you can and should make in your life, but don’t condemn yourself as not good enough and that others do not accept you. Ephesians chapter 1 says that you are chosen by God to be washed of your sins through the blood of Jesus and to be adopted as His child. You are accepted by God, and you are to be “to the praise of his glory!”

Purpose

The last step I am writing about is about purpose. What is one thing that you really enjoy doing that is a blessing to the church or Kingdom? God has a purpose for you to fulfill. You are a part of His kingdom that you can put time and energy into. God has called each one of us to be a servant, to follow in the footsteps of our Lord Jesus. It can be as simple as giving a glass of cold water in the name of Jesus. No task is too small or mundane to be a part of His kingdom. Be available. Have the heart of a servant. When you see a need, offer a helping hand or a listening ear.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. 5 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: 6 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: 7 But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:” (Philippians 2:4)My wife and I recently celebrated our third anniversary. I wish I could say that we always lived out the things that I wrote in this article, but we are human and did come short at times. But we can both say from experience that the things I wrote are real and true. There is a pathway to joy and fulfillment as an unmarried person. Jena pursued midwifery and sacrificed a lot to serve mothers and babies. Always ready to drop whatever she was doing or jump out of bed in the middle of the night to go serve. I did a lot of Bible studies and also trips to the Middle East to study the Bible in a different measure. God has graciously given me the privilege to visit places where few people have been. I’ve been able to see where many of the people in the Bible lived and walked, including Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and, best of all, Jesus. These people left behind a witness of faith and obedience. Let us follow them!

“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, 2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. 3 For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds . . . (Hebrews 12:1-3).

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; 13 And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. 14 Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: 15 Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled . . . (Hebrews 12:12-15)

“Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear” (Hebrews 12;28).

“תַּגִּיד לִי אָרוֹחַ חַיִּים; בְּנִכְרוֹתֶךָ שִׂמְחָה מְלֵאָה; בְּיָמִינְךָ נֵעָמוֹת לְעוֹלָם” (תהלים 16:11).

“וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ נָטוּעַ עַל־פַּתְחוֹת מָיִם, אֲשֶׁר פִּרְיוֹ יִתֵּן בְּעִתּוֹ, וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא־יִבּוֹל, וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יָעֲשֶׂה יִצְלָח” (תהלים 1:3).

לאלוהים יש נתיב שמסודר לכל אחד ואחת מאיתנו שיוביל ללב מלא. בנוכחות אלוהים יש שלמות של שמחה! רצון אלוהים הוא שלבך יהיה כעץ על שפת הנהר — מלא חיים, בריאות, כוח ופרי. הוא רוצה שתחווה חן, שמחה ושלום בחיי היומיום שלך. אלוהים רוצה למלא את לבך ברצונותיו ובמטרותיו. הוא משתוקק שתשאף לדעת את רצונו ותכניתו. אם תצעדי/תצעוד בשבילו, תמלאי/תמלא בברכה ובחסד. זה לא אומר שכל רצון שעשוי להיות לך יתגשם (איני חושב שזה יקרה אי פעם לאף אחד בחייו), אלא שהלב שלך יהיה מלא בברכות אלוהים. לבך לא חייב להרגיש כמדבר — מי החיים יכולים למלא אותו.

“וּמִי שְׁתָה מִן־הַמָּיִם אֲשֶׁר אֶתֶּן־לוֹ, לֹא יִצְמָא עוֹד; אֶלָּא הַמָּיִם אֲשֶׁר אֶתֶּן־לוֹ יִהְיוּ־בּוֹ בְּאֹמֶץ מַיִם הַזָּרִים לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם” (יוחנן 4:14).

איפה מתחילה המלאות?

המלאות מתחילה ביחס שלך עם אלוהים. האם הוא מרגיש קר ומרוחק עבורך, או שאת/ה מוצא/ת שמחה ושלום בתפילה ובהליכה איתו? האם את/ה יודע/ת שחטאיך נסלחו ושאתה/התקבל/ה כבנו/בתו? האם את/ה מציית/ה לאלוהים מלב שלם או שיש אזורים בחייך שבהם את/ה מתנגד/ת לרצונו כפי שנתגלה בתנ"ך? ההליכה באהבה ובחסד של אלוהים היא הדבר החשוב ביותר שאת/ה יכול/ה לעשות בחיים. זו הצעד הראשון על הנתיב ללב מלא.

אם את/ה נאבק/ת בקשרך עם אלוהים ואינך בטוח/ה באהבתו, בסליחתו ובהתקבלותך, הנה כמה הכוונות מהתנ"ך עבורך.

“וְהַצְּדָקָה הַמִּן־הָאֱמוּנָה דֹּבֶרֶת כָּךְ, אַל־תֹּאמַר בִּלְבָבְךָ מִי יַעֲלֶה הַשָּׁמָיְמָה? (כִּי לְהוֹרִיד אֶת־הַמָּשִׁיחַ); 7 אוֹ, מִי יִרְדֶּה לִתְהוֹם? (כִּי לְהָקִים אֶת־הַמָּשִׁיחַ מִן־הַמֵּתִים.) 8 וּמַה־אָמְרוּ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה? הַדָּבָר קָרוֹב אֵלֶיךָ, בְּפִיךָ וּבְלִבְּךָ: זֶה־דְּבַר הָאֱמוּנָה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנַחְנוּ מְבַשְּׂרִים; 9 כִּי אִם־תּוֹדֶה בְּפִיךָ אֶת־יֵשׁוּעַ הָאָדוֹן, וּבְלִבְּךָ תִּאֱמֵן כִּי הָאֱלֹהִים הֵקִים אֹתוֹ מֵהַמֵּתִים, תִּוָשַׁע; 10 כִּי בְּהַשְׁתַּחֲווּת לֵב נִאֱמַן־אִישׁ לְצְדָקָה, וּבְהוֹדָאָה בַּפֶּה הוּא נִתָּן לִיִשׁוּעָה” (רומים 10:6-10).

אין לחשוב שמשיח נמצא במקום בלתי-נגיש ואינו זמין עבורך. המשיח מתגלה לך דרך הכתובים, רוח הקודש שלו, ובאמצעות יצירתו. חסר אמונה, חטא, אי-ציות, וחוסר סליחה לאחרים יכולים למנוע ממך לחוות את אהבתו וחסדו. לפתוח את לבך אליו באמונה, להאמין בלבך ולהתוודות בפיך על אדון ישוע תשיב את יחסך עם אלוהים. הוא ישטוף את חטאיך ויקבלך כבנו/בת. המשיח בא לעולם כדי להסיר את הפירוד בינינו ובין אלוהים. הוא שילם את המחיר על חטאנו ואשמתנו. נוכל לקבל את מתנת הישועה על ידי אמונה ותשובה. אמונה היא פשוט לשמוע את דבר אלוהים ולקבלו ללבנו.

כאשר אנו מקבלים את דבר אלוהים ללבנו, הדבר מאפשר לנו לציית לרצונו. אנו בוחרים להאמין לכל מה שאלוהים דבר אלינו בתנ"ך. אנו משחררים את כל הספקות ומקבלים את דברו. התשובה היא סיבוב מהירה מהרצון האגואיסטי שלנו ומהדרכים החוטאיות שלנו ובחירה לציית לאלוהים ולדברו. בִּאֶחד יוחנן 1:9 אמר אלוהים שאם נתוודע על חטאינו, הוא יסלח לנו. האם את/ה מאמין/ה בזה באמת? האם קשה לך לקבל שהוא יסלח לך? קשה שאלוהים ישקר, ולכן דברו והבטחותיו תמיד ברי אמון.

דרכים מעשיות ללכת עם אלוהים

“לָכֵן עַכְשָׁו אֵין־הָרְשָׁעָה לַהֲמֻשָּׁעִים בַּמָּשִׁיחַ יֵשׁוּעַ, הַהֹלְכִים לֹא עַל־הַבָּשָׂר כִּי־אִם־עַל־רוּחַ” (רומים 8:1).

ישנם דרישות רוחניות נדרשות כדי ללכת עם אלוהים. אם לא יש לנו לב נכון, הדברים המעשיים הללו לא באמת יעזרו לנו ללכת עם אלוהים. הם יהיו רק פעילות ריקה ללא משמעות אמיתית ותועלת מועטה.

בלב מלא אמונה ואהבה עלינו להאמין לכל דבר בתנ"ך. עלינו להאמין לכל ההיסטוריה שבו, לכל מה שהוא אומר על האיש ישוע, לכל הנבואות, ולכל הכיוון שאלוהים נותן לנו בדבר.

נדרש גם לב נכנע ובחירה ללכת ולציית לאלוהים בכל דבר. אין אזור שבו נבחר להזניח או לא לציית. עלינו להיות מודים על חטאינו ולהיוולד מחדש ברוח אלוהים.

התפלל. עבור עצמך, למען מלכות אלוהים, משפחתך, הכנסייה, השכנים, האלמנות והאלמנים, יתומים, מיסיונרים, ממשלות, והחולים. התפלל בעד אנשים שאיבדו יקיריהם, רעבים, אסירים, ואנשים שזקוקים לישועה. בקש מאלוהים לשלוח פועלים לכרם.

למד את הדבר. שיננו אותו ולקרוא אותו לאחרים. דונו בו.

שירו תהילות לאלוהים! אלוהים היה רחום כלפיך. שמח/י בישועתך!

“וּכְּדֵי שֶׁהָגֵיוּ גּוֹיִם לְכַבֵּד אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים עַל־רַחֲמָיו; כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב, עַל־כַּךְ אֲנִי־אוֹדְךָ בְּתוֹךְ הַגּוֹיִם, וְאֶזְמְרָה לְשִׁמְךָ. 10 וְשׁוּב אָמַר, שְׂמְחוּ גוֹיִם עִם־עַמּוֹ. 11 וְשׁוּב, הַלְלוּ יָהּ כָּל־הָגוֹיִם; שַׁבְּחוּוּהוּ כָּל־הָאֻמִּים” (רומים 15:9).

תַּחֲנוּן (תַּכְסִית)

צעד גדול נוסף בדרך ללב מלא הוא Contentment — שובע שבע וצניעות הנפש. אינך יכול/ה להיות מלא/ה אם אינך שבע/ה בידיעה שאת/ה נמצא/ת ברצון אלוהים.

“יִהְיֶה שִׂיחֵכֶם בְּלִי־חִמָּה; וְהָיוּ מְרֻצִּים בְּאֵלֶּה שֶׁלָּכֶם; כִּי־אָמַר לֹא אוּסִפְּךָ וְלֹא אֶנָּחֵךְ. 6 עַל־כֵּן נִגְדַּל וְנֹאמַר בְּבִטָּחוֹן, ה' עוֹזֵר לִי וְלֹא אִירָא מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם לִי” (ע Hebrews 13:5).

מהי חמדנות? ההגדרה שלי לחמדנות היא רצון חזק לדבר מה שנמצא מחוץ לרצון אלוהים עבורי עכשיו. בדרך כלל חמדנות תדחוף אותך להפר את הכתובים ואת רצון אלוהים, כדי לנסות להשיג את הדבר שאת/ה מבקש/ת. לדוגמה, אם את/ה חמדן/ת לגבי כסף, תטה לעשות פעולות בלתי-אתיות או להזניח להלך לפי הכוונה שבתנ"ך במרדף אחרי כסף. ייתכן שתרמה, תגנוב, תטעה, תגבה מחיר מופרז, או תהפוך לעבודת יתר ותזניח את אלוהים, המשפחה, הכנסייה או נזקקים.

אלוהים נתן לנו תשוקות, וטוב לעקוב אחריהן אם ליבנו נכנע, מבקש את רצון אלוהים ורודף אותו בהתאם להנחיות שבתנ"ך. שאפו להתקדם, אך אל תכפו את רצונכם שלכם. היו פתוחים לאנשים שאלוהים שָׁם בחייכם כדי לכוון.

אולי את/ה בגיל שחבריך מתחילים להתחתן. גם את/ה רוצה להתחתן, אך כל הדלתות נסגרות בפניך. נראה שאלוהים מגלה את רצונו לאחרים אך לא לך. דע/י שתפילה שלא נענתה היא תשובה עבורך כאן ועכשיו.

אלוהים מגלה את רצונו לך יום אחרי יום ורגע אחרי רגע. אנשים נשואים אינם יודעים את רצון אלוהים לטווח הארוך לחייהם יותר מאחרים שאינם נשואים. המציאות היא שהמשפחה שלי יכולה להילקח ממני ברגע. לא מובטח לאיש כל דבר ארצי למחר. אלוהים מבטיח לנו ברכות רוחניות אך לא ברכות פיזיות או ארציות.

היזהר/י עם הציפיות שלך. את/ה יכול/ה ליצור לעצמך סבל רב אם אתה/את בעל/ת ציפיות חזקות. כדוגמה, בפרק מתי 20 יש את סיפור בעל הבית שהבטיח לעובדיו די־נק לתשלום ליום. מאוחר יותר ביום העסקה, הוא שכר עובדים אחרים. בערב, כשפדה את עובדי משמרתו, התחיל משלמי החל מאחרונים ושילם לכל אחד נטו. בגלל נדיבותו, העובדים הראשונים ציפו ליותר מה שהובטח להם. משום שציפו שיעניק להם יותר מטרצה, הם קיפחו עליו. אל תצפה/י בציפיות חזקות לדבר שאלוהים לא הבטיח בתנ"ך, גם אם נדמה לך שאלוהים גילה לך זאת ברוחו. עדיף להיות בעל/ת לב ענו־נפש ופתוח כלפי אלוהים, משפחה ואחים ואחיות באמונה.

קִהֲלָה

חברות עם עם אלוהים היא צעד חשוב נוסף בדרך למלאות. אל תתבודד/י — הצטרף/י לעמכם של אלוהים.

“וּמְשְׁבַעַת קִבֵּלוּ אֶת־דְּבָרָיו וְהָיוּ נָתוּן לָהֶם כְּמַעֲשֵׂה כְּמִסְפָּר שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים נְפָשׁוֹת. 42 וְהָיוּ נְמַצִּים בְּתֹם בְּדִקְלוּת הַתּוֹרָה הַשְּׁלֹשׁ־הַשָּׁלוֹשׁ, וּבְחֶבְרוּת, וּבְשְׁבִירַת־לֶחֶם, וּבְתְפִלּוֹת” (מעשי השליחים 2:41).

קל ליפול במלכודת של להרגיש שאת/ה שונה מכולם ושאינך שייך/ת. זכר/י שכולם ייחודיים, וביחד אנו מרכיבים את גוף המשיח. את/ה חבר/ה חשובה/ה ובעל/ת מתנות וכשרונות שנחוצים בקהילה המקומית שלך. בילו זמן עם אנשים וחפשו דרכים להיות ברכה ולעזור לאחרים.

זהות

קבלי/קבל את זהותך. ייתכן ותתהה/תתהי מי אני? היכן אני משתלבת/מתאים? זה יכול להיות קשה במיוחד אם יש לך תשוקה חזקה להתחתן אך אינך נשוא/ה. אולי את/ה רואה אחרים הופכים למה שאת/ה רוצה להיות אך עדיין לא.

אולי תתהה/תתהי מה לא בסדר איתי שאני לא נשוי/ה? זו חשיבה שגויה. המציאות היא שיש הרבה נשואים שנמצאים במצב גרוע יותר ממך. הייה פתוח/ה כאשר הסובבים אותך מביעים מחשבות על שינויים שאת/ה יכול/ה וצריך/ה לעשות בחייך, אך אל תאשימי/תאשימי את עצמך כרע/ה מספיק ושהאחרים לא מקבלים אותך. פאולוס באפיסים פרק א אומר שאת/ה נבחר/ת על ידי אלוהים להטהר מחטאיך דרך דם ישוע ולהיות מאומץ/ת כילד/ה שלו. את/ה מקובל/ת על ידי אלוהים, ועליך להיות “לשבח כבודו!”

מטרה

הצעד האחרון עליו אני כותב הוא על מטרה. מהו הדבר האחד שאת/ה באמת נהנה/ית לעשות שהוא ברכה לכנסייה או למלכות? לאלוהים יש מטרה שאת/ה צריך/ה להגשים. את/ה חלק מממלכתו שלהשקיע בה זמן ואנרגיה. אלוהים קרא לכל אחד ואחת מאיתנו להיות עבד/ה, ללכת בעקבות רגליו של אדוננו ישוע. זה יכול להיות פשוט כמו לתת כוס מים קרים בשם ישוע. אין משימה קטנה מדי או שגרתית מדי כדי להיות חלק מממלכתו. הייה זמין/ה. היה/י בעל/ת לב של משרת/ת. כשאת/ה רואה צורך, הושיט/י יד מסייעת או אזן/י אוזן קשבת.

“אַל־יַּבִּיט כָּל־אִישׁ אֶל־דְּבָרָיו הוּא לְבַדּוֹ, כִּי אִם־גַּם אֶל־דְּבָרֵי הָאֲחֵרִים. 5 יְהִי בְּכֶם הַמַּחְשָׁב הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר גַּם בְּמָשִׁיחַ יֵשׁוּעַ הָיָה; 6 אֲשֶׁר בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים הָיָה, לֹא חָשַׁב הֲרָהֹם שֶׁלִּהְיוֹת שָׁוֶה־עִם־הָאֱלֹהִים לִגְנֹב; 7 אֶלָּא הִשְׁתַּמֵּם מֵכָּבוֹד וְלָקַח עַל־עַצְמוֹ צֶלֶם עֶבֶד, וְנִמְצָא בְּדֶמוּת אָדָם” (פיליפיים 2:4-7) אשתי ואני חוגגים לאחרונה את יום הנישואין השלישי שלנו. הייתי בן 38 וג'נה הייתה בת 29 כשנישאנו. באביב האחרון ברכנו בתינוקת מתוקה, ג'יאנה. הלוואי יכולתי לומר שתמיד חיינו לפי הדברים שכתבתי במאמר זה, אך אנחנו אנושיים ולעתים נכשלנו. אבל שנינו יכולים לומר מניסיון שהדברים שכתבתי הם אמיתיים ונכונים. יש נתיב לשמחה ומילוי גם לאדם בלתי-נשוי. ג'נה רדפה אחרי התמחות בלידת נשים ותרמה רבות לשרת אמהות ותינוקות. תמיד מוכנה להניח הכול או לקפוץ מהמיטה באמצע הלילה כדי ללכת ולעזור. אני ערכתי הרבה לימודי תנ"ך וגם מסעות למזרח התיכון ללמוד את הכתובים במידה שונה. אלוהים נתן לי בחסדו את הזכות לבקר מקומות שבהם מעטים ביקרו. יכולתי לראות היכן רבים מהדמויות בתנ"ך חיו והלכו, כולל נח, אברהם, יצחק, יעקב, משה, דוד, ובִּטוּב־לב ישוע. אנשים אלה השאירו עדות של אמונה וצייתנות. נלך אחריהם!

“וּכִּי רָאִינוּ כֹּה כִּסָּה־עֵדִים גְּדוֹלָה, נַשְׁלִיךְ עַל־כָּל־מַשָּׂא, וְאֶת־הַחֵטְא הַבָּא־מִשָּׁם מְכַבֵּּד בָּנוּ עַל־עַצְמֵנוּ, וְנָרוּץ בְּסַבְלָנוּת אֶת־הַמָּרְתָּה הַנִּתֶּנֶת־לָּנוּ, 2 הַמַּבִּיט בְּיֵשׁוּעַ הַמְחִיל וּבֹשֵׁל אֶת־אֱמוּנָתֵנוּ, אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׂמַחַת אֲשֶׁר נִתְחָנְהָה לוֹ סָבַל אֶת־הַצְּלָב וּמָזַל אֶת־הֲשָׁפָלָה, וַיֵּשֵׁב בִּימִינוֹ שְׁמוּת־הָאֱלֹהִים. 3 כִּי שְׁקֹל בְּעֵינֶיךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר סָבַל כְּפִרְעֹת הַמְּחָטְאִים עַל־עַצְמוֹ, פֶּן־תִּתְעַיֵּף וְתִשְׁכָּל בְּמַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם . . . ” (ע Hebrews 12:1-3).

It was one of those Sunday afternoons in late spring when the sun was finally shining warmly. It was the time of year when little boys seem to have plenty of extra energy. Little Davy was sitting on the road bank with some neighborhood boys who had stopped by. He felt like jumping up and down in anticipation of the upcoming race.

Two older boys, Big David and Paul, showed up with brand-new bicycles. These were not the ordinary bicycles the other boys had. They were beautiful Vista bicycles with gleaming new paint, shiny chrome fenders, and three speeds. These bicycles glided smoothly on the chip-and seal road without a rattle. With new ball bearings, they whizzed along with hardly any effort being applied to the pedals. Even though there did not seem to be much difference between the bicycles, Big David’s was a gleaming chestnut brown, and Paul’s a sparkling metal flake blue.

“Well,” Big David began to brag, “With my longer legs, and freshly sprayed WD40, my bike is sure to be the fastest.”

“No,” challenged Paul, “my shorter legs can pump faster, and Schwinn’s high-test bicycle oil by far outperforms WD40, which really is only for squeaks.”

“A race! A race!” the other boys said, “Why not settle it with a race?”

“Okay,” Big David said, “We’ll have a race and see whose bike is really the fastest.”

“You bet!” Paul agreed. “We’ll start at the top of Billy’s hill and race all the way down to the bottom,” he said, pointing to the road bank where the other boys were sitting.

One, two, three, GO and they were off! Down the hill they came, pedaling for all they were worth.

“Go Paul!” and “Go Big David!” shouted the boys at the bottom of the hill. All the commotion woke up Little Davy’s rat terrier dog, Nellie. Yapping loudly, Nellie zoomed around the silo as fast as her four little legs could carry her. She headed straight for Big David’s bicycle in the front, barking loudly to try to make it stop. Poor Nellie did not realize another bicycle was trying to pass up the first one.

Thump, the passing bicycle hit the dog! Crash, bang, the two bicycles ran into each other!

“Hey – aye!” Oooff! Two boys flew over the handlebars and landed hard on the road. Those shining bicycles were no longer gleaming. They were lying on a heap, scratched and streaked with tar. Nellie limped back beside the silo and stayed lying there for several hours.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.

זה היה אחד מאותם אחר־צהריים של יום ראשון בסוף האביב, כשהשמש סוף־סוף הפציעה בחמימות. היה זה עונת השנה שבה נראים הבנים הקטנים מלאים באנרגיה נוספת. דייבי הקטן ישב על שפת הכביש עם כמה בנים מהשכונה שעברו שם. הוא חש כאילו רוצה לקפוץ למעלה ולמטה בציפייה למרוץ המתקרב.

שני בנים גדולים יותר, דוד הגדול ופול, הופיעו עם אופניים חדשים לחלוטין. אלה לא היו האופניים הרגילים של שאר הילדים. אלה היו אופני Vista יפים עם צבע חדש נוצץ, דפי כרום מבריקים, ושלוש הילוכים. אופניים אלה גלשו בצורה חלקה על הכביש המרוצף ללא רעידות. עם מיסבים חדשים, הם חלפו כמעט בלי מאמץ על הדוושות. אף על פי שלא נראה שיש הבדל גדול בין האופניים, אלה של דוד הגדול היו חומניים בוהקים בצבע שזיף, ואלה של פול היו כחולים מנצנצים בצבע מתכתי.

"נו," התחיל דוד הגדול בהתנשאות, "עם הרגליים הארוכות שלי, וב‑WD40 שנרוסס עכשיו כראוי, האופניים שלי בטוח יהיו המהירים ביותר."

"לא," אתגר פול, "הרגליים הקצרות שלי יכולות לדחוף מהר יותר, והשמן האיכותי של שנוין הרבה יותר טוב מ‑WD40, שזה באמת בשביל צלצולים."

"מרוץ! מרוץ!" אמרו שאר הילדים, "למה לא להכריע את זה במרוץ?"

"טוב," אמר דוד הגדול, "נעשה מרוץ ונראה מי האופניים האמיתיים המהירים."

"בין השורות!" הסכים פול. "נתחיל מראש הגבעה של בילי ונרוץ כל הדרך למטה," אמר כשהוא מצביע על שפת הכביש שבה ישבו שאר הילדים.

אחת, שתיים, שלוש — וצאו, והם יצאו לדרך! מטה את הגבעה הם ירדו, דוושו במלוא כוחם.

"קדימה פול!" ו"קדימה דוד הגדול!" צעקו הילדים בתחתית הגבעה. כל ההמולה העיר את כלבת ראט־טרייר של דייבי הקטן, נלי. נלי יללה והתרוצצה סביב האורווה במהירות שארבע רגליה הקטנות יכולות לשאת אותה. היא פנתה ישר לאופני דוד הגדול מלפנים, נבחנה חזק בניסיון לעצור אותם. המסכנה נלי לא הבינה שאופניים נוספים מנסים לעקוף את הראשונים.

תוף, האופניים העוברים פגעו בכלבה! קרעך, בום — שני האופניים התנגשו זה בזה!

"היי — אייכ!" אאוף! שני הבנים עפו מעל הכידון ונחתו בחוזקה על הכביש. אותם אופניים מבריקים כבר לא נראו נוצצים. הם שכבו בערימה, מפוספסים וכתומים מזפת. נלי חזרה צולעת לצד האורווה ושכבה שם מספר שעות.

שאר הילדים עמדו על הגדה עם הפה פתוח. במהירות הם רצו אל שני הבנים ששכבו ליד אופניהם החדשים. "אתם בסדר?" שאלו.

"אהיה טוב," אמר פול באיטיות, "אבל אין עוד מרוצים. למי בכלל אכפת מי האופניים המהירים ביותר."

אפילו שדייבי הקטן הוא עכשיו סבא, הוא לא שכח את מרוץ האופניים באותו אחר־צהריים של יום ראשון מזמן, כאשר דוד הגדול ופול למדו שהתפארות והראות בדרך כלל מגיעות לסיום מתרסק.

The other boys stood on the bank with their mouths open. Quickly, they ran to the two big boys lying by their new bicycles. “Are you okay?” they asked.

“I’ll be okay,” Paul said slowly, “but no more races. Who even cares whose bike is the fastest.”

Even though Little Davy is now a grandpa, he has not forgotten the bicycle race on that long ago Sunday afternoon, when Big David and Paul learned that bragging and showing off usually comes to a crashing end.

늦봄의 어느 일요일 오후, 마침내 따스한 햇빛이 비치던 날이었다. 그때쯤이면 꼬마 소년들은 유난히 에너지가 넘쳐 보이곤 했다. 어린 데이비는 동네 아이들이 모여 앉아 있는 도로 둑에 앉아 있었고, 곧 있을 경주를 생각하며 펄쩍펄쩍 뛰고 싶은 기분이었다.

두 형인 큰 데이비와 폴이 새 자전거를 타고 나타났다. 이 자전거들은 다른 아이들이 가진 평범한 자전거와는 달랐다. 반들반들한 새 페인트, 빛나는 크롬 펜더, 그리고 세 단 기어가 달린 아름다운 비스타 자전거였다. 칩·앤·실(포장 마감) 도로 위에서 덜커덩거림 없이 부드럽게 미끄러졌다. 새 볼베어링 덕분에 페달에 거의 힘을 주지 않아도 쑥쑥 나아갔다. 두 자전거가 크게 다르지 않아 보였지만, 큰 데이비의 것은 광이 나는 밤갈색이었고 폴의 것은 반짝이는 금속 플렉 블루였다.

“있잖아,” 큰 데이비가 자랑을 늘어놓기 시작했다. “내 다리가 더 길고, 방금 뿌린 WD40도 있으니 내 자전거가 분명 제일 빠를 거야.”

“아니야,” 폴이 반박했다. “내 다리는 더 짧지만 더 빨리 펌핑할 수 있고, 슈윈의 고성능 자전거 오일이 WD40보다 훨씬 성능이 좋아. WD40은 사실 삐걱거릴 때만 쓰는 거잖아.”

“경주! 경주!” 다른 아이들이 말했다. “경주로 정하면 되지 않을까?”

“좋아,” 큰 데이비가 말했다. “경주해서 누가 진짜 빠른지 보자.”

“내기다!” 폴이 동의했다. “빌리 언덕 꼭대기에서 출발해서 여기 도로 둑까지 내리막 전 구간을 달리자,”라고 그는 다른 아이들이 앉아 있던 도로 둑을 가리키며 말했다.

하나, 둘, 셋, 출발! 그들은 출발하자마자 내리막을 향해 힘껏 페달을 밟으며 내려갔다.

“가라, 폴!” “가라, 큰 데이비!” 아이들이 언덕 아래에서 외쳤다. 소란에 잠들어 있던 어린 데이비의 랫 테리어 종 개 넬리가 깨어났다. 요란스럽게 짖으며 넬리는 네 개의 작은 다리로 실로처럼 실컷 달려 사일로를 빙글빙글 돌았다. 그는 맨 앞에 있던 큰 데이비의 자전거를 향해 달려가 그것을 멈추려는 듯 크게 짖었다. 불쌍한 넬리는 앞에 있던 자전거를 다른 자전거가 추월하려 한다는 것을 몰랐다.

쿵, 추월하던 자전거가 개를 쳤다! 쾅, 쾅, 두 대의 자전거가 서로 부딪혔다!

“이런 – 아얘!” 으억! 두 소년이 핸들바를 넘겨 도로에 세게 떨어졌다. 반짝이던 자전거들은 더 이상 빛나지 않았다. 긁히고 역청 자국이 묻은 채로 한 더미에 누워 있었다. 넬리는 다리를 절며 사일로 옆으로 기어 와 몇 시간 동안 그곳에 드러누워 있었다.

다른 아이들은 둑에 서서 입을 벌리고 바라보았다. 재빨리 그들은 새 자전거 옆에 누워 있는 두 형에게 달려갔다. “괜찮아요?” 하고 물었다.

“난 괜찮을 거야,” 폴이 천천히 말했다. “하지만 이제 그만이야. 누가 자전거가 더 빠른지 누가 신경 쓰겠어.”

어린 데이비는 지금은 할아버지가 되었지만, 오래전 그 일요일 오후의 자전거 경주를 잊지 못했다. 그날 큰 데이비와 폴은 자랑과 과시가 보통 어떻게 처참한 결말을 맞는지를 배웠다.

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

当我归信的时候，我从未听过“再洗礼派”（Anabaptist）这个词。我也几乎没听过如何向别人作见证。我记得当时想到所有那些对我所经历的事一无所知的朋友们。我交往了七年的女友也不明白。我脑中不断回响一句话：“我必须告诉他们！”有件美好的事临到我，人人都需要知道同样的事也可以临到他们！我记得有一次我和我弟弟在想找个能向许多人传讲耶稣的地方。我们决定去看一场大联盟棒球赛。我很紧张，很害怕，我永远不会忘记所发生的事。我以前从未在大群人面前发言，但当我张口时，神充满了我的口。

我不仅去跟陌生人说话。当我看到一个老朋友时，我也会告诉他们发生在我身上的事。他们通常会说他们以前听过，试图说服我安下来、放松。我得先承认，在最初几年里我确实犯了一些错误。我惊讶地注意到，许多人并不喜欢我，但看起来最不喜欢我的，反而是那些自称为基督徒的人。有一天我拜访一位年长的男人，他说他一生大部分时间都是基督徒。在交谈中，他指着一个电灯泡说：“你看见那个电灯泡吗？它不会说话。”我很震惊。他在告诉我，虽然耶稣说我们是世上的光，但灯应该是安静地发光的。灯不说话。

我很惊讶。这是真的吗？我回家做了查经。不久我就找到了像马太福音4章23节这样的经文，“耶稣走遍加利利，在他们的会堂里教训人，宣讲天国的福音，并医治百姓各样的病症。”然后在马太福音第九章，当耶稣“看见众人，就怜悯他们；因为他们困苦流离，如同羊没有牧人。于是对他的门徒说，庄稼多，工人少；所以你们当求庄稼的主，打发工人为他的庄稼收成”（马太9:36-38）。

在我看来，无论耶稣走到哪里，他都在向人谈论天国。我见过有人以令人反感的方式为神作见证。但那是否意味着我们不该作见证？如果你读使徒行传，那几乎就是你所看到的——福音往外传！有一段记载当局抓住了门徒，并说如果他们肯闭嘴就可以获释。然而，门徒说他们不能。“因为我们不能不说所看见的事”（使徒行传4:20）。后来他们被沉默了——以至于死。

过了一段时间，我听说了这些被称为再洗礼派的人。当我研究他们时，我开始看到他们也不愿保持沉默。我订了一本《殉道者之镜》（The Martyr’s Mirror），当我读到这些活像门徒的人时，我惊讶不已。他们应验了耶稣所说的话，“你们为我的名被众人恨恶；惟有忍耐到底的必然得救”（马太10:22）。并且在罗马书8章36节写道，“正如经上所记：‘为你的缘故，我们终日被杀；人看我们如宰羊之人。’”

亲爱的弟兄姊妹们，我相信那火正在减弱。我听见许多我们的再洗礼派人谈论过平静与安稳的生活。耶稣在撒种的比喻中告诉我们：“那在荆棘里的，就是听了道，惟有今世的思虑和钱财的迷惑，把道挤住了，不能结实”（马太13:22）。那会不会就是我们中间许多人的处境？我们生活在美国这个自由的国度，金钱似乎容易获得。是否可能我们已被自己的财富和今世的忧虑所迷惑？我们是不是为了避免被世界逼迫，而变得像世界一样？

许多年前，一群再洗礼派人逃避逼迫，搬到一个压迫较少的国家。他们开了一家家具店维持生计，但他们卖不出任何家具，因为他们是令人畏惧的再洗礼派。不久，情况变得绝望，因为他们没有钱买食物。一天，一个富有的人走进了店里。所有工人都停下手中的活儿。他们心想：“也许这个人会买点什么，我们就能吃饭了！”一位年长的弟兄走近这位可能的顾客，问他是否认识耶稣。简短交谈后，那人愤怒地冲出店门。饥饿的工人们问那位年长的人为何把他们唯一的买主赶走。他解释说，让这个人认识耶稣，对他来说比赚点钱更为重要。

在早期再洗礼派人的心态中，耶稣的福音是第一位的。正如使徒行传中，他们不能不讲他们所看见和听见的事。他们也“终日被杀”。

那么，我们如何看待那节关于平静与安稳生活的经文呢？这节经文见于提摩太前书2章1-2节：“所以我劝你，第一要为万人恳求、祷告、代求、感谢；为君王和一切在位的，也该如此，使我们可以敬虔端正地度日，平静无事。”使徒保罗写这话时是什么意思？他是说我们应该对福音保持沉默，永不挑战罪人吗？很难相信保罗在告诉我们做他从未做过的事，做基督自己也从未做过的事。事实上，圣经中没有一个跟随神的人会对他们的信仰保持沉默。在许多早期基督徒因信仰被逮捕的记载里，当局会恳求他们闭嘴！但他们拒绝了，就像门徒一样。他们宁可选择死亡，也不愿要那种平静安稳的生活。

一位被捕的年轻再洗礼派人留下一位怀着头胎的爱妻。当局等到孩子出生后，把婴儿带到狱中的新父亲面前。他们告诉他他现在成了父亲，可以回家与妻儿同住。他还可以继续抱持相同的信仰，但必须保持沉默，不得在国教面前指责罪恶。年轻的父亲拒绝了。对他而言，沉默不是一个选择。他被拿去火刑处烧死。

那么，提摩太前书2章1-2节是什么意思？似乎圣经和早期教会的基督徒都是致力于传播福音，致力于基督的教会。他们到处宣讲福音，在山上、树林里或任何人会来的地方举行聚会。那是他们的生活。保罗在提摩太前书2章中的意思是，我们应当祈求当权者让我们平安生活，好使我们能传播福音。基督徒当出去传道，努力进入天国。我们的祷告是愿掌权者让我们平安生活，同时我们侍奉那和平之君。

今天如果你安定下来、过一种平静安稳的生活，永不挑战罪人或纠正弟兄，那样做很容易成为基督徒。但谁说跟随基督会容易？

当我们住在海地时，我们教会的会众有关跟随耶稣代价的教导。听到海地人将耶稣的教导应用在他们生命中的见证，令人惊讶。有一次，两位会友告诉我们他们因为跟随福音可能将失去工作。听见他们为真理站立使我很欢喜。教会里另一位姊妹告诉我，她孩子就读的学校有制服，女生必须穿裤子。当她送女儿穿着端庄的裙子去学校时，女儿带回校长的便条，说她不可以再穿那种东西回学校。

彼得前书4章14节说：“你们若为基督的名受辱便是有福的，因为神荣耀的灵，常住在你们身上。这是他们辱骂你们，你们却得荣耀。”

真正的喜乐来自于受苦。受苦来自顺服耶稣。我们是否过于忙于琐事，而任凭世人下地狱？让我们像早期基督徒一样跟随耶稣，使人无法否认神的大能在他们中间运行。我们有人人都需要的东西。我们还在等什么？让我们重聚，重新聚集，否认自己，背起十字架，跟随他！
